name: 14Strings! Cornell Filipino Rondalla
description: 14Strings! is a Filipino style Rondalla based in Ithaca, New York. The main instruments are 14 stringed plucked instruments like the bandurria, the laud (lute), and the octavina. Our mission is to further the appreciation for and engagement in the tradition of the Rondalla, both for our members and the wider Cornell and Ithaca communities. All are always welcome regardless of background or musical experience.

name: 180 Degrees Consulting at Cornell University
description: 180DC at Cornell provides high-quality consulting services to socially conscious businesses and nonprofits in the Ithaca community and beyond to produce innovative and lasting results. Our team of passionate social impact leaders will develop professional skills through hands-on learning to solve modern business challenges.

name: 23 New Org
description: This is a placeholder for new org registration to be able to attend Workshops.

name: 302 Wait Avenue Co-op
description: We are a cooperative living house on north campus that cares for one another and promotes a safe living space for women and non-binary identifying people.

name: 660 Stewart Cooperative
description: The purpose of 660 shall be to provide quality housing, or rather a home to its members, by promoting the concept of cooperative living in accordance with the spirit of the Rochdale Principles of Cooperation.

name: A BIRDSONG Program
description: Building inclusive research and designing supportive outreach and networking for growing talents Outreach programs in STEM provide powerful opportunities for learning. For kids, these programs can cultivate life-long interests in STEM topics and even ignite the pursuit of STEM- related careers. However, communication and perceptual differences/disabilities make accessing community spaces and outreach materials inaccessible for many people. Furthermore, institutional opportunities to train STEM students in disability justice, accessibility and inclusive practices are rare. This team’s goal is t

name: A Seat at the Table
description: It is our purpose to provide a professional, supportive, educational, and social venue where all students can discuss issues affecting and pertaining to their respective communities as well as social issues which they feel passionate about, all through a business lens (i.e. freedom of speech and religion, race relations in the workplace, ESG and sustainability efforts, and more). Essentially, our priority is to allow for conversation and education surrounding Business Ethics and Human Resources in a way that develops students professionally through consulting projects.

name: AAP - Cornell AAP ASSOCIATION
description: An anthology of projects from artists, architects, and planners, ASSOCIATION strives to highlight cross-disciplinary connections and reveal new relationships between the works produced by the three departments we represent. Through the careful curation and presentation of yearly submissions since 2005, each volume serves as a record of the work produced by the current AAP community, as well as a source of inspiration for years to come.

name: Absolute A Cappella
description: Established in 2001, Absolute A Cappella is an a cappella group at Cornell University and was founded on the core values of singing, friendship, and pineapples. Absolute performs two concerts each year as well as a variety of arch-sings. The group sings a range of genres, from indie pop to alt rock. Absolute is always finding exciting new ways to sing and perform, and most importantly, have fun while doing what we love.

name: Absolute Zero Break Dance Club
description: Our goals are the mastery of our bodies in dance through practice, and the fostering of relationships with crew members, breakdance club members, alumni, other dance troupes, the larger Cornell community, friends, and acquaintances through our love of breaking, funkstyles, and music.

name: Acacia
description: Human Service

name: ACE: The Ace/Asexual Support Group at Cornell
description: ACE is a student-run social support group for individuals of the Cornell community who identify as ace/aro or ace/aro-questioning. ACE provides its members with a support network and a safe space to meet and discuss ace related issues and experiences. ACE is also dedicated to developing the ace community at Cornell and improving visibility and availability of information surrounding the ace community.

name: Actuarial Society at Cornell
description: Our club aims to provide awareness for the actuarial profession and to assist those striving to become an actuary by strengthening their leadership, networking, professional, and actuarial skills.

name: Advocacy Center of Tompkins County
description: Supporting survivors of sexual and domestic violence

name: AEM Graduate Student Association
description: AEM Graduate Student Association is a graduate student organization in the field of applied economics and management at Cornell University. The organization's purpose is to provide a framework for common activities of its members, to support interaction among its members on a regular basis, and to support graduate students in academic and other ways while studying at the Charles H. Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management.

name: African Dance Repertoire
description: To foster the awareness of African cultures through music, dance, and theatrical performances both on and off campus.

name: AFRICAN GRADUATE STUDENTS ASSOCIATION AT CORNELL
description: AfriGA’s mission is to create a welcoming and supportive community for African graduate students at Cornell University. We are committed to promoting academic excellence, celebrating our cultural heritage, and empowering our members to achieve personal and professional success.

name: AFROTC Detachment 520
description: The mission of the Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps (AFROTC) 520th Cadet Wing is to recruit, educate, and develop cadets in a high-quality training environment and commission the strongest leaders for the United States Air Force and Space Force.

name: After Eight A Cappella
description: After Eight's purpose is to entertain audiences at Cornell and elsewhere while providing women and gender minorities the chance to perform contemporary music a cappella.

name: Agua Clara
description: AguaClara Cornell is a student-led program that develops and implements sustainable, gravity-powered water treatment technologies to bring safe water on tap to communities around the world.

name: Aikido Club at Cornell
description: The Cornell Aikido Club promotes the study of the Japanese martial art, Aikido. We offer classes, resources on learning more about Aikido, and information on upcoming seminars.

name: Air and Sea Hospitality
description: This organization explores the airline and cruise industry as a whole and exposes members to the various opportunities that exist within the businesses. We provide resources to help you learn more about the industry and build the knowledge and network to work in it.

name: Akwe:kon
description: Akwe:kon (pronounced uh-GWAY-go) opened its doors in 1991, making it the nation's first university residence hall established to celebrate American Indian culture and heritage. In the Mohawk language, Akwe:kon means "all of us," reflecting the spirit of inclusiveness the house offers to students and the broader community. Akwe:kon's 35 residents represent diverse cultures and backgrounds; roughly half are Native American. Whatever their cultural background or tribal nationality, residents share an interest in past and contemporary Native issues and the importance of community and extended fami

name: ALANA Intercultural Programming Board
description: We seek to provide the Cornell community with wide and diversified programming on a regular basis as well as allocate funds to registered student organizations for programs that encourage diversity and intercultural efforts.

name: Albanian Student Association at Cornell
description: The Albanian Student Association at Cornell brings together students of Albanian descent and everyone who wants to learn about Albanian history, culture, politics, and beyond. Our purpose is to provide an opportunity for Albanian students to meet, interact with each other, and help new students coming from Albania. ASAC serves to promote the awareness of cultural diversity on campus by organizing cultural and social events on campus. The membership of ASAC is open to all Albanian students and every student of Cornell University.

name: Alexander Hamilton Society
description: The Alexander Hamilton Society (AHS) is an independent, non-partisan, not-for-profit organization dedicated to promoting constructive debate on basic principles and contemporary issues in foreign, economic, and national security policy. AHS seeks to identify, educate, and launch young men and women into foreign policy and national security careers imbued with the Hamiltonian perspective of strong and principled American leadership in global affairs. Hamiltonians are united by a deep conviction, rooted in the history of the last century, that the world is a better, safer, and more prosperous pl

name: Alpha Chi Omega
description: Alpha Chi Omega was founded at DePauw University in Greencastle, Indiana on October 15, 1885. Its seven founders, who were all music students, sought "friendship, artistic society and advancement of the 'principles of true womanhood.'" Today, Alpha Chi Omega has over 200,000 members nationally with over 135 collegiate chapters and 200 alumnae chapters. The Zeta Phi chapter of Alpha Chi Omega was founded at Cornell in 1984 with 55 women. In the past thirty years, the Zeta Phi chapter has flourished from a small group of women meeting in classrooms to recognition as one of the strongest sororiti

name: Alpha Delta Phi
description: Alpha Delta Phi aims to foster personal growth for undergraduates and alumni across social, ethical, leadership, scholastic, community service, and literary areas.

name: Alpha Epsilon Delta; Pre-Health Honor Society
description: Alpha Epsilon Delta meetings provide a non-stressful environment for members to come together in a supportive setting to discuss and understand the full meaning of our pursuit of a career in healthcare. We discuss current medical events and ethical issues, host guest panels, share advice on the medical school application process, get certified in Narcan and CPR administration, and plan social and service events.

name: Alpha Epsilon Phi
description: Alpha Epsilon Phi was founded on October 24th, 1909 by seven young women at Barnard College. Our mission is to to inspire and support exemplary women dedicated to friendship and a lifelong commitment to Alpha Epsilon Phi while building on the vision of our Jewish founders. The Kappa Chapter of Alpha Epsilon Phi sorority was founded on Cornell's campus in 1920. AEPhi's national motto is "Many Hearts, One Purpose", and this rings true here at Cornell. Our sisterhood is comprised of women with a wide range of backgrounds, interests and aspirations. Our organization values scholarship, service and

name: Alpha Epsilon Pi
description: Alpha Epsilon Pi, the Jewish Fraternity of North America, was founded to provide opportunities for Jewish men seeking the best possible college and fraternity experience. We have maintained the integrity of our purpose by strengthening our ties to the Jewish community and serving as a link between high school and career. Alpha Epsilon Pi develops leadership for the North American Jewish community at a critical time in a young man's life. Alpha Epsilon Pi's role is to encourage the Jewish student to remain dedicated to Jewish ideals, values, and ethics and to prepare the student to be one of to

name: Alpha Gamma Rho
description: The Beginnings of Alpha Gamma Rho start in 1912 with the foundation of the Caduceus chapter at Cornell University. The founders were a close knit group of men dedicated to issues concerning agriculture. On December 19, 1914, Caduceus received a charter from Alpha Gamma Rho national and has Zeta Chapter ever since. The first AGR house sat at 409 Dryden Ave until 1916 when a new house was built at 203 Highland Ave, the present location of the house. Since 1914, Alpha Gamma Rho has been the home to over 1700 men. Alpha Gamma Rho (AGR) is the national agricultural fraternity, with sixty two chapte

name: Alpha Iota Gamma Gamma Chapter
description: Alpha Iota Gamma (╬æ I ╬ô) serves as a professional, academic, and social foundation for men and women dedicated to pursuing a career in healthcare. The brothers and sisters of Alpha Iota Gamma uphold a commitment to discipline, compassion, and integrity, key ethical pillars in healthcare and life. The bonds formed in Alpha Iota Gamma between students with diverse healthcare interests creates a comprehensive network at the undergraduate level and beyond. Members of Alpha Iota Gamma have the opportunity to meet other students interested in healthcare careers, get peer and professional level adv

name: Alpha Kappa Alpha
description: Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated is an internationally recognized sorority that was founded on the campus of Howard University on January 15th, 1908. Our sorority has since flourished to serve communities all across the world and is now comprised of over 390,000 members. Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated aims to cultivate and encourage high scholastic and ethical standards, to promote unity and friendship among college women, to study and help alleviate problems concerning girls and women in order to improve their social stature, to maintain a progressive interest in college lif

name: alpha Kappa Delta Phi
description: The sisterhood of alpha Kappa Delta Phi provides women with a sense of belonging that nurtures life-long friendships, develops self-empowered leaders, and strengthens communities through service, scholarship, and Asian-Awareness.

name: Alpha Kappa Psi
description: Alpha Kappa Psi is Cornell University's Original Co-Ed Professional Business Fraternity dedicated to providing a professional and social environment in which its brothers can thrive. Founded in 1904, Alpha Kappa Psi is the nation's oldest professional business fraternity as well. Our chapter at Cornell University was founded in 1998 and is one of over 190 College Chapters across the nation, Canada, and the United Kingdom. We host and engage in a variety of professional, social, and philanthropic activities that help develop experienced and ethical leaders and foster life-long bonds and memorie

name: Alpha Omega Epsilon Professional Engineering Sorority
description: Our purpose is to promote ideals and objectives that further the advancement of female engineers and technical scientists and build a foundation for lifelong bonds of sisterhood.

name: Alpha Phi
description: Alpha Phi was the first American college sorority. It was founded at Syracuse University in 1872, where Alpha Chapter still exists. At its formation the sisterhood numbered ten women. One of these was Martha Foote Crowe, who later became Alpha Phi's first president. "Pursuing their studies in a thoroughly male-dominated environment, these women had a pressing need for friends who could sympathize with each other's problems and support each other's aspirations."(The Ivy Leaf) In addition, Alpha Phi organized the first interfraternity association, known today as the National Panhellenic Conferen

name: Alpha Phi Alpha
description: Alpha Phi Alpha, the first intercollegiate Greek-letter fraternity established for African American Men, was founded at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York by seven college men who recognized the need for a strong bond of brotherhood among African descendants in this country. The visionary founders, known as the "Jewels" of the fraternity, are Henry Arthur Callis, Charles Henry Chapman, Eugene Kinckle Jones, George Biddle Kelley, Nathaniel Allison Murray, Robert Harold Ogle, and Vertner Woodson Tandy.

name: Alpha Phi Omega - Gamma Chapter
description: Alpha Phi Omega is a national gender inclusive community service fraternity for college students. APO strives to help each member develop leadership skills, secure lasting friendships, and provide service to others. The award-winning Gamma Chapter has grown to into a close-knit organization of over 400 members, providing meaningful service to the Cornell campus, Ithaca community, and national and global organizations.

name: Alpha Sigma Phi
description: Iota Chapter at Cornell was founded on March 27, 1909, by a group of ten undergraduates. The new fraternity prospered, and in 1913 it moved to its current location teetering over the edge of Fall Creek Gorge. The west wing containing 15 single rooms and the north wing, with expanded dining and social facilities, were added in 1924. Major improvements have been made to Rockledge Estate regularly. Alpha Sig has made and continues to make distinctive contributions to the Cornell community. Andrew Dickson White, the first president of and co-founder of Cornell, was initiated into the fraternity at

name: Alpha Xi Delta
description: Alpha Xi Delta was founded in 1893 by ten young women at Lombard College, Galesburg, Illinois, who shared a vision and a dream of a national organization dedicated to the personal growth of women. One of the oldest women's fraternities, Alpha Xi Delta is proud of its rich history. As one of the ten founding fraternities of the National Panhellenic Conference, it was Alpha Xi Delta's first NPC Chairman who wrote the Panhellenic Creed, which is still recited on college campuses today. Since that time more than a 100 years ago, the spirit of Alpha Xi Delta has enriched the lives of thousands of w

name: Alpha Zeta
description: Founded in 1901, the Cornell Chapter of Alpha Zeta is a co-ed, honors, professional, and social fraternity for anyone with an interest in agriculture. We provide a unique community on campus that provides opportunities for community service, social activities, and professional networking. The goals of our Fraternity are to foster high standards of scholarship, character, leadership, and fellowship and also to promote the advancement of agriculture. Our main agricultural outreach event, Ag Day, is held every semester and brings farm animals and agricultural equipment to the Ag Quad to expose th

name: Alpine Ski Racing
description: The Cornell Alpine Ski Team is a club sport open to all current undergraduate students at Cornell University. The team provides a format for competitive ski racing as well as development of new racers. We train on-snow at Greek Peak, which is conveniently located about 30 mins from campus.

name: Alumni Affairs & Development
description: As a Cornell student, you’re now part of a life-long network of Cornellians that spans time zones, generations, disciplines, and life experiences. Today’s graduates join a community of more than 250,000 alumni who live and work in communities around the globe. We invite you to connect with the amazing professional and social network of Cornell alumni. Join regional events happening in your area when you’re home on break. Connect with alumni online. Or get involved in the Senior Class Campaign. After you graduate, check out your local Cornell Club and connect with Cornellians here, there, and e

name: Alzheimer's Buddies
description: Alzheimer's Buddies at Cornell is a student-led organization aimed at overcoming the social disengagement experienced by those affected by intermediate-to-late-stages of Alzheimer's Disease. The purpose of this organization is to pair students to volunteer 1-on-1 with dementia residents, build social skills as well as raise awareness through participating in fundraisers and hosting talks on current advancements in Alzheimer's Disease research.

name: Amber Dance Troupe
description: Amber Dance Troupe's purpose is to spread the rich heritage of Chinese culture and the beauty of Chinese dance to Cornell and local community. Anyone interested can learn Chinese dance skills through regular practice and get opportunity to perform on various stages.

name: American Cancer Society at Cornell
description: Our organization runs various events throughout the year to spread cancer awareness and raise money for the American Cancer Society. Our biggest event is Relay for Life, an all-night fundraiser that the entire Cornell community is encouraged to attend. We fundraise before and during the event, which includes speakers, performances, food, and activities.

name: American Fisheries Society Student Subunit at Cornell
description: To advance the knowledge of fisheries and aquatic science at Cornell, promote professional development of undergraduate students, and facilitate collaboration of students and fisheries professionals at Cornell.

name: American Hotel and Lodging Association Student Chapter at Cornell University
description: The purpose of the chapter is to be the primary advocates of the American lodging industry for SHA students through education, information and member services, and to build meaningful and professional connections between the American Hotel and Lodging Association and Cornell University. Our main goals are as follows: 1. To provide members opportunities to exchange ideas, strategies, and contacts with industry leaders at any of AH&LA events throughout the year. 2. To educate members on the latest industry trend and research through AH&LA online information services. 3. To expose new members to

name: American India Foundation Cornell Chapter
description: The purpose of the AIF Cornell Chapter shall be to provide an avenue for high-achieving undergraduate and graduate students with a passion for international development and social change to help create a more equitable India through ambassadorship and fundraising efforts supporting AIF’s initiatives in education, livelihood, and public health–improving the lives of India’s underprivileged.

name: American Indian and Indigenous Student Empowerment
American Indian and Indigenous Studies Program
description: As Cornell University's American Indian and Indigenous Studies Program (AIISP), our mission is to aid the development of new generations of educated Indigenous and non-Indigenous people who will contemplate, study and contribute to the building of Indigenous nations and communities on a global scale.

name: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
description: The primary vision of Cornell University's AISES chapter is the development of a new generation of educated Native leaders who will in turn contemplate, study, and contribute to the building of a Nation and community among Native Americans.

name: American Institute of Architecture Students Cornell Chapter
description: The AIAS Cornell Chapter aims to promote excellence in architectural education, training, and practice; to foster an appreciation of architecture and related disciplines; to enrich communities in a spirit of collaboration; and to organize undergraduate and graduate Cornell students and combine their efforts to advance the art and science of architecture.

name: American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE) at Cornell University
description: We are Cornell's student chapter of the American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE), a national network of chemical engineering professionals and students. Our chapter's mission is to strengthen the Cornell ChemE community and enrich the ChemE undergraduate experience through professional, outreach, and social programming.

name: American Lung Cancer Screening Initiative at Cornell
description: ALCSIC aims to promote awareness for lung cancer screening for individuals at high-risk of developing lung cancer at Cornell University and the larger Ithaca community through educational efforts, community outreach, and health literacy engagement. Activities may include advocating for Congress members to support lung cancer bills, presenting to various stakeholders to build awareness, and working with local health departments to educate and bring actionable change to the community.

name: American Meteorological Society at Cornell Chapter
description: We are Cornell Weather. Our mission is to encourage the pursuit of meteorological knowledge on Cornell's campus and create a community within the Atmospheric Science department. We also seek to introduce undergraduates to various professional opportunities in the Atmospheric Sciences and facilitate research, and help them work on skills crucial to the science in ways that help the Cornell community at large.

name: American Red Cross (Community Partner)
description: Red Cross volunteers and staff work to deliver vital services – from providing relief and support to those in crisis, to helping you be prepared to respond in emergencies.

name: American Red Cross at Cornell
description: The American Red Cross prevents and alleviates human suffering in the face of emergencies by mobilizing the power of volunteers and the generosity of donors. The organization works closely with the American Red Cross to help fulfill its humanitarian missions and uphold its values.

name: American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Cornell Chapter
description: The purpose of the American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Cornell Chapter is to cultivate a community of scholars dedicated to scientific discovery and promoting interdisciplinary research while giving students more opportunities to learn about the fields of biochemistry and molecular biology.

name: American Society of Landscape Architects Cornell Graduate Chapter
description: Landscape architects lead the planning, design, and stewardship of healthy, equitable, safe, and resilient environments. The Society’s mission is to advance landscape architecture through advocacy, communication, education, and fellowship. The ASLA at Cornell University exists to support the students of the Department of Landscape Architecture in meeting their academic and professional goals, advocate for the profession of Landscape Architecture on and off campus, and harness the skills of its members to design and work for more accessible, sustainable, and beautiful spaces.

name: American Society of Mechanical Engineers at Cornell University Chapter
description: Cornell ASME aims to enrich the lives of students of the Sibley School by providing professional and social networking events, information about post-graduation career paths, and local outreach activities. We uphold the ASME mission to serve diverse global communities by advancing, disseminating and applying engineering knowledge for improving the quality of life, and communicating the excitement of engineering.

name: Anabel's Collaboration and Education
description: Passionate about food? Want to promote food justice on campus? For students interested in collaborating with Anabel's Grocery, our student-run nonprofit grocery store, join Anabel's Collaboration and Education. Help us develop projects that support a socially just and environmentally sound food system with an awesome team!

name: Animal Advocacy at Cornell
description: The purpose of Animal Advocacy at Cornell (AAC) shall be to provide a space for individuals of all backgrounds who have an interest in ending suffering and exploitation of all animals, through advocacy, education, outreach, campaigning, and a plant-based lifestyle. AAC seeks to increase the accessibility of a plant-based diet and help individuals explore the world of plant-based eating.

name: Animal Science Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of this organization is to promote stronger graduate student relations with peers and mentors within Animal Sciences and other disciplines.

name: Animal Science: Mentoring Our Undergraduates
description: The mission of Animal Science: Mentoring Our Undergraduates is to foster mentorship between current Animal Science students and incoming Animal Science students with hopes to ease the transition into the program and build a community of students that spans generations.

name: Anjali at Cornell
description: Founded in 2011, Cornell Anjali aims to spread awareness of South Asian classical dance forms such as Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, and Odissi. We perform as a group both on and off campus, sponsor many South Asian cultural events, perform at our annual showcase, and also hold workshops for those interested in the aforementioned art forms. We aim to perform, promote, and spread the love of South Asian classical dance throughout Cornell.

name: Anthropology Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of Anthropology Graduate Student Association shall be to represent the interests of graduate students in the Anthropology PhD and CIAMS MA programs in relation to the Department, Graduate Field, and University, keep records of graduate student activities and concerns for future cohorts, and help foster community among graduate students.

name: AppDev at Cornell
description: The philosophy of Cornell AppDev is to curate a tight-knit, inclusive community where any person can be part of the process to solve problems through app development. We do this by building apps using industry-level techniques with an emphasis on mobile development, cultivating a strong mentorship culture, and educating the next generation of Cornellians in our craft.

name: Applied & Engineering Physics Society
description: The purpose of this organization is to develop a strong and welcoming undergraduate culture in the Applied & Engineering Physics department. This group will create an infrastructure for undergraduates interested in or affiliated with A&EP to both act as and seek academic mentors, spend more time with A&EP peers in a social setting, participate in outreach events to encourage undergraduates to join the A&EP major, and to facilitate communication between the undergraduate community and the A&EP department faculty. The A&EP Society intends additionally to provide opportunities for members to expl

name: Applied Physics Graduate Society
description: The purpose of the APGS is to facilitate communication among the applied physics graduate students as well as the broader Cornell community. Our goals include disseminating important information to graduate students and acting as a formal voice for graduate students within the workings of the department. Additionally, the APGS fosters community among physics graduate students by organizing social events and discussion forums. With a founding principle of “... any person ... any study,” Cornell is an equal opportunity employer and educator. For more information, visit hr.cornell.edu/eeo.

name: Applied Public Policy Strategies at Cornell
description: With the ever-evolving policy and governance sphere, Applied Public Policy Strategies (APPS) empowers students to deliver innovative, data-driven solutions to complex government and policy challenges. By combining strategic consulting skills with a passion for public service, we foster impactful change and develop the next generation of civic-minded leaders at Cornell and beyond. Working with leading think tanks, non-profits, governments, and industry innovators, we strive to drive meaningful policy outcomes and create sustainable solutions that address today’s most pressing challenges.

name: Apprenti of Prometheus (Ph.D. Student Association)
description: Over 2000 years ago, Prometheus stole fire from the gods and brought it to humanity in the form of technology, knowledge and civilization. Today, the Ph.D. students association of Johnson Graduate School of Management has the ambitious objective to facilitate the development of new knowledge in the fields of Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management and Organisation, OTIM, and Strategy. Our mission is to organize meetings among Ph.D. students of Johnson Graduate School of Management in order to provide networking opportunities and to facilitate the exchange of ideas.

name: Arab Student Association
description: The purpose of ASA is to create a welcoming and inclusive community for individuals interested in Arab language, culture, and heritage, with the goal of fostering cross-cultural dialogue and mutual understanding on campus and beyond. Those individuals also have the opportunity to increase awareness of pertinent issues in the Arab world both on the Cornell campus and in the larger Ithaca community. ASA is a nonpartisan student group. As such, it will not be associated with or have any bias towards regional Arab political, religious, and ideological entities.

name: Archery Club at Cornell
description: The Cornell Archery Club provides a forum for the discussion and practice of the traditional sport of archery. Our charge is to promote an environment where any and all members of the Cornell community can participate in a classic sport and learn the elements of collegiate archery. In pursuit of this goal, we facilitate weekly shoots, where archers of all skill levels can practice and socialize, learning from more experienced archers and developing their own skills and their understanding of the sport. We also attend local, state and national competitions for members who are interested in comp

name: Architects, Artists, and Planners of Color
description: The mission and purpose of Architects, Artists, and Planners of Color shall be to amplify the BIPOC voices in AAP. AAPOC does this by creating a safe and welcoming space that fosters inclusion and a sense of unity throughout AAP. AAPOC works to create a network that supports BIPOC students.

name: Armenian Student Organization
description: To foster community among students and locals with an interest in Armenian heritage on Cornell's campus through social/cultural events, Armenian language and culture classes, and educational events (guest speakers, workshops, conferences). To educate the Cornell campus about the Armenian language, culture, and history. To establish a greater and more inclusive sense of community by collaborating with other organizations.

name: Army ROTC Club
description: The Army ROTC Club at Cornell University provides leadership development within the framework of the Army Values, while promoting Equality, Fraternity, and Liberty within Cornell Leadership development efforts. In addition, the Army ROTC Club will impart education and outreach regarding Cornell's military history and achievements.

name: Art and Business Club at Cornell
description: The Art and Business Club at Cornell (ABCC) helps Cornell artists to build a clearer public identity: who they are, what they make, and why their work matters. ABCC turns artwork into profiles, exhibitions, social storytelling, and eventually stronger connections to galleries and collectors. We aim to give student artists the polish and platform they deserve, showcase their work to wider audiences, and help them enter the professional art world. We welcome students from every background who are interested in the intersection of art and business.

name: Art Beyond Cornell
description: Art Beyond Cornell aims to bring new perspectives to both Cornell students and institutionalized youth in the Tompkins County area by providing a means of connection, self-expression, communication, growth, and joy through art.

name: Artificial Intelligence Club at Cornell
description: The Artificial Intelligence Club is dedicated to fostering a collaborative and innovative community of students passionate about the intersection of artificial intelligence and business. Our mission is to empower our members with the knowledge, skills, and connections necessary to excel as leaders in the rapidly evolving field of AI-driven business strategy.

name: Artistic Beads Club
description: The purpose of the Artistic Beads Club shall be to teach its members to make a variety of objects out of beads and bond with peers in a safe space.

name: Asha Cornell
description: Asha Cornell works to bring social awareness about the plight of education into the Cornell community through events such as fundraisers and other cultural activities. These activities include celebrations of Indian culture such as classical concerts featuring renowned Indian artists and movie series of recent Bollywood films, through which we hope the Cornell community attains a deeper glimpse into Indian culture. The funds we collect go towards catalyzing socio-economic change in India through the education of underprivileged children.

name: Asian & Asian American Center
description: Founded in 2009, the Asian & Asian American Center (A3C) brings together the rich diversity of Asian Pacific Islander Desi American experiences (to include East, South, Southeast Asian, Pacific Islander, bi/multi-racial/ethnic, etc.) to foster an inclusive Cornell campus community. Our programs focus on advocacy, education, identity and community building.

name: Asian American Intervarsity
description: Asian American InterVarsity is a group of students on campus with a vision to see students transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed. Through sharing the wide range of stories that make up the Asian American experience and exploring how they have shaped us, AAIV exists to explore how Jesus can transform pain and brokeness into celebration and restoration for Asian Americans.

name: Asian Pacific Americans for Action
description: APAA (established in 1972) is a group of passionate students dedicated to advocating for the AAPI community at Cornell. APAA builds on its past work in promoting the fundamental importance of political education and history through advocacy and discussion. AAPA is committed to furthering AAPI awareness on campus and to politically empowering and advocating for the needs of Asian-Pacific American students. Furthermore, APAA builds coalitions with other students of color and social justice groups to facilitate a more unified community of color. In the past two years, APAA held discussions on rev

name: Asian Studies Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of the Asian Studies Graduate Student Association shall be to build community among and advocate for graduate students in the fields of Asian Studies and Asian Literature, Religion & Culture.

name: ASL @ Cornell
description: ASL @ Cornell aims to promote heightened awareness of and appreciation for American Sign Language (ASL) and Deaf culture in collaboration with Cornell’s ASL/Deaf Studies program. In doing so, we hope to cultivate an inclusive environment on campus and in the city of Ithaca that welcomes Deaf and hard of hearing individuals while allowing all students to develop a greater understanding of ASL and encouraging them to apply their classroom knowledge to the community.

name: Asociación de CentroAmericanos Unidos
description: The purpose of ACaU is to provide a secondary home for Central American students and anyone interested in Central American culture. Thus, ACaU fundamentally prioritizes empowering Central American students while fostering awareness of its rich, complex culture at Cornell University and the greater Ithaca area.

name: Asociación de Sudamericanos Unidos
description: The purpose of ASaU is to increase South American visibility within the greater Ithaca area, mainly serving Cornell University students. ASaU aims to foster a community for this underrepresented community while welcoming others as a learning opportunity.

name: Assisting People Across Nations
description: The purpose of APAN is to provide a platform for students to engage in humanitarian fundraising efforts that support global human rights initiatives. Our focus is on raising awareness and financial resources for nonprofits that provide medical aid and essential services in crisis-affected regions. By supporting a range of organizations rather than one individual organization, we empower members to design and lead targeted fundraising campaigns aligned with causes they are passionate about, fostering leadership development and a strong sense of global responsibility.

name: Association for Students and Community

By promoting active engagement and collaboration, BSO strives to enhance the overa

description: Cornell Club Baseball is dedicated to playing competitive baseball in a fun, engaging environment. description: As a women-led, interdisciplinary organization focused on the affordable housing industry, we aim to empower young women and equip them with the proper tools necessary for their professional development, technical knowledge, network, and more. Our objectives are to introduce top-tier students to the affordable housing sector, facilitate connections with industry mentors, and foster relationships that connect talented individuals with leading companies, building their personal and professional development for years to come.

name: Charity Outreach and Student Teamwork Club
description: To spread awareness and fundraise for trustworthy charities by hosting campus social events and using communication networks.

name: ChemE Car at Cornell
description: The purpose of Cornell ChemE Car is threefold. The first purpose is to design and build a shoe box-sized car that is powered and stopped via chemical reactions. The second purpose is to provide students with the opportunity to apply engineering knowledge and skills. The third purpose is to contribute to the development of Chemical Engineering at Cornell University through attendance at regional and national competitions, research and development, and student-driven innovation.

name: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Graduate Women's Group
description: The purpose of CBEWomen shall be 1) to focus on issues pertinent to affiliates of the School of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, and 2) to encourage students (such as but not limited to girls) to enter engineering through outreach.

name: Chemical Engineering Graduate Student Association (ChEGSA)
description: The mission of Chemical Engineering Graduate Student Association (ChEGSA) is to bring together the graduate students and postdocs of the R.F Smith School of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering (CBE), through both professional and social events. Through these events, we strive to improve the well-being, connections, and skills of our members so that they can strive for greatness while they are here at Cornell and beyond graduation.

name: Chemistry Peer Advisors at Cornell
description: We are dedicated to helping underclassmen navigate the chemistry major. To do this, we bridge the gap between prospective chemistry majors and upperclassmen. Through the community we've built, we are able to tutor, advise, and build lasting social and professional connections.

name: Chemists for Outreach and Graduate Inclusion
description: The purpose of COrGI shall be to build a more inclusive environment within the chemistry department at Cornell by: 1) Promoting diversity within chemistry 2) Advocating for departmental policies related to diversity and inclusion 3) Hosting outreach events targeted towards underrepresented groups 4) Providing workshops, info-sessions, and an open space where graduate and undergraduate students can have their voices heard and get the support they need to pursue their academic and career goals.

name: Chess Club at Cornell University
description: To imbue the Cornell and Ithaca community with the spirit and skill of competitive chess. To foster the growth of our nationally recognized Chess Team. To have fun!

name: Chesterton House, Inc.
description: We are affiliated with Chesterton House, the CURW affiliated Cornell ministry for Christian students, focused on introducing students to the historic Christian intellectual tradition in order to empower more faithful Christian living.

name: Chi Psi
description: Chi Psi is a Fraternity of gentlemen that strive to pursue excellence in every facet of our daily lives.

name: Chinese Bible Study
description: Chinese Bible Study (CBS) is a student-run Christian fellowship who seeks to know Christ and make Him known. We are a tight-knit community committed to encourage and help each other grow as brothers and sisters in Christ!

name: CHINESE DRAGON SOCCER CLUB
description: A non-competitive soccer club for Chinese students and scholars. • Organized weekly training and games on campus through social media • Connected with neighbor universities for friendly matches • Participated in Intramural and Annual Ivy Cup soccer tournaments

name: Chinese Drama Society at Cornell
description: We aim to promote theatre performances in Chinese language at Cornell University, through regular performances and other exchanges, to provide performing arts entertainment for the Chinese-speaking community (including language learners) and to diversify the multi-cultural performing arts scene at Cornell. We are an independent student organization registered with Cornell University.

name: Chinese Students and Scholars Association at Cornell
description: Cornell Chinese Students and Scholars Association (Cornell CSSA) is a voluntary, non-profit organization whose members are students and scholars coming from China. The operating body of CSSA is the CSSA council, which consists of volunteers committed to serving members of CSSA and prompting the welfare of the Chinese community.

name: Chinese Students Association
description: The Chinese Students Association (CSA) is one of Cornell's oldest and largest cultural and social organizations, with roots dating back to 1904. Our mission is to provide a community of friendship and support for Chinese / Chinese American students through weekly general body meetings and larger-scale cultural and social events. Students of any and all backgrounds are welcome!

name: Chordials
description: The Chordials are an award-winning co-ed a cappella group from Cornell University in Ithaca, NY. The group, known for their edgy and passionate style, sings in Ithaca and across the Northeast. Each semester, they put on one major concert on campus: "After Hours" in the fall, and "Cocktail Hour" in the spring. In 2013, they went to ICCA Finals in New York City and were awarded 3rd place overall. In June 2020, they released their most recent studio album, Fire & Concrete.

name: Chorus at Cornell University
description: The purposes of the Chorus are the study, practice, performance, and promotion of choral music at the university, within the Ithaca community, and beyond.

name: Christian Business Society
description: The purpose of CBS is to promote Christian community within the undergraduate business-focused programs at Cornell, educate both members and non-members about the integration of faith and work in one's professional life, and provide resources and mentorship for career exploration, academic success, and internship/job recruiting.

name: Christian Union VITA
description: Christian Union seeks to provide opportunities for students to become involved with Christian community and enjoy fellowship, with an emphasis on developing Christian leaders. The organization seeks to offer support for Christian students, as well as resources to help non-Christian students learn about Christianity. Christian Union's activities include Bible courses, weekly large group meetings featuring community speakers, conferences, leadership development, social events, and more.

name: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints Student Association
description: The purpose of the LDSSA shall be to fortify the Cornell LDS community, to raise awareness and education regarding the LDS faith, and to work cooperatively with other faiths in strengthening and building the Cornell community through service, dialog and fun events.

name: Cinema Student Advisory Board at Cornell University
description: The Cornell Cinema Student Advisory Board is an organization of students, both undergraduate and graduate, whose purpose is to represent and promote Cornell Cinema, as well as to advise and assist Cornell Cinema in its overall mission to offer the Cornell and greater Ithaca community a wide variety of cinematic and media experiences, for both educational and entertainment purposes.

name: Circle K at Cornell
description: Circle K at Cornell is a part of Circle K International. Our organization is based around the 3 tenets: service, leadership, and fellowship. This year we are focusing on the ways we can do small acts of service to improve the day to day lives of those in our community.

name: Civil and Environmental Engineering Graduate Student Association
description: The Civil and Environmental Engineering Graduate Student Association (CEE GSA) organizes social and cultural events for graduate students as well as promotes professional activities. The CEE GSA strives to foster communication among graduate students from different concentrations, staff and faculty, and to provide a forum for the free exchange of ideas.

name: Claritas: A Journal of Christian Thought
description: The Cornell Claritas is an ecumenical, interdenominational Christian publication that was founded on the hope of starting thoughtful Christian conversations within the academic community. Through our journal, blog, and events, we seek to articulate and connect the truth of Christ to every person and every study.

name: Class Notes
description: The Class Notes is a co-ed a cappella group with the purpose of bringing high quality music to the Cornell community.

name: Classics Society at Cornell
description: The Classics Society shall be to foster an appreciation of the study of ancient Greece and Rome, by looking to its languages, philosophies, archaeology, art, history, literature, and cultures to inform our contemporary world.

name: Club Sports Council
description: CSC allocates funds to nearly 70 undergraduate student organizations. Our mission is to support club sport teams in their ability to foster community and belonging at Cornell through funding opportunities.

name: Co-Ed Wrestling Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of Club Wrestling shall be to provide an opportunity for members of the Cornell community to learn and practice wrestling.

name: Coalition for De-Polarization at Cornell
description: The unifying goals of CDPC are to improve the preparation and mental wellbeing of all Cornellians in the context of polarization, and to reduce polarization where appropriate. CDPC aims to showcase cross-political agreement, promote empathy and constructive disagreement across ideological boundaries, teach skills to navigate a polarized world, and sponsor other activities relevant to its goals. CDPC does not typically promote any political ideology over others, and may serve as a platform for unifying voices during times of divided campus opinion, including advocating for depolarization, areas

name: Coalition for Healthy School Food
description: The Coalition for Healthy School Food (CHSF) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that introduces plant-based foods and nutrition education in schools to educate the whole school community about the health, environmental, and social justice issues of our food choices.

name: Coastal Conservation Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of the Coastal Conservation Club at Cornell shall be to: (1) educate and involve the Cornell community in marine conservation and policy, (2) lead fundraising efforts for marine conservation and research-oriented organizations, (3) drive local and oceanic policy change as it relates to marine and aquatic life, and (4) connect students with nature through hands-on participation in marine preservation. Coastal Conservation Club at Cornell exists to facilitate Cornell’s coastal relationships through guest speakers, cleanup within Ithaca’s context and beyond, trips, workshops, and more

name: CoCitizens Lab
description: Empowering collaborative, democratic and sustainable initiatives in your communities.

name: Cog Dog Theatre Troupe
description: The purpose of the Cog Dog Theatre Troupe is to put on theatre that provokes reflection, creates discussion and inspires action and change. In particular, our being independent allows us to engage students across all colleges and majors This organization is a registered student organization of Cornell University.

name: College and Career Readiness Club
description: The mission of The College and Career Readiness Program shall be to establish a career and college readiness program to provide a direct link between Cornell students and high school students. We will establish an academic curriculum to be used as a handbook to aid mentor meetings, as well as a podcast series. The goal of this organization is to be a supportive organization for first-generation and low-income high school students pursuing college or other career-related goals. We aim to pair Cornell students with a high school in the Ithaca area in order to provide individualized help and grou

name: College of Veterinary Medicine Office of the Dean
College Republicans at Cornell
description: The College Republicans organize activities, host speakers, participate in debates, and much more while promoting conservative principles in a social and educational manner. Our principles are grounded in the fundamental ideals of the American republic and the supreme object of our efforts is the advancement of a just civil government and responsible citizenry.

name: Collegetown Magazine
description: Collegetown embodies the youth, vigor, and hope of a Collegetown called Ithaca, New York, by producing interesting, thoughtful, and sharp journalism that fosters public discourse and community at Cornell and in the local community.

name: Collegiate New York Farm Bureau at Cornell University
description: The Purpose of the Organization shall be: i. To serve as a connection between current industry professionals and agricultural students. ii. To Interact with legislators at both the State level in Albany and the national level in Washington, D.C.; iii. To promote agriculture and related fields; iv. To offer opportunities for students in leadership and citizenship engagement encompassing career development, service learning and professional networking; v. To familiarize members with, and to maintain cooperative relations with, NYFB and AFBF organizations; and vi. To create a diverse student orga

name: COLLIS Institute for Catholic Thought and Culture
description: COLLIS's mission to create and foster a student community in support and partnership with COLLIS Institute, a Catholic institute associated with Cornell University.

name: Colombian Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of the Colombian Association shall be to create a community of solidarity and networking among the Colombian community at Cornell University and any other member of the community interested in the country. It aims to be a collective space to offer collective support, networking, to encourage research and interdisciplinarity.

name: Colombianos Unidos
description: The mission of Colombianos Unidos shall be to provide a location and community in which students can cultivate their knowledge of culture, community, identity, and all things related to the country that unites us—Colombia.

name: Combat Robotics at Cornell
description: The mission of Combat Robotics @ Cornell (CRC) is to inspire students both inside and outside of engineering to develop skills and gain experience in the exciting field of combat robotics. We strive to create a community where above all, learning is encouraged and members are willing and able to contribute to the best of their abilities, whether it be through helping to build the robot, organizing logistics for competition, securing sponsorships and grants from companies, or working to maintain the team's public image through the team's website and social media accounts. Our organization aims

name: Committee on US/Latin American Relations Cornell Chapter
description: The Committee on U.S.-Latin American Relations (CUSLAR) is a Cornell University-based organization, founded in 1965, which seeks to promote justice and mutual understanding among the people of the United States, Latin America and the Caribbean. The members of CUSLAR are a diverse group of people united in our concern about the role of the United States in the social, political and economic affairs of the region. CUSLAR supports the right of the people of Latin America and the Caribbean to self-determination and control over decisions that affect their lives and communities.

name: Communication Graduate Student Association
description: We are the official club organization for graduate students in the Department of Communication. Our duty is foster a sense of community within the department. We start by making sure that the graduate students have opportunities to relax, have fun, and socialize throughout the year. Additionally, we support department efforts to further their professional development through such events as workshops and roundtable discussions.

name: Community Church Leadership Program
description: The purpose of CCLP shall be to offer a holistic whole person approach to leadership development that is grounded in the Pentecostal Christian faith and focused on successful student outcomes. Primarily, this organization focuses on spiritual, intellectual, vocational, social, and professional leadership development. We believe in James 2:26, that faith without action is dead.

name: Community Elderly Partnership at Cornell
description: The mission of Community Elderly Partnership at Cornell (CEP) is to reduce social isolation and improve the quality of life for residents of nursing homes in the Ithaca community. CEP aims to achieve this mission by visiting local nursing homes every week in order to foster relationships and mutual learning amongst its members and the residents. Additionally, CEP strives to promote intergenerational awareness of the issues that face the elderly in today’s society. https://tinyurl.com/Officer-Responsibilites

name: Community Gardens at Cornell
description: We have 3 purposes. One is to rent for a modest charge that includes plowing, compost, cover crops, and water, garden plots to Cornell students and members of the Cornell family and community. Second, we furnish surplus vegetables we grow to the local food banks .Third, we encourage Cornell scientists and researchers to visit and watch what we do in case we can provide some location that may assist their research.

name: Community Learning and Service Partnership
description: The Community Learning and Service Partnership program (CLASP) is a mutual learning opportunity for Cornell employees and students to work together in learning partnerships. Employees can set personal learning goals for the semester, such as learning basic computer skills, English language learning, and more.

name: Community Partnership Funding Board
description: The Community Partnership Funding Board (CPFB), is a student-run board that seeks to foster student leadership and social responsibility by encouraging students to take action against social problems. The CPFB assists students in developing grassroots community action projects and administers grants made possible by the Student Activities Fee via the Student Assembly.

name: Community Work Study Program
description: The Community Work-Study Program, sponsored by the Cornell Public Service Center (PSC), enables Cornell Federal Work-Study (FWS) students to work for nonprofit organizations, schools, and municipalities mainly in Ithaca and Tompkins County but also anywhere in the U.S.

name: Compass: The Cornell & George Junior Republic Partnership
description: Our organization functions in association with and with support from the Einhorn Center for Community Engagement and the George Junior Republic High School (GJR). Our objectives are: 1. To centralize the needs and interests of the GJR students in the development and maintenance of quality after-school programming 2. To critically reflect on off-campus civic engagement and the larger systems in which we enact such engagement 3. To nourish a reciprocal partnership in which Cornell students both provide resources for and learn from GJR students 4. To provide support and opportunities for personal

name: Computational & Quantitative Social Science at Cornell
description: The mission of Computational & Quantitative Social Science at Cornell shall be to apply mathematical, statistical, and computational methods to conduct and advance interdisciplinary social science research on pressing real-world questions.

name: Computational Biology Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of the CBGSA is to build a community for the Computational Biology students and support them for success in graduate school and their future careers.

name: Computational Sustainability Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of Computational Sustainability Club at Cornell shall be to build a community around computational approaches to environmental challenges by eliminating barriers to entry, empowering students through workshops and panels, student-led local projects, and fostering networks in computational sustainability.

name: Computer Reuse Association at Cornell
description: The Cornell Computer Reuse Association Club (CCRA) is a student organization at Cornell University dedicated to "donate[ing] computers and other computer-related technology to humanitarian organizations in the developing world and in the local Ithaca community." The students, along with their adviser, collect and refurbish used computers and donate them to community centers, orphanages, schools and other organizations in the United States and developing countries. In its many years of existence, the organization has donated over 2,000 computers to places as far away as Nicaragua, Zambia, Jamai

name: Concrete Canoe at Cornell
description: Our team’s mission is to collaboratively engineer the most strong, lightweight canoe possible out of concrete mixtures. We present our work in the spring ASCE Regional Concrete Canoe Competition through a presentation and a race, displaying our innovative new concrete mix and molding techniques.

name: Conference & Event Services
description: Conference & Event Services

name: Consult Your Community at Cornell
description: Small businesses are symbols of the American Dream brought to life. According to the Small Business Administration, they employ nearly 60% of the private workforce and created nearly 70% of net new jobs after the 2008 recession. The economy relies on small businesses, but they're in trouble. Only 50% of small businesses make it to their 5th year of operations. Many small business owners struggle with turnover of staff and operational issues, and many do not capitalize on digital tools to grow their business. CYC selects only the most highly qualified undergraduates from America's best universi

name: Consulting Group at Cornell
description: The Consulting Group at Cornell is a student organization that provides strategic consulting services to businesses, education institutions and non-profit organizations. Founded in 2007, we have advised over 60 clients across a diverse range of industry and functional areas, and have become the premier undergraduate consulting organization at Cornell University. Our dedicated team of student consultants deliver high impact services to clients through semester-long projects in the Fall and Spring academic semesters. With support from experienced faculty advisers from the Johnson, Dyson, and Ind

name: Contigo Peru
description: As a cultural organization, Contigo Perú aims to showcase and promote awareness of the abundant and diverse Peruvian culture. In addition, we look forward to engaging in close observance, discussion and analysis of the various events and issues related to Perú and its neighboring South American countries.

name: Convocation Committee
description: Create an experience that embodies our class that stays with students for a lifetime.

name: Corean Graduate Catholic Community at Cornell
description: To provide a ground for Korean or people of Korean descents who believe in Roman Catholicism to carry out and continue the work of Jesus Christ on Earth through fellowships and different activities.

name: Cornell Advancing Science and Policy Club
description: Learn about and create a community interested in science policy issues, educate the public about science and policy, & prepare for a career in science policy, industry, or media.

name: Cornell AI Alignment Club
description: CAIA is a community of students and researchers conducting research and outreach to mitigate risks from advanced AI systems. #Artificial Intelligence #AI Safety #AI Alignment #AI Policy #AI Governance #AI Forecasting

name: Cornell AI Strategy Club
description: To lower the barrier of entry of AI education and provide it to all students from all majors, with any skill level. We will do this by providing relevant lessons/presentations, facilitating leadership experience through hands-on projects and workshops, hosting speakers across the industry, and fostering the larger AI community on campus.

name: Cornell Algo Trading Club
description: Cornell Algo Trading Club exists to turn rigorous, reproducible research into live, student-managed algorithmic strategies while cultivating an open, practitioner-led education and speaker program that equips Cornell students to think critically, build responsibly, and communicate clearly about systematic investing.

name: Cornell Alpha Fund Club
description: Cornell Alpha Fund Club, located at Cornell University, is, and shall be, an organization devoted to maintaining a diversified portfolio of investments in various asset classes, while honing investment knowledge and skills of its members and inspiring discussion around current industry news and market trends.

name: Cornell Alternative Investments Club
description: Cornell Alternative Investments Club seeks to offer high-quality educational, professional, and experiential learning opportunities for Club Members. The organization is devoted to providing a robust, informational, and beneficial experience for club members.

name: Cornell Amateur Radio Club
description: The Cornell Amateur Radio Club, W2CXM, is a group of undergraduates, graduates, and other members of the Cornell and Ithaca community whose common interest is the hobby of amateur radio. Amateur radio activity at Cornell University dates as far back as 1915, under the callsign "8XU." Formed in 1949, the CARC has been licensed under the callsign "W2CXM" since 1951.

name: Cornell Amnesty International Club
description: The Amnesty International Club at Cornell University strives to promote and protect human rights both locally and globally. Through advocacy, education, and action, we aim to raise awareness of injustices and mobilize the campus community to stand in solidarity with marginalized and oppressed individuals. Our work aligns with Amnesty International's core values of justice, freedom, and equality, as we campaign against violations such as discrimination, unjust detentions, and threats to freedom of expression. By fostering an inclusive and informed student body, we seek to empower individuals to

name: Cornell Anglers' Society
description: The purpose of Cornell Anglers’ Society (CAS) is to promote sustainable fishing practices, educate others on fishing/fishery conservation, and create a family-like community. It aims to provide a diverse environment for members dedicated to fishing, aquatic life, and their sustainability.

name: Cornell Anime Club
description: The Cornell Anime Club is an independent, student-run organization founded at and affiliated with Cornell University. It was established in the spring of 1988 by Masaki Takai (’91) and Kay Lillibridge (’92). The purpose of the Cornell Anime Club (formerly the Cornell Japanese Animation Society) is to spread our love of Japanese animation and to allow fans to celebrate and expand their interest in the medium as a community.

name: Cornell Anti-Detention Alliance Club
description: The Cornell Anti-Detention Alliance, affiliated with the Feminist, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Program at Cornell, supports detained and previously detained immigrants through direct services and grassroots advocacy. We demand a humane immigration system that does not exploit and incarcerate immigrants, in Upstate New York and beyond.
