name: Cornell Architecture Student Practice Club
parent: AFFILIATION: College of Architecture Art and Planning
description: To give students experience in an architecture firm structure and give them the opportunity to work on infrastructure and design projects that will build their desired skills. Bonus purpose is to provide Cornell Students the opportunity to design infrastructure projects that can be built around campus.

name: Cornell Asian Pacific Student Union
description: The Cornell Asian Pacific-Islander Student Union is the umbrella organization for Asian/Asian-American and Asian-interest organizations at Cornell University. We aim to bring undergraduate organizations representing students of Asian descent together to facilitate networking among the members of the community. We strive to be the platform for the Cornell community to learn about and understand our diverse ethnic backgrounds in order to form a more cohesive community.

name: Cornell Assistive Technologies Project Team
description: The mission of the Cornell Assistive Technologies Project Team is to champion inclusivity by developing assistive technologies for people with disabilities and to raise awareness about the impact of adapted solutions and assistive technologies among youths and communities in Ithaca and beyond.

name: Cornell Astronomical Society
description: The purpose of our organization is to: 1) Unite the people at Cornell who are fascinated by astronomy, stargazing, and/or the night sky. 2) Run weekly public stargazing nights at Fuertes Observatory. 3) Provide the opportunity for the public and club members to learn more about astronomy and stargazing. 4) Teach club members how to use our telescopes and become better stargazers.

name: Cornell Athletics
description: Athletics & Physical Education byline funding from the SA and GPSA

name: Cornell Aviation Club
description: The mission of this organization is to cultivate a community of students who are interested in aviation, from those who already have a pilot's license to those who just think planes are cool. We provide students with the opportunity to explore the world of aviation through learning opportunities, connections to industry leaders, and tangible experiences with flying. We have events throughout each semester, including club meetings, events at the Ithaca Airport (e.g. visiting the East Hill Flying Club to learn about being a private pilot, a tour of the control tower, etc.), and aviation industry

name: Cornell Ballet Club
description: The purpose of Cornell Ballet Club shall be to extend the opportunity of classical ballet technique to all Cornell students who seek to continue their artistic growth in this discipline, fostering a tight-knit and close community of talented ballerinas and ballet dancers. We are a student-led group that meets weekly to take ballet classes and learn variations and classical ballet repertoire, working on pieces for our semi-annual showcase.

name: Cornell Big Red Club Volleyball
description: The Cornell Big Red Club Volleyball is a student-run organization at Cornell University for female athletes who wish to play competitive volleyball. Our mission is to provide a safe, fun environment. Practices are held biweekly and the ladies travel to other Colleges and Universities in the Northeast in order to participate in NWVCL tournaments.

name: Cornell Bioacoustics Club
description: Explore the fingerlakes region through sound, connecting people to the nature around us acoustically. We want to reach out between disciplines to make the acoustical world as accessible as possible and connect people of all pursuits: artists, engineers, scientists, and the local community to explore, celebrate, and share the nature that surrounds us.

name: Cornell BioVentures and Life Sciences Entrepreneurship Club
description: The mission of Cornell BioVentures is to provide students with hands-on experience in biotechnology investing and venture creation through two integrated arms: Public Equities and Translational Venture. Members conduct scientific, clinical, commercial, and financial diligence to evaluate therapeutics investments, develop investment theses, and assess emerging technologies for company formation.

name: Cornell Bitcoin Club
description: The purpose of the Cornell Bitcoin Club shall be to contribute to fostering a global network of Bitcoin students, promoting education and collaboration and connecting students with opportunities and resources within the Bitcoin ecosystem. As Bitcoin is for every human, so is the Cornell Bitcoin Club.

name: Cornell Brawl Stars Club
description: Brawl Stars is a popular mobile game that has been established ever since Dec 12, 2018. However, over the past few years (2024-2026), Brawl Stars saw a large increase in player base. Due to its increasing popularity, making a club where the people at Cornell can play Brawl Stars and find teammates makes sense. It is easily accessible since it is a free mobile game, our organization would allow people who enjoy playing to connect over this shared interest and make friends while also encouraging new players. While Brawl Stars is a game of skill, strategy is also very important for victory, so th

name: Cornell Business Analytics Club
description: Cornell Business Analytics Club is a student-run organization that offers pro-bono business analytics consulting services to clients, both on and off campus. Our motto stems from the idea that data-driven decision making is a key to successful businesses and organizations.

name: Cornell Capital Club
description: (Through our rigorous 10-week new member education process, new members work on two case studies of successful startups. This process provides members with a deep understanding of how to obtain investment, manage finances, develop ideas, and drive company growth. In the final three weeks, students work with teammates to initiate and develop their own projects. Then, they pitch to successful investors associated with Cornell Capital Club, which is an exclusive opportunity available only to Cornell Capital Club members)

name: Cornell Career Network
description: At Cornell, you’re not just developing a career, you’re shaping your future. The Cornell Career Network is a collaborative, campus-wide ecosystem that provides the resources and support to help you explore your options, refine your vision, and build the skills and connections to thrive in an ever-changing world.

name: Cornell Catholic Graduate and Professional Student Group
description: The purpose of our organization is to create a community of Catholic graduate and professional students at Cornell and encourage the discussion of topics related to the Catholic faith and life as a professional or graduate student.

name: Cornell Center for Astrophysics and Planetary Science
Cornell Center for Social Sciences
description: CCSS accelerates, enhances, and amplifies this research by providing advanced computing and other research infrastructure, seeding grants and fellowships, supporting quantitative and qualitative research, and building a diverse and inclusive community of scholars.

name: Cornell Chai Club
description: The mission of the Cornell Chai Club is to provide a platform for students to explore and appreciate the rich cultural traditions of tea from around the world, engage in meaningful discussions, and build lasting connections through shared experiences. We strive to promote relaxation, cultural exchange, and a deeper understanding of the art of tea-making.

name: Cornell Chapter of International City/County Management Association
description: The purpose of the Cornell University City/County Management Association shall be to integrate students into the local government management profession by providing a connection to local government leaders, resources, and the ICMA Code of Ethics. Additionally, we serve as a leadership pipeline by developing the next generation of local government professionals through networking opportunities, skill development, mentorship, and professional engagement, including free access to resources and the annual ICMA conference.

name: Cornell Chapter of Partners in Health Engage
description: At Partners in Health, we believe healthcare is a universal human right. Around the world, we fight injustice by providing care first to those who need it most. We are a team of students committed to healthcare equity and community education around the importance of equitable healthcare systems through driven campaigns that build and direct power towards generating new resources, fostering public discourse, and advocating for effective policies that advance health care as a human right. We are fervently dedicated to advocacy for the federal funding and policy needed to support Partners in Heal

name: Cornell Chimes
description: The Cornell Chimes The bells of Cornell, referred to as the Cornell Chimes, are the heartbeat of campus life, marking the hours and chiming daily concerts. The original set of nine bells, a gift of Jennie McGraw, first rang out at the university's opening ceremonies October 7, 1868. Over time the chime has been recast and expanded to 21 bells. Three concerts are performed each day while classes are in session.

name: Cornell Cinema
description: Cornell Cinema is one of the leading campus film exhibition programs in the country and an integral part of the fabric of campus life at Cornell. The cinema presents more than 75 films each semester and features an eclectic mix of contemporary and classic titles from around the globe. Working in collaboration with partners across campus and beyond, Cornell Cinema seeks to spark conversation, inspire innovative thinking, and advance interdisciplinary teaching through collective encounters with the art of film. The cinema operates four to five nights per week in the historic Willard Straight The

name: Cornell Club Ice Hockey D2
description: Our purpose is to increase the skill level of players dedicated to playing hockey at Cornell so that they may enjoy playing hockey at the collegiate level through a low time commitment. The organization competes at the Division II level of AAU College Hockey and practices twice a week throughout the season. The team may occasionally promote players to the AAU D1 Club Hockey team based on performance and/or need.

name: Cornell Club Rowing
description: We provide an opportunity for all past and new rowers a chance to get back on the water. The goal of the team is to foster discipline, focus, and friendship on and off the water. We compete in various local regattas through the Cascadilla Boat Club (CBC). As a competitive team, hard work is expected.

name: Cornell CMSX
description: To maintain and build on CMSX, a course management system used by Cornell's faculty and students to aid the daily administration of classes.

name: Cornell Coffee Club
description: Coffee Club is founded on three tenants a. Education: officers oversee lessons regarding the science, history, politics, economics, and social impact of coffee b. Outreach: officers communicate with local organizations about opportunities for collaboration c. Craft: officers oversee education regarding coffee brewing processes

name: Cornell Cognitive Science Club
description: Our mission is to build community for Cognitive Science majors and students interested in the mind and brain. We explore diverse fields—neuroscience, psychology, computer science, linguistics, philosophy, and more—by hosting social events, academic discussions, creative projects, and community service opportunities.

name: Cornell Commodity Trading Club
description: To inform Cornell students about the commodity trading industry as a whole and explore the job opportunities within.

name: Cornell Companions
description: Cornell Companions is an animal-assisted activities and animal-assisted therapy program. We strive to educate our volunteers on the beneficial effects of the human-animal bond, and to foster positive relationships between people and animals.

name: Cornell Concert Commission
description: The purpose of Cornell Concert Commission shall be to provide the Cornell community with popular and diverse, contemporary musical entertainment which is both financially sound and responsive to the community's needs and desires.

name: Cornell Consulting Club
description: The mission of Cornell Consulting Club is to bring management consulting acumen and industry exposure to students of all levels and all backgrounds. The club has three main purposes: to teach its members the skills and tools fundamental in strategy consulting, to provide students with practical experience by working on projects with local, national and international businesses (and provide clients with top of the line services), and to bridge the gap between its members and the consulting industry through company visits and networking events.

name: Cornell Contra Dance Club
description: The purpose of Cornell Contra Dance Club shall be to promote and facilitate engagement in contra dancing in the Cornell community.

name: Cornell Cooperative Extension of Tompkins County
description: Cornell Cooperative Extension puts knowledge to work in pursuit of economic vitality, ecological sustainability and social well-being.

name: Cornell Coptic Club
description: The mission of establishing a Coptic Club on our college campus is rooted in the desire to create a nurturing and inclusive space for students of the Coptic faith and those interested in learning about it. Our mission is to foster a sense of community among Coptic Orthodox students, helping them strengthen their spiritual journeys, maintain their cultural heritage, and engage with the wider campus community. We aim to promote interfaith dialogue, understanding, and respect while serving as a resource for those seeking knowledge about the Coptic Orthodox tradition. Through our activities, event

name: Cornell Credit Investment Club
description: The Cornell Credit Club aims to enhance students’ understanding of credit scores and personal financial literacy through practical education and peer collaboration. We empower members to build and manage their credit responsibly, develop lifelong financial habits, and gain confidence in navigating the financial systems that shape their futures. By fostering awareness and accessibility, we strive to create a more financially informed Cornell community.

name: Cornell Cup Robotics
description: The mission of this team is to provide a valuable, practical experience for students with robotics and embedded systems, and to demonstrate the extraordinary technology that we are able to create.

name: Cornell Current Club
description: Cornell Current is Cornell University's first current events and industry trends organization created to provide Cornell students a forum to proactively analyze the global and industry trends that are shaping our world today. Our members are not looking to simply discuss current events and industry trends as it pertains to the facts of what happened. We are highly interested in analysis of these trends: the why, the cause and effect, the bigger ramifications, and data-driven forward outlook to where trends could end up.

name: Cornell Dance Team
description: We are the Cornell University Dance Team! Since our establishment in 2017, we have been sharing our love of dance both on campus and with the community.

name: Cornell Data Strategy Club
description: The purpose of Cornell Data Strategy Club is to serve as a platform for students interested in merging data science with business consulting and finance.

name: Cornell Department of Music
description: Our special distinction is a dedication to excellence in the study of music that reflects a concern for the constant interaction of scholarship, performance, and composition by faculty members and students alike. We present numerous concerts throughout the year that are open to all.

name: Cornell Dining
description: Cornell Dining takes pride in providing our guests with a rich dining experience, and not just a meal. There's always something new and different to choose from at our 30 campus eateries, which include dining rooms, cafes, coffee houses, and food courts, and convenience stores.

name: Cornell Employees Working Remotely
description: This group was created by the Division of Human Resources to serve as a forum to connect, share experiences, ask questions, and offer tips/best practices - all related to remote work.

name: Cornell Entertainment Engineering & Design Club
description: To inspire the next generation of entertainment innovators.

name: Cornell Equity Derivatives Club
description: The Cornell Equity Derivatives Club (CEDC) seeks to educate, empower, and connect students interested in the complex and rapidly evolving world of equity derivatives — including options, futures, and other structured products.

name: Cornell Ethics Bowl Club
description: Our mission as the Cornell Ethics Bowl shall be to foster collaborative discourse around contemporary ethical issues. The APPE "supports and trains the next generation of ethics faculty and professionals, works to improve ethical conduct in our communities and workplaces, and advances public dialogue in ethics and values."

name: Cornell Fanworks Club
description: The Cornell Fanworks Club seeks to provide an open, inclusive, and collaborative space for creating and discussing all types of fanworks including, but not limited to, fanfiction, fanart, fan videos, and cosplay. Creators and consumers of fanworks from all fandoms are welcome and encouraged to participate.

name: Cornell Fashion Collective
description: The Cornell Fashion Collective, formerly the Cornell Design League, is a student-run organization that provides members of the Cornell community with an outlet to express creativity in fashion and fashion management. Each spring, our organization presents a professional runway show featuring the talent of students who both design apparel and manage the operations of the show. Our organization gives students the opportunity to practice design, demonstrate their talents, and learn how to produce a large-scale fashion event.

name: Cornell Fashion Industry Network
description: The purpose of CFIN shall be to serve as Cornell's direct link to the fashion industry by facilitating relationships between students and alumni as well as teaching tangible networking and professional skills.

name: Cornell Filipino Student Association
description: 1. To promote and protect the interest of the Filipino community. 2. To promote awareness of Filipino values and culture within the community and CFA. 3. To foster unity and friendship among its members. 4. To promote friendship and cooperation with other organizations and entities.

name: Cornell Financial Analysts Club
description: CFA is formed with the vision to give students the opportunity to further their education in the finance industry, ultimately being able to secure employment. CFA will expose its members to a proprietary 10-week education series focused on financial services interview preparation, real-world professionals, and programs in order to enhance the learning experience. We welcome and encourage all students at Cornell to join the CFA community. We welcome and encourage all students at Cornell to join the CFA community. CFA will provide support, guidance, and the ability for students to collectively o

name: Cornell FinTech Club
description: The Cornell FinTech Club (CFT) is the first all-encompassing, undergraduate-led fintech club that aims to create spaces and opportunities for students interested in fintech through weekly discussions, continuous education, and events such as hackathons, conferences, and corporate speakers.

name: Cornell Go Club
description: "The Cornell Go Club is dedicated to promoting the study and enjoyment of the ancient strategic board game Go (also known as Weiqi in Chinese or Baduk in Korean). Our mission is to create a welcoming community where players of all skill levels, from complete beginners to experienced competitors, can learn, play, and appreciate the depth and beauty of the game. We host weekly meetings every Thursday from 7-11pm in Willard Straight Hall, offering friendly matches, teaching sessions, and casual tournaments. The Cornell Go Club aims to foster strategic thinking, cross-cultural understanding, and a

name: Cornell Golf Club
description: The purpose of the Cornell Club Golf Team is to combine as a unit of competitive golfers in the Cornell community to grow in our appreciation and expertise of the game. The Cornell Golf Team will conform to the uniform system of handicapping and rules set forth by the United States Golf Association. The Club Golf Team will be committed to the traditions and history of the game and compete on a national level as members of the National Collegiate Club Golf Association.

name: Cornell Graduate Product Management Club
description: The purpose of the Cornell Graduate Product Management Club shall be to empower graduate students to envision, design, and develop impactful products through cross-disciplinary collaboration, bridging academia and industry via experiential learning opportunities, and fostering a community of future leaders equipped with the skills, resources, and networks to drive meaningful innovation

name: Cornell Growth Capital Club
description: The Cornell Growth Capital Club is looking to mentor future generations of leaders in the financial industry specifically those who are looking to enter the field of growth capital. During our new member education process, we will provide hands-on experience through mock portfolios and mentorship to provide a basic understanding of the growth capital and the related fields of private equity, venture capital, credit, and investment banking. In addition, we hope to inspire and provide members with knowledge not only in the growth capital industry, but wherever your career takes them. In true Cor

name: Cornell Hedge Fund Club
description: Through real-world investing experience, ongoing education, and mentorship, we seek to provide students with the opportunities to develop their skills and interests in finance, regardless of their background. We are committed to our foundational values of integrity, innovation, and diversity to sustain an atmosphere that maximizes our members' personal and professional growth.

name: Cornell Horn Club
description: To share the beautiful sound of all brass instruments with the Cornell community.

name: Cornell Housing
description: Housing and Residential Life at Cornell provides student support and programming in the residence halls to make your experience engaging, meaningful, and gratifying. Our living and learning environment comprises seventeen undergraduate residence halls, including communities for first-year students, upper-level students, and our eight Program Houses as well as residential communities for Graduate and Professional students. Residential life at Cornell promotes the intrinsic value and worth of the individual in a welcoming and inclusive community.

name: Cornell Human Ecology in New York City
Cornell Hunger Relief Program
description: Cornell Hunger Relief Program works to learn about local and global food systems and to address hunger issues in Ithaca and Tompkins County by facilitating food drives to benefit local food pantries.

name: Cornell Hyperloop Project Team
description: The purpose of Cornell Hyperloop shall be to bring the concept of Hyperloop to life, spearhead the development of Hyperloop technology, and show the world that Hyperloop is the next breakthrough in the transportation industry.

name: Cornell ICPC Club
description: Cornell ICPC Club is Cornell's official competitive programming team. Every year, we participate in the International Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC) and organize training sessions to help team members improve their problem-solving and algorithmic thinking skills.

name: Cornell IMSD/Office of Inclusion & Academic Excellence
description: The Office of Inclusion & Academic Excellence (OIAE) strives to comprehensively embed and integrate Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), accessibility, and inclusive well-being in the CVM and the veterinary profession enhancing a greater sense of belonging through community-building and respectful dialogue.

name: Cornell In Washington
description: Cornell in Washington, through the Brooks School of Public Policy, provides a transformational semester, a Washington internship, world-class courses, and signature D.C. experiences.

name: Cornell Indoor Futsal Club
description: The purpose of CORNELL INDOOR FUTSAL CLUB shall be to promote community, belonging, and fitness through a shared passion for the sport of futsal.

name: Cornell Institute for China Economic Research
Cornell Institute for Food Systems
description: Today’s society, and specifically global food systems, is faced with the challenge of feeding seven billion people – nine billion by 2050. The Cornell Institute for Food Systems (CIFS) comprises a multidisciplinary group of Faculty Fellows who tackle diverse issues in the food industry to meet this challenge. CIFS Faculty Fellows engage with the Institute and its industry partners in a variety of mechanisms including collaborative research, scientific advisory roles, and the development of student talent pipelines.

name: Cornell Institute for Healthy Futures
description: Cornell Institute for Healthy Futures (CIHF) is an academic center combining hospitality, environmental design, and health policy and management into a broad-based platform to improve service in healthcare. To achieve this goal, the institute develops and supports multidisciplinary educational programs, sponsors and disseminates research, and hosts conferences, roundtables, meetings, and practicum projects.

name: Cornell Investments Club
description: The purpose of Cornell Investments Club shall be to provide a comprehensive and generalist investment education that covers all facets of the finance industry. Our aim is to equip members with a broad understanding of investment strategies and financial principles, enabling them to navigate the complexities of various financial markets.

name: Cornell Lab of Ornithology
description: Our mission is to interpret and conserve the Earth’s biological diversity through research, education, and citizen science focused on birds and nature.

name: Cornell Latine Policy Forum
description: The Cornell Latine Policy Forum unites undergraduate, graduate, and Ph.D. students who are dedicated to examining how public policy and administration can advance equity and inclusion for Latine communities. We provide a space for discussion, research, and collaborative learning that connects academic perspectives with the lived experiences of Latine populations across local, national, and global contexts.

name: Cornell Latinos in Business Club
description: The purpose of Cornell Latinos in Business (CLB) Club shall be to provide Latino students and students interested in LatAm at Cornell University with the necessary resources and opportunities to succeed in a career in business through comprehensive education and community. The organization will honor Cornell University's broader mission of ‘Any Person, Any Study’ by allowing anyone interested in business to apply.

name: Cornell Law School Dean of Students Office
description: Cornell Law School's mission remains that articulated by Cornell President Andrew Dickson White upon the founding of the law school 132 years ago: "Our aim is to keep its instruction strong, its standard high, and so to produce … a fair number of well-trained, large-minded, morally based lawyers in the best sense."

name: Cornell Law Squash Association
description: To promote wellness and camaraderie in the Law School community through use of Myron Taylor Hall's athletic facilities.

name: Cornell Mafia Club
description: We hold weekly meetings for the purpose of playing Mafia, a role-playing game that blends logic and psychology with a twist of mystery. A dynamic conflict between an uninformed majority and a hidden, well-informed minority—and often, third parties with their own chaotic goals. Games are moderated by members brave enough to put their game design to the test. Membership is free and easy: just show up! 9PM Fridays at the Keeton House downstairs lounge (near the dining hall).

name: Cornell Malaysian Students Association
description: COMSA is an association that conducts activities to promote esprit de corps among Malaysian students at Cornell.

name: Cornell Marketing Club
description: Cornell Marketing Club aims to help students with their professional careers by demonstrating the relevance of marketing and strategy in every aspect of the business world.

name: Cornell Matcha Club
description: The purpose of Cornell Matcha Club is to bring the Cornell community together through a shared love of matcha and conversation. At each meeting, we will share traditional matcha, as well as the history and traditions of matcha.

name: Cornell Medical Brigade Club
description: The proposed objective for this club is to equip and provide pre-med students and their peers with the necessary resources, skills and opportunities to make a significant and meaningful impact in a country that lacks adequate healthcare facilities. This organization will not only assist those in need, but also provide hands-on experience (under the supervision of the national chapter) for students to immerse themselves into their future profession. This will enable students to have a deep understanding of the challenges of the healthcare system and the complexities of providing medical care in

name: Cornell Men's Club Basketball
description: To provide students with a fun and competitive environment to play basketball, and compete against local and national competition.

name: Cornell Men's Volleyball Performance and Development Club
description: The Men’s Volleyball Performance & Development Club at Cornell was created to expand access to organized, high-level men’s volleyball for students who are passionate about the sport but not currently part of the travel A/B teams. Each year, over 35–40 students try out for the existing club, with fewer than 5 earning roster spots—leaving many experienced and motivated athletes without a structured environment to continue improving. This organization fills that gap by providing a comprehensive training and performance program focused on skill development, athletic preparation, and internal compe

name: Cornell Mergers & Acquisitions Club
description: The purpose of Cornell Mergers and Acquisitions Club shall be to expand students' understanding of the legal and financial complexities concerning the mergers and acquisitions process.

name: Cornell Negotiation Student Society
description: The Cornell Negotiation Student Society commits itself to promoting the interpersonal skills of negotiation, mediation, conflict resolution, and alike pursuits; to promoting scholarship in the aforementioned fields; to encouraging diversity in people and thought in the aforementioned fields.

name: Cornell New Hire Class of 2020
description: The New Hire Class of 2020 is an affinity group for benefits-eligible full-time employees who were hired and/or started their positions within a year. This will be a space where you can connect with colleagues from across the university who are fellow new hires. Share tips and information that support thriving at Cornell and in the Ithaca community.

name: Cornell Nightlife Hospitality Club
description: The Cornell Nightlife Hospitality Club explores the operational and managerial aspects of nightclubs, bars, and casinos. CNHC connects Cornell community members who are interested in the nightlife segment of hospitality with each other as well as with leaders in the field. These leaders have included Bill Walshe (CEO of Viceroy Hotels), David Grutman (Founder of Groot Hospitality), Sean Christie (Executive Vice President of Business Development at Wynn Resorts), and Scott Gerber (Principal and CEO of Gerber Group). The Cornell Nightlife Hospitality Club has pioneered a new path to learning abo

name: Cornell Nuclear is Clean Energy Club
description: Our mission is to raise awareness about nuclear power being a clean energy that can largely benefit decarbonization goals and eventually start including nuclear engineering and nuclear energy policy courses in Cornell’s curriculum.

name: Cornell Orchestras Board
description: The purpose of the Cornell Orchestras Board is to unify the members of both the Cornell Symphony and Chamber orchestras through various performance, service, and social events throughout the year. The board also plans orchestra tours and community outreach events within the Ithaca community.

name: Cornell Organization for Labor Action
description: The purpose of the Cornell Organization for Labor Action shall be to advance economic and workplace justice through collective, non-hierarchical organizing. We support and engage in the global struggle for labor rights, from efforts on our campus to those across the world. We foster solidarity between students and workers and advocate for systemic change toward economic justice through education and activism.

name: Cornell Origami Club
description: The purpose of Cornell Origami Club shall be to practice folding techniques, foster community, and cultural appreciation through the ancient art of origami.

name: Cornell Out of the Darkness Campus Walk
description: AFSP's mission is to save lives and bring hope to those affected by suicide. We fund research to improve interventions, train clinicians in suicide prevention, and advocate for policy that will save lives. We work to find better ways to reach those who suffer, and encourage schools, workplaces, and communities to make mental health a priority. Whether you’ve lost someone or are struggling with suicidal thinking, you are not alone. We bring people who have been affected by suicide out of the darkness, and give them opportunities to help others.

name: Cornell Outdoor Education
description: Cornell Outdoor Education develops teamwork, leadership, and growth through outdoor experience. We do so by: Teaching outdoor skills and judgment for lifelong recreation and fitness. Promoting environmental responsibility through personal connection to the natural world. Empowering individuals and groups to move beyond self-imposed limitations. Igniting a passion for experiential learning. Enhancing initiative, self-reliance, and compassion for others. Cornell Outdoor Education serves the broad membership of the Cornell community: students and student instructors, faculty and staff, alumni and

name: Cornell Partners in Expansion & Capital Club
description: CPEC aims to cultivate a dynamic and innovative community where aspiring finance professionals can engage deeply with the world of private equity. Our mission is to provide our members with unparalleled educational experiences, hands-on investment opportunities, and strategic networking platforms.

name: Cornell Pharmaceutical Outreach Club
description: The purpose of Cornell Pharmaceutical Outreach Club shall be to bring pharmaceutical industry leaders to campus through our outreach efforts and educate students on the drug development process, financial obligations of pharmaceutical companies, and opportunities that may exist within the industry for students across a wide variety of studies.

name: Cornell Physical Education and Recreation
description: Cornell Recreational Services offers a wide variety of fitness, wellness, sports and open recreation activities for Cornell students, staff, faculty, retirees and their spouses/partners. Through our broad-based programs, we try to promote a healthy and holistic lifestyle throughout the campus community. Recreational Services encompasses the Cornell Fitness Centers, Helen Newman Bowling Center, Helen Newman Hall Recreation Center, Intramural Sports, Noyes Community Recreation Center, and the Cornell University Wellness Program. name: Cornell Physical Intelligence Club
description: Our mission is to conduct rigorous, interdisciplinary research in physical artificial intelligence, with a focus on intelligent robotics systems. We aim to study how mechanical design, electrical systems, and artificial intelligence converge in the development of novel robotic systems that "think" through their bodies.

name: Cornell Pickleball Club
description: The Cornell Pickleball Club is dedicated to fostering a vibrant and inclusive community where students, faculty, and staff of all skill levels can come together to enjoy the sport of pickleball. We aim to create a welcoming environment that encourages sportsmanship, personal growth, and a lifelong love for the game.

name: Cornell Pogo Club
description: Our mission is to spread the joy, creativity, and athletic challenge of pogo sticking across the Cornell community. We aim to build an inclusive space where students of all skill levels — from first-time jumpers to advanced trick riders — can learn, train, and innovate together.

name: Cornell Pokémon ACE Trainers Club
description: The purpose of Cornell Pokémon ACE Trainers shall be to organize and host Pokemon related events on Cornell grounds to create an accessible environment available to interested students. This organization achieves this hosting related events centered on the Pokemon Trading Card Game (TCG), Video Game Championship (VGC), Pokemon GO, and trading to allow members to collaborate with peers through casual play, tournaments, and trading. These activities offer students opportunities to connect, compete, and deepen knowledge of Pokemon.

name: Cornell Poker Club
description: The mission of Cornell Poker Club is to provide undergrads with opportunities to learn, play, and master the exciting game of poker through meetings, social events, and tournaments. We also hope to promote diversity and inclusion to make poker available to all.

name: Cornell Policy Group
description: Cornell Policy Group is a non-partisan student-run think tank that engages college students in policy research, writing, and local advocacy.

name: Cornell Political Union
description: To provide Cornell a forum for the bipartisan debate and parliamentary discussion of political topics; to periodically publish bipartisan policy proposals and/or resolutions incorporating the findings of the debate and parliamentary discussion; to reduce hyper-partisanship through the thoughtful incorporation and acceptance of all political ideologies, and by the perseverance of strict neutrality by the Union's leadership; to sponsor events to promote the political education of the members and the Cornell community.

name: Cornell Productions
description: Cornell Productions (CP) is an entirely student-run organization that works to fulfill the lighting and sound reinforcement needs of on-campus events. We provide services for both student-run and non-student run events of all sizes. Our mission is to provide lighting and sound services professionally and entirely to our client's satisfaction.

name: Cornell Public Affairs Student Society
description: The Cornell Public Affairs Society (CPAS) is the official student-led organization representing the public policy student community at the Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy. Our mission is to foster a collaborative, inclusive, and engaged student community that supports academic success, professional development, public service values, and meaningful peer connections.

name: Cornell Real Estate Club
description: The Cornell Real Estate Club provides educational, professional, and networking opportunities that enable students to succeed in their real estate endeavors. The Cornell Real Estate Club leverages the University's unparalleled resources in business, hospitality, law, architecture, urban planning, public policy, and sustainability to develop well-informed professionals who understand the complexity of today's real estate industry. The Cornell Real Estate Club collaborates with the Center for Real Estate and Finance, Cornell Real Estate Council, and the Associate Real Estate Council (AREC-the gr

name: Cornell Roundnet
description: This organization is designed for the dual purpose of introducing new players to the game of Spikeball and connecting experienced players with others of similar skill levels. Even for students who have never heard of or seen Spikeball before, we aim to teach everything we know: the rules, the basics of play, and more advanced moves and tactics when appropriate. For us, Spikeball has provided countless afternoons and evenings of fun and we hope to share that with the rest of the Cornell community!

name: Cornell Russian Language Club
description: The mission of the Russian Language Society at Cornell is to provide a safe space for cross-cultural exchange using the Russian language as a medium for communication. Members will connect with each other through the cooking of our traditional dishes and celebration of cultural holidays. In addition, we hope to help members connect more deeply with their cultures by showcasing films, reading books, and playing games all in our native language.

name: Cornell School of Integrated Plant Sciences Graduate Student Council Club
description: The Graduate Student Council (GSC) is a representative body of graduate students across the five sections within SIPS: Horticulture, Plant Breeding and Genetics, Plant Biology, Soil and Crop Sciences, and Plant Pathology and Plant-Microbe Biology. We host SIPS-wide social and educational events. Representing the collective voice of SIPS graduate students, we to discuss current policies, action items, or concerns that arise within the SIPS community.

name: Cornell Seismic Design Project Team
description: The purpose of this organization is to give students hand-on experience in seismic design while building structures to compete with other colleges and universities across the country. Students will use computer softwares, learn about design and seismology, and review the litigation codes for competition provided by the EERI Student Leadership Council.

name: Cornell SoLyra JPop Dance Club
description: SoLyra is Cornell’s only Japanese Pop (JPop) dance group. We strive to build a welcoming community where students can explore JPop dance inspired by anime and idol culture, develop performance and production skills, and share their passion through dance covers, media content, and live showcases. Our mission is to celebrate and spread JPop culture across the Cornell campus and the local community, offering all interested members opportunities to participate in regular practices and perform in events throughout the year.

name: Cornell Storm Chaser's Club
description: The purpose of the Cornell Storm Chasers shall be to increase our awareness and knowledge about meteorology outside the classroom, become active participants in the National Weather Service Skywarn program, expand diversity both within and outside of the Department of Atmospheric Science, and offer immediate relief if necessary. name: Cornell Strategy Solutions Club
description: The goal of the club is to make consulting resources available to all Cornell students and draw from the rich and diverse experiences of the student body.

name: Cornell Student Athletes for Sustainability
description: The mission of this organization is to build a strong community of student-athletes who simultaneously develop a sense of awareness and active responsibility surrounding sustainability in athletics and beyond. Through student-led projects, integration of sustainable practices, and acts of community service, we aim to help mitigate climate change and other environmental issues our world faces. The desired result of this organization — widespread attitudinal and behavioral change amongst the athletic community, through efforts by individual players and their teams — will help us reach university

name: Cornell Supper Club
description: A supper club run by students that bring our Cornell community together over incredible food and extraordinary hospitality.

Cornell Technology Consulting Club

name: Cornell Turkish Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of Cornell Turkish Graduate Student Association is to unite Turkish graduate students across disciplines, promote Turkish culture and values, support academic excellence and professional development, and serve as a bridge fostering collaboration, dialogue, and cross-cultural exchange between Türkiye and the Cornell community.

name: Cornell Undergraduate Animal Behavior Club
description: Create a space for students fascinated by how animals think, communicate, and act. Explore the biological, ecological, and evolutionary roots of behavior. Connect students across majors who share a curiosity for animal minds and interactions. Bridge classroom learning with real-world science through research, outreach, and discussion. Build an inclusive, collaborative community that values all taxonomic perspectives- from insects to mammals.

name: Cornell Undergraduate Research Board
description: The Cornell Undergraduate Research Board (CURB) is an organization dedicated to serving the Cornell undergraduate research community throughout the entirety of the process of developing their undergraduate research career. CURB hosts a variety of events throughout the year to help students engage with research through opportunities in getting involved in research, networking with professors, presenting their work, and aiding in the transition to Graduate school.

name: Cornell Undergraduate Research Journal
description: To provide a platform for Cornell undergraduate students to showcase their exemplary scholarly work to the student body and general public, and to offer the student body a wide range of academic perspectives, provoking intellectual pursuits and collaboration.

name: Cornell Undergraduate Research Magazine Club
description: The Cornell Undergraduate Research Magazine (CURM) is a magazine written and published by undergraduates, featuring profiles of student researchers from across the Cornell campus. CURM highlights how Cornell students extend their academic interests beyond the classroom. Regular columns include a look at research by a graduate student, a faculty member, and an alum. The vision of CURM is to provide student researchers with a platform to humanize their research and broadcast it to a general readership.

name: Cornell Undergraduate Sports & Entertainment Law Society Club
description: Foster meaningful dialogue between law students and undergraduates through shared programming and mentorship. Connect students with professionals in sports and entertainment law through speaker events and networking opportunities. Expose members to the breadth of the industry and help them build familiarity with its challenges and career paths. Build a supportive community of students who share an interest in the intersection of law, sports, and entertainment. Provide members with a platform to research, write, and share perspectives on key issues shaping the field.

name: Cornell Undergraduate Turkish Student Association
description: TSA is a student organization that aims to foster the Turkish community at Cornell via several activities, to provide a platform through which we can seek support and guidance, to ask some advice for our daily and academic life, to meet new people, and socialize. In short, the TSA exists to create a community and maximize the joy of the time we have here.

name: Cornell Unicef Chapter
description: The Cornell UNICEF chapter organizes on Cornell campus to advocate for an equitable world for every child. We won't stop upholding the rights of all children and empowering every child everywhere.

name: Cornell United Football Club

Beyond the field, we cherish the bonds that unite us as friends and teammates, creating an inclusive environment where personal growth flourishes. Committed to excellence and sportsmanship, we seek success in every match while understanding the significance of shared experiences. Our love for the beautiful game fuels our drive to improve, pushing us to represent Cornell University at regio

The member groups of CURW sponsor services, social and cultural events, and lectures. Chaplains and spiritual advisors are available to counsel you and your family in times of crisis.

name: Cornell University Class Councils

We aim to prioritize our relationship with other student organizations and use our resources to plan class events, collaborate with other student groups, and establish and execute traditions. The Class Councils shall also strengthen student ties to the University by providing services to Cornell students before and after graduation.

name: Cornell University Parole Initiative Club
description: We strive to foster relationships between people in prison and volunteers as a way to educate the community regarding the inner-workings of the criminal legal system and challenge traditional hierarchies of privilege and power. We also strive to promote relationships that are collaborative, meaningful, and long-lasting, and that are guided by principles of solidarity, self-determination, and love.

description: "Our mission – which drives each of us, every day – is to empower young adults with diabetes by providing access to the peer support, connections, and expert resources they need to thrive." We want to bring this community to Cornell!

name: Cornellians for Life

name: CSalt

The team is comprised of the Aerodynamics and Controls, Mechanical, and Propulsion subteams. Each year the team works to produce an aircraft that meets the unique mission requirements of that year’s competition. The team’s success is predicated upon it’s innovative design approach, use of cutting edge rapid prototyping methods, and the creativity of our dedicated members. name: CU GeoData

name: CU Library
description: Welcome! In a time of rapid change, Cornell University Library continues to stand at the center of intellectual life on campus. With world-class collections and services — print, online, and in person — our Library serves as an indispensable partner in study, teaching and research at the university.

description: The Cuban American Student Association (CASA) is an organization that is dedicated to the discussion of cultural, social, and political issues concerning Cubans in and around the Cornell community and nationwide. It provides academic and emotional support for Cubans at Cornell and educates the Cornell community about issues concerning Cubans.

name: Cycling Club at Cornell
description: Cornell Cycling is a community of cycling enthusiasts across all disciplines. We promote both safe recreational riding as well as support a racing team for our more competitive members.

description: Delta Delta Delta Fraternity, founded in 1888 at Boston University, began as an organization concerned with the growth and development of college women and has evolved into a leader among sororities. The Alpha Beta Chapter was founded at Cornell University in 1913 and celebrates nearly 100 years of history in Ithaca, New York. Beginning with only a handful of members in 1913, the Alpha Beta Chapter now boasts over 130 active collegiate members, as well as a strong alumnae presence. description: Delta Gamma offers to women of all ages a rich heritage based on principles of personal integrity, personal responsibility and intellectual honesty. Its primary purpose is to foster high ideals of friendship, promote educational and cultural interests, create a true sense of social responsibility, and develop the finest qualities of character. Our chapter is made up of over 125 incredibly talented, diverse, and intelligent women, and every unique woman serves as an inspiration to me on a daily basis. name: Delta Kappa Alpha Professional Cinematic Society
description: Delta Kappa Alpha is proud to be the nation's oldest cinema society since 1936. We are a values based organization that strives to provide opportunities for professional growth and leadership development for students of all genders with an affinity for film, television, and entertainment. DKA members benefit from professional development programming, networking, and real-world experience in writing, filming, producing, editing, and more!

name: Delta Kappa Epsilon
description: DKE strives to develop a culture and an expectation of​ undergraduate​ chapters who perform in the top tier of fraternities at their institutions​;​ and a vibrant network of ​alumni who are motivated to stay involved with the fraternity after graduation. We will do this by providing our undergraduates with the leadership​ skills, and the operational resources they need, to excel in today’s Greek environment; and by developing alumni networking programs which are relevant and engaging, and are beneficial to both alumni and undergraduates.

name: Delta Sigma Pi
description: Delta Sigma Pi is a professional fraternity organized to foster the study of business in universities; to encourage scholarship, social activity and the association of students for their mutual advancement by research and practice; to promote closer affiliation between the commercial world and students of commerce, and to further a higher standard of commercial ethics and culture and the civic and commercial welfare of the community.

name: Delta Sigma Theta
description: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated is a public service organization of college educated women committed to the development of its members and uplifting the community. The Magnificent Mu Gamma Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated was charted on May 4, 1975. Our chapter members strive to carry on the legacy of our beautiful founders and the thousands of women who came before us through sisterhood, scholarship and service.

name: Delta Upsilon
description: Delta Upsilon is the premier men's fraternity committed to Building Better Men for a global society through service, leadership development and lifelong personal growth for our diverse membership.

name: Democrats at Cornell University
description: The mission of the Cornell Democrats shall be to actively represent and promote the Democratic Party's interests and ideals within the Cornell community and to foster a community of progressive individuals on the Cornell Campus. The Cornell Democrats shall actively support principles of social, political, and economic justice.

name: Department of Anthropology
description: The Department of Anthropology faculty conduct ethnographic and archaeological as well as biological research that brings hard-won fieldwork to the development of cutting edge social and cultural theories. Our students and faculty work around the globe: from Ithaca, India and Indonesia to the Caribbean and Central America; from Japan, Africa and Nepal to China and the Caucasus; and from the circumpolar North to the Global South.

name: Department of Art
description: At Cornell, the study of art is an education in creating artistic objects, spaces, and experiences that reflect intellectual judgment, philosophical understanding, historical knowledge, and ethical principles that engage and influence the often bewildering complexity of contemporary life within and beyond the academy. Students develop the skills specific to the practice of art in addition to and within the understanding that there are more general skills necessary to a critical apprehension of the collective condition. description: Cornell AAP's Department of City and Regional Planning (CRP) provides a dynamic, rigorous, and supportive context for addressing the most timely planning questions of our time: from social and environmental justice to equity and access to essential services and infrastructures; from climate change adaptation to land use, zoning, and sustainable transportation and housing. Students are challenged to think creatively, critically and historically about the world around them as they identify and interpret the power of image, sound, gesture and movement and cultivate their own artistic and academic voices.

Through a two-year project cycle, our teams identify biomedical challenges, research and develop novel solutions, and design, prototype, and test functional medical devices. name: Digital Tech & Innovation
description: Cornell Digital Tech & Innovation (DTI) makes community impact through technology. We create websites, mobile apps, and community-based initiatives to create positive experiences for people at Cornell and beyond. We foster our personal growth and teach others while always being professional, open-minded, and inclusive.

The organization will help members learn about the different skillsets and careers available within each academic major and professional concentration. Members will also gain the skills necessary to be successful at networking and interviewing to eventually enter the business world as well-rounded and prepared candidate. Overall, the main objective of DLT is to cultivate a community of professional and individual excellence.

These events would often have an educational purpose and could feature guest speakers, workshops, conferences, etc.

Our repertoire includes genres such as traditional Chinese, Asian popular music, film soundtracks, and even East-West fusion. We will expand our impact through outreach, collaboration, and participation in the wider Cornell community as Eco representatives. In doing so, we will act as an environmental hub for campus.

description: Cornell Economics Society strives to provide economics students with the resources necessary to achieve their academic and professional goals. Finally, we seek to encourage students to integrate economics in life and discourse outside of the academic realm.

This creates valuable opportunities for researchers to practice giving technical presentations and to generate new research collaborations. Additional guest speakers from inside or outside Cornell may be invited to speak on technical or non-technical topics of interest to the EDS community. Occasional social events may be organized through EDS but the primary purpose is to generate scholarly discussion of science and engineering.

name: EMBA Consulting Club at Cornell

We aim to cultivate strong professional and personal bonds, inspire each other, and have fun along the way. Join us to build lasting connections, share experiences, and grow both personally and professionally.

name: Emergency Medical Service at Cornell University
description: Cornell University Emergency Medical Service (CUEMS) strives to provide professional, efficient, and effective first-response basic life support care to the Ithaca campus and surrounding areas. Serving Cornell students, faculty, staff, visitors, and their families, CUEMS responds to all 911 calls for medical assistance twenty-four hours a day, seven days per week during the academic year. CUEMS provides extensive, weekly training to all squad members consisting of New York State certified emergency medical technicians. The society can enhance student interaction with the field and cultivate a welcoming and inspiring culture around electronic circuits at Cornell.

name: ENG - Society of Asian Scientists and Engineers at Cornell

By providing these opportunities to our members we aim to create a community where our members have a chance to further their career and strive to build a vibrant community that fosters social, cultural, and professional connections while promoting mutual professional and interpersonal growth and support among our members."

We strive to build strong, long-lasting relationships grounded in mutual respect, cultural understanding, and local empowerment. Through this work, we develop a deeper understanding of global challenges, resource limitations, and the importance of equity and sustainability in engineering.

We serve as a platform for EMBA students to explore and accelerate entrepreneurial ideas, connect with like-minded peers, engage with seasoned founders and investors, and gain the skills and resources needed to launch and grow impactful businesses. name: Expanding Your Horizons at Cornell
description: The primary purpose of Expanding Your Horizons is to organize a day-long conference in the spring semester which will be open to 7-9th grade girls from all over New York state. The goals of the conference are to stimulate the participants' interest in math and science through hands-on activities, to provide them with female scientist role models (who are Cornell University graduate and undergraduate students), and to foster awareness of opportunities in math and science-related careers. The series, typically consisting of three events a year, is an integral component of the composers' experience at Cornell and provides a critical environment for collaborations with professional musicians both inside and outside of Ithaca. Since its inception, the ESSC has been dedicated its efforts to showcasing world premieres by Cornell's emerging composers.

name: Fantastic Fungi Fanatics
description: The Fantastic Fungi Fanatics club creates a platform for people to share their passion for fungi. description: The purpose of the Fantasy & Epics Book Club shall be to form Cornell's only all-fantasy book club that cultivates excitement surrounding fantasy, epics and fairytale. The club will host monthly book discussions as well as reading sessions, PowerPoint nights, trivia, author panels and more. We hope to bring more whimsy and magic to the lives of Cornell students.

name: Field Hockey Club at Cornell
description: We're a competitive and fun club that loves the game of field hockey. We compete in the New York State Club Field Hockey League in the fall and traditionally participate in at least one or two tournaments in the spring.

description: CUFSC supports Cornell's competitive and recreational figure skaters by holding practice sessions and participating in US Figure Skating's (USFS) Collegiate Skating Program. Members are expected to have a basic competency in figure skating, demonstrated by passing USFS tests or taking figure skating PE classes at Cornell. CUFSC also organizes a competition team that travels to intercollegiate events in the surrounding area, including to universities such as MIT and NYU. To benefit the Cornell community, CUFSC hosts public figure skating shows at Lynah Rink each semester that foster a positive

name: Film Club at Cornell
description: We watch, critique, and appreciate films from around the world. Join us every Friday at 7:30 PM in the Schwartz Film Forum for weekly screenings and discussions. No experience is necessary to join!

name: Finance Club at Cornell
description: Since our inception, Cornell Finance Club has been focused on providing our members the skills and connections to navigate the financial services industry. We partner with numerous financial services firms through corporate-sponsored stock pitches as well as club-exclusive networking sessions.

name: First Congregational Church of Ithaca
description: Our mission at FCCI is to Be the church: Protect the environment. Care for the poor. Forgive often. Reject racism. Fight for the powerless. Share earthly and spiritual resources. Embrace diversity. Love God. Enjoy this life!

name: First Generation Student Union
description: The First Gen Student Union aims to promote community, resources, advocacy, and empowerment for all students who identify with the first-generation and/or low-income student experience. We consider you a first-generation college student if you come from a family in which neither of your parents or guardians has obtained a four-year college degree. name: First Love at Cornell
description: To spread the love of Christ to the Cornell University community, fostering Christian fellowships, training leaders, and teaching the Word of God, with commitment and respect to all.

name: First-Generation & Low-Income Student Support
description: Welcome to First-Generation & Low-Income (FGLI) Student Support Center! We promote awareness, identity exploration, community engagement, and self-advocacy for students who identify with the first-generation and/or low-income student experience.

name: Flora Rose House
description: Building community within the west campus housing system.

description: Food & Beverage Society's (FBS) mission is to provide students with a structured and practical educational experience that focuses on the industry application that foundational classes set at Cornell. Additionally, FBS will provide students with the opportunity to network with seasoned alumni, connect with world class faculty at Cornell and contribute to the local community. The Food & Beverage Society will unite students, alumni in industry, and community leaders with a passion for innovation surrounding the food and beverages space.

name: Food Recovery Network at Cornell
description: The Food Recovery Network promotes social welfare and attentive food-use by re-directing extra foodstuffs from Cornell's dining facilities to local food pantries. The focus of our group is to ensure that lower income areas have a dependable supply of nutritious meals. Our organization bridges Cornell and Ithaca providing an opportunity for students and locals to work together in shared commitment to fight hunger and reduce waste.

name: Food Science Club
description: The purpose of Food Science Club shall be to foster a close relationship among the Food Science students and faculty at Cornell University; to encourage leadership and acquaint students with the scope of food science and technology; to spread awareness of food science to the Cornell University and larger Ithaca community; to provide members with opportunities to engage with the professional food industry.

name: Footvolley at Cornell
description: The purpose of Footvolley shall be to play and promote the sport of footvolley through practices and competing in tournaments throughout the United States.

name: Foreign Language Introduction Program
description: The Einaudi Center's Foreign Language Introduction Program, formerly known as the Afterschool Language and Culture Program, has introduced thousands of children in Upstate New York to world languages and cultures. Volunteers from Cornell and surrounding communities who speak world languages provide fun ways for K–12 students to learn about and engage with our increasingly interconnected world.

name: Forte Campus at Cornell
description: Mission: To build a supportive community for Cornell undergraduate women where they can develop personal and professional skills through education, mentorship, and networking resources. Core Values: We value empowering women to pursue their diverse interests and foster new relationships through learning in every facet of life, whether it be personal or professional. We strive to create a supportive, open-minded, intimate community of motivated women, who are inspired to give back to the organization.

name: Free Space Dance
description: Free Space Dance Club is a vibrant, inclusive community of over 300 graduate and undergraduate students at Cornell University who share a passion for dance. We provide workshops in hip hop, jazz, and K-pop that welcome dancers of all levels — from complete beginners to experienced performers. Our mission is to create a supportive environment where members can explore movement, improve their skills, stay active, and connect with others through the joy of dance.

name: Friends of Farmworkers
description: Friends of Farmworkers was founded to provide consistent ESL instruction to area farmworkers who know little or no English.

name: FSAE Racing at Cornell
description: The purpose of Cornell Racing FSAE shall be to design, manufacture and compete a vehicle according to the rules and regulations of the Formula SAE competition.

name: Future Civilizations Society
description: We seek to envision the world that will follow the age of automation before it arrives. We aim to create an interdisciplinary community at Cornell where engineers, designers, social scientists, and artists collaborate to imagine the next evolution of civilization: cities that are intelligent, equitable, and deeply human in the age of autonomy.

name: Gaming at Cornell
description: The purpose of Gaming at Cornell shall be to promote all forms of gaming for members of Cornell. These forms of gaming can include game design, esports, casual video games, board games, and other categories up to the discretion of the eboard.

name: GEEKS - Grads Employing Empathy, Knowledge, & Service
description: The reasons that this organization was formed include the following: A. To allow CU graduate students the opportunity to serve the community B. name: Gender Equity Resource Center
description: The mission of the Gender Equity Resource Center (GenEq) is to foster a more vibrant campus community by supporting the full and active participation of women and gender expansive students in both their personal and educational pursuits at Cornell. The Center champions endeavors that support women's education, empowerment, and advancement at Cornell and beyond. GenEq strives to be a welcoming space for people of all genders and identities. name: Gender Justice Advocacy Coalition
description: The Gender Justice Advocacy Coalition (GJAC) is a byline-funded student organization committed to justice and advocacy for all genders. We operate out of an intersectional and global lens with a focus on gender-marginalized folks. We aim to encourage meaningful and critical conversations related to the gendered lived experiences of all people. We seek to foster relationships with campus partners in order to support and amplify the work of Cornell social justice organizations through funding, awareness-raising, and advocacy.

name: Generative AI at Cornell
description: Our mission is to lead the exploration and innovation of generative AI and large language models (LLMs) at Cornell, with a focus on transforming the educational landscape. We envision building an inclusive and forward-thinking community where students collaborate to integrate these advanced AI technologies into educational tools, enhancing learning experiences and accessibility. By engaging in cutting-edge AI projects, we aim to apply generative AI and LLMs in practical, real-world educational settings, while fostering a culture of mentorship, continuous learning, and shared knowledge.

name: Genetics, Genomics, & Development Graduate Student Association
description: GGD GSA serves to enrich the academic and social environment for the graduate students in the Field of Genetics, Genomics, and Development in the department of Molecular Biology and Genetics.

name: Georgian Students Society
description: The mission of the Georgian Students Society shall be to bring together Georgian students at Cornell University to share and celebrate Georgian culture, foster a sense of belonging, and promote cross-cultural understanding through educational and social initiatives.

name: German Studies
description: German Studies at Cornell enables students to develop the linguistic, literary, and cultural competency required of world citizens in the twenty-first century. The interdisciplinary and cross-cultural orientation of our curriculum is designed to fulfill the needs of our diverse student population. We encourage students to choose from the broad range of courses we offer in collaboration with other units such as Government, Philosophy, History, Comparative Literature, Jewish Studies, and Performing and Media Arts. description: Ghanaians at Cornell is a cultural community that strives to share the Ghanaian culture with the Cornell and Ithaca communities. We provide a home away from home. We are a small Ghana.

description: Gift of Life Cornell University raises awareness for the bone marrow donation process. In collaboration with the Gift of Life, one of the nation's public bone marrow and blood stem cell┬áregistries, Gift of Life Cornell University organizes events, campaigns, trainings, and seminars to register new potential donors, raise monetary funds, and educate the community about the bone marrow donation process. Gift of Life Cornell University is dedicated to expanding the bone marrow registry and supporting those who have been affected by the cancer experience.

name: Glee Club, Cornell University
description: The oldest student run organization on Cornell's campus, the Glee Club strives to bring choral music to the world through performances on and off campus. Rehearsals are held twice a week in Sage Chapel. Notable events include a winter tour (both national and international), and the Homecoming concert as well as collaborations with orchestras for the presentation of major works. The Glee Club also serves as the torch bearers of the traditional Cornell Songs.

We are a family of highly-motivated students that is part of a global collegiate network of over 60 chapters dedicated to foster deep and trusting personal relationships both with our current members and accomplished alumni.

name: Global Cornell
description: Global Cornell is a community of belonging with a border-crossing spirit of exploration, learning, and shared discovery. Our internationally engaged units foster high-impact international research and collaborations, teach and mentor the next generation of global citizens, and support international experiences and cultural exchange for all Cornellians. Together, we make a world of difference. Global Cornell includes the Mario Einaudi Center for International Studies, Education Abroad, and International Services.

name: Global Development Student Advisory Board
description: The mission of the Global Development Student Advisory Board is to build a community of students who possess a passion for uniting critical scholarship and practice at the intersections of agricultural, environmental, life, and social sciences, to advance a more equitable, sustainable, and food-secure world for all. Side-by-side with our diverse network of global and community partners, we demonstrate our commitment to inclusion, innovation, and furthering the study and practice of global development. We embrace a transdisciplinary approach that emphasizes real-world engagement on a global sca

description: The Global Health Student Advisory Board (GHSAB) is a student-led board that works in collaboration with the DNS Global Health Program. The GHSAB develops and improves global and public health programming that engages students, faculty, staff, and alumni across the university. Through our unequivocal passion for global and public health, we aim to increase awareness of global and public health issues while promoting health equity, diversity, and inclusion. As a diverse group of students—representing different races, ethnicities, geographies, genders, majors, and professional aspirations—we all

name: Global Impact at Cornell
description: Global Impact at Cornell (GIC) is a student-led organization dedicated to advancing health equity through direct service, education, and global partnerships. GIC connects Cornell students with meaningful, hands-on opportunities to support underserved communities both locally and internationally, focusing on sustainable solutions in public health, clean water access, and renewable energy. By collaborating with established nonprofit partners and engaging students in service-based learning, GIC fosters cultural humility, social responsibility, and leadership rooted in compassion and action.

name: Global Medical Missions Alliance
description: Global Medical Missions Alliance (GMMA) is a Christian organization that mobilizes and networks mission-minded healthcare professionals to serve as mentors to the next generation of healthcare professionals on medical mission trips.

Our consultants are top students from Cornell University, trained specifically to understand how to tackle nonprofits’ and social impact organizations’ biggest challenges.

We want to support graduate students in balancing academic and personal lives by providing a space where they can relax their minds and expand and reevaluate their mindset towards life's circumstances. This organization is a registered student organization of Cornell University.

In addition to representing the students in matters of university governance, the GPSA has the responsibility for setting and administering the Student Activity Fee for graduate and professional students. GAL is open to graduate and professional students from all backgrounds who support this mission.

As such, we are committed to building unity with everyone on the Cornell campus who are committed to improving the culture of the academy.

Our organization also aims to advocate for affordable homeownership, aligning with Habitat's overarching mission.

We hope to represent Cornell's finest when we perform on campus and strive to be ambassadors of music to Cornell as we travel around the world.

description: Hans Bethe House is the third of five residential colleges built at Cornell in the first decade of the 21st century comprising the university's West Campus House System. It opened in the fall of 2007. The House accommodates 280 sophomores and 100 juniors and seniors in a faculty-led, student-governed residential community. The name honors long-time and beloved Cornell faculty member Hans A. Bethe.

Through education, outreach, and service, we promote understanding and the development of inclusive communities. name: Hawaii Club at Cornell
description: The Cornell Hawai'i Club is a cultural/social organization whose purpose is two-fold. First, we are here to welcome new and current students from Hawai'i and provide them with a network of other Hawai'i students in the Cornell and Ithaca areas. Second, we share the Hawaiian culture with the Cornell and Ithaca communities. The Hawai'i club completes these tasks through various events: spam musubi making nights, BBQ's, winter clothes shopping trips, and in the spring we put on a Lū'au! Johnson Museum of Art welcomes visitors to experience original works of art across a wide spectrum of global traditions, time periods, and media for education, inspiration, and delight. Additionally, we aim to spread awareness and information about reptiles, amphibians, and conservation through outreach events with local communities.

The club's main focus is in the German Longsword tradition, however, we are open to studying other weaponry and styles based on member interest. Therefore, a large portion of club activity will be dedicated to safety training and conditioning, and sparring will be done with feders (plastic swords).
