name: History of Art and Visual Studies Association HAVSA
description: The purpose of History of Art and Visual Studies Association shall be to provide graduate students enrolled in Cornell’s department of History of Art & Visual Studies PhD program with a forum for discussing department business, upcoming events, and scholarly interests relating to the field of art and visual studies. This organization will also provide an opportunity for graduate students in the department to organize events and collaborate on papers, exhibitions, and conference papers/panels.

name: History of Art Club
description: HART Club seeks to cultivate an understanding of art history as a field and career among Cornellians and work to foster a deeper appreciation for art, artists, and art historians by providing the community with opportunities to engage directly with art and art history.

name: Homelessness Action Project at Cornell
description: Homelessness Action Project at Cornell is a registered student organization committed to supporting local nonprofits and efforts that uphold the dignity and rights of individuals experiencing homelessness.

name: Hong Kong Student Association
description: To promote awareness and passion of Hong Kong culture through the organization of culturally related events.

name: Hopelessly Yellow at Cornell
description: Founded at the University of Michigan in 2021, Hopelessly Yellow is a digital brand promoting mental wellness and positivity through writing, design, music, and media. Now at Cornell University, Hopelessly Yellow strives to foster a passionate community for all. More than just a club, Hopelessly Yellow embodies a blissful feeling, a fresh mindset, and a golden lifestyle.

name: Hortus Forum - Undergraduate Horticulture Club
description: Cultivating a positive social community which fosters a passion for plants and teaches the value of horticulture. Hortus Forum has a key role in providing educational experiences beyond the classroom and teaching the Cornell community about plants. This includes but is not limited to: field trips, presentations and workshops, promotion of internships, career development opportunities, and social events. Plant sales are a necessary function of the organization; they are a means of generating revenue, and are utilized as learning opportunities and outreach. Although plant sales primarily encompa

name: HOSA - Future Health Professionals - Cornell Chapter
description: To empower HOSA-Future Health Professionals to become leaders in the global health community, through education, collaboration, and experience.

name: Hospicare & Palliative Care Services
description: Our mission is to bring medical expertise and compassionate, respectful care to people and their loved ones at any stage of a life-threatening illness, and to provide information and education about advanced illness, dying, and bereavement to the entire community.

name: Hospitality Asset Managers Association, Cornell University Student Chapter
description: The Hospitality Asset Managers Association Club at Cornell University aims to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry practice in hospitality asset management. Our purpose is to enrich our members' understanding and capabilities through engaging educational programs, guest lectures from industry leaders, and hands-on opportunities. We strive to cultivate a community of aspiring professionals equipped with the knowledge and skills to excel in the dynamic field of hospitality asset management.

name: Hotel Ezra Cornell
description: Hotel Ezra Cornell (HEC) is a weekend-long business conference organized and executed by the students of the School of Hotel Administration. The conference boasts a series of educational seminars, food and beverage events, and leisure activities to generate thought-provoking conversation about the industry and build long-term relationships between current and future hospitality professionals. A 102-year-old tradition of the school, HEC allows students to practice the skills they have learned in the classroom and showcase their talents to industry leaders, supporting the program's mission of "S

name: Hotel Graduate Student Organization
description: Our mission is to serve and benefit students in the Master of Management in Hospitality at Cornell University, and the entire graduate and professional student body at Cornell University.

name: Hotel Sales and Marketing Association International Cornell Chapter
description: HSMAI operates as part of a greater international organization, boasting memebrs from numerous universities and companies around the globe.

name: Hotel School Diversity and Inclusion Office
description: The Hotel School Diversity Enhancement Committee advises the school on student, staff and faculty diversity issues and fosters understanding of the connection between diversity and the creation of an inclusive environment that allows for success in composition, engagement, inclusion and achievement.

name: Hotel Society, Collegiate Chapter
description: The Cornell Hotel Society, Collegiate Chapter (CHS,CC) is dedicated to supporting the Nolan Hotel School students and their interests through the promotion of active involvement in student organizations by coordinating school wide events and networking opportunities with our alumni. All students of the Nolan Hotel School, graduate and undergraduate, attain membership upon matriculation. CHS, CC works closely with the Cornell Hotel Society (CHS) Global Chapter to maintain the connection between the alumni and the students at the Nolan Hotel School.

name: Human Centered Design Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of this organization is to foster community among graduate DEA students and to set up events which would be beneficial academically and professionally.

name: Humanities Scholars Program
description: Supporting independent undergraduate research in the humanities.

name: Humor Us! Sketch Comedy
description: Humor Us! is a sketch comedy group at Cornell. We put on shows throughout the semester similar to episodes of Saturday Night Live. In fact, we are often confused with the cast of Saturday Night Live, so for future reference, we are the better looking ones. Members of Humor Us write, produce and act out all of our own material, and we love to share it with the Cornell community. Meet the group and watch some of our past shows at http://www.humoruscomedy.com.

name: Hunter R. Rawlings III Cornell Presidential Research Scholars
description: The Hunter R. Rawlings III Cornell Presidential Research Scholars (RCPRS) Program provides highly motivated undergraduate students with the opportunity to engage in sustained, faculty-mentored research throughout their undergraduate careers. Open to students from all Cornell colleges and across every discipline—including the humanities, social sciences, physical and biological sciences, engineering, and the arts—the program supports students in pursuing their intellectual interests through original research in close collaboration with faculty and other mentors. Each year, the program supports

name: Hydroponics at Cornell
description: Cornell Hydroponics aims to bring together students with a passion for advancing agricultural technology through the use of hydroponics - growing crops in nutrient rich solution without soil.

name: iGEM at Cornell
description: Cornell Genetically Engineered Machines (iGEM) is an award-winning synthetic biology research team comprised of over 50 undergraduate students in five subteams: Wet Lab, Product Development, Policy and Practices, Business, and Wiki/Design. Using techniques in genetic engineering, the team develops projects that address local and global problems related to medical applications, environmental concerns, and human and animal health. Each year, the team competes with over 450 multidisciplinary teams from all around the world at the iGEM Grand Jamboree, currently hosted in Paris, France, hosted by t

name: Ignite
description: The purpose of Ignite is to give people who identify and do not identify as Christian to give space to seek the meaning and theological basis of Christianity from a non-denominational and ecumenical lens. We strongly believe that the best way to learn about Christianity is to actively participate in the customs and traditions performed. This will be well accomplished through a service.

name: Illuminations
description: Illuminations is Cornell's co-ed undergraduate Chinese dance troupe dedicated to sharing Chinese culture by teaching and performing various styles of dance and original choreography. Illuminations performs numerous times throughout the year at a range of cultural events, culminating in an annual showcase during the spring semester.

name: ILR Black Student Union
description: The ILR Black Student Union (ILR BSU) strives to foster solidarity between Black ILRies by providing a sense of community, academic resources, and a lifelong support network for all things work. The founding members have set a vision to enrich Black ILRies and the wider community through Black intellect and perspectives. We collectively stand against the injustices that Black workers face and are equally committed to advancing the initiatives and philosophy of all Black students in ILR.

name: ILR Graduate Student Association
description: The ILR Graduate Student Association at Cornell University’s School of Industrial and Labor Relations (ILR GSA) is dedicated to fostering an inclusive and supportive environment for ILR graduate students while aligning with the overarching missions of ILR and Cornell University. As members of the 2024 GSA board, we are committed to building our community through student advocacy, transparent communication, and opportunities to form meaningful connections within the ILR graduate community.

name: ILR International Graduate Student Association
description: The ILR IGSA is instituted to contribute to developmental needs of the international community of graduate students at the ILR School.

name: ILR Office of Career Services
description: The ILR Office of Career Services strives to engage undergraduate and graduate students in career exploration, development, and mapping future career goals.

name: ILR Office of Engaged and Experiential Programs
description: Our office serves as a hub for engaged and experiential learning and research opportunities offered at the ILR School and seeks to create new engaged experiences for ILR students.

name: ILR Student Government Association
description: To actively and aggressively represent the undergraduate population of the ILR School and Cornell University through education, programming, and any activities that will enhance the educational circumstances of the ILR School.

name: ILR Women's Caucus
description: The purpose of the ILR Women's Caucus (ILRWC) is to work towards gender equality through open dialogues, professional development, and philanthropy and advocacy initiatives.

name: Impact Dance Troupe
description: Impact Dance Troupe is Cornell University's oldest dance troupe offering choreography and performance opportunities in ballet, modern, jazz, contemporary, hip-hop, tap, and more! Each semester, members perform original choreography in Impact shows as well as a variety of benefit shows in collaboration with other campus organizations. We are one of the only groups to have no dues, fees, or costs, and are an equal opportunity, student-run group.

name: Impact Investing at Cornell
description: Impact Investing at Cornell's mission is to provide a platform for undergraduate students to gain tangible experiences and insight into the impact investing field from the private equity scope. We aim to develop a network of future leaders in this sector through our Associate Development Program (ADP), events, and consulting project partnerships with established impact funds.

name: Impact Week at Cornell
description: The purpose of Belonging@Cornell 360 is to further demonstrate our commitment to creating a cultural environment that respects and celebrates diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging throughout the academic year. Collaborating with collegiate partners, we host a series of thematic monthly events that will: 1) Raise awareness of diversity, equity, inclusion, belonging, and justice issues within academia and industry. 2) Support the development, engagement, and empowerment of faculty, staff, and students. 3) Provide opportunities to share best practices and models of excellence among collegia

name: In Transcription Club at Cornell
description: As the first step of gene expression, DNA is transcribed into mRNA. Having a similar goal, InT wants to become the transcription step that helps transform our community members into future leaders such as scientists, entrepreneurs, or investors that change the world with life science.

name: Independent Freedom Caucus
description: The purpose of the Independent Freedom Caucus shall be to promote and encourage conservative intellectualism and social cohesion. The Caucus provides a home for undergraduate conservative leaders and thinkers to earnestly seek truth through rigorous debate and lively social programming.

name: India Association at Cornell University
description: We aim to foster an environment of comfort and camaraderie among International students in Cornell's Graduate and Professional schools, with a focus on students of Indian origin. Also, we strive to spread awareness and celebrate Indian culture in all its vivid glory.

name: Indigenous Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of the Indigenous Graduate Student Association shall be to foster community building among Indigenous graduate and professional students and allies. Further, the organization seeks to enhance personal, academic, and professional growth and development in a stable, community-based, peaceful environment, and to serve as a conduit for graduate and professional student issues and concerns, contributing to improving the experience of Indigenous students in graduate and professional education. name: Indonesian Association at Cornell
description: The Indonesian Association at Cornell aims to serve as a second home for the Indonesian community at Cornell University.

name: Indoor Drumline at Cornell University
description: The Cornell University Indoor Drumline aims to rehearse and perform a full-length indoor percussion show for several competitions within the New York State Percussion Circuit (NYSPC) during the course of the Spring semester.

name: Information Science Graduate Student Association
description: The ISGSA promotes professionalization and socialization for graduate students in the department of Information Science.

name: Information Science Student Association - Cornell University
description: As the Information Science Student Association (ISSA) we are open to all students (majors, minors, or undeclared) interested in Information Science or Information Science, Systems, & Technology. The Information Science Student Association is here to improve the student experience and spread the word about our fast-growing and cutting-edge major. Our club plans networking events, social events, corporate information sessions, and meet-and-greets with Cornell faculty.

name: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
description: IEEE at Cornell seeks to support undergraduate students interested in Electrical & Computer Engineering with high quality career, academic, and social programming.

name: Intellectual Property and Ethics Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of the Cornell Intellectual Property and Ethics Club (referred to hereafter as "CIPEC") shall be to provide students of Cornell University with an opportunity to learn about and engage with the complexities of Intellectual Property and the ethics associated with it. This engagement will be bolstered through research, debates, discussions, and presentations by club members and guest speakers.

name: Interdisciplinary Psychology Club at Cornell
description: Fostering and promoting an open, interdisciplinary platform for the science and application of psychology

name: Interfaith Council at Cornell
description: The Cornell Interfaith Council seeks to promote interfaith dialogue and support religious life on campus, while encouraging shared understanding and celebration of our differences.

name: Interfraternity Council
description: The self-governing body for the 33 recognized Interfraternity Council fraternities at Cornell. Creates policies, oversees the judicial process, and plans programming and initiatives for the community. Has a 9 person elected IFC Exec Board.

name: International Affairs Review at Cornell
description: The Cornell International Affairs Review is a student-run publication at Cornell University dedicated to publishing papers that contribute to our collective understanding of contemporary international affairs.

name: International Affairs Society at Cornell
description: The Cornell International Affairs Society (CIAS) is Cornell's primary international relations club and official Model United Nations team. Its mission is to cultivate within students an enhanced understanding of international affairs while developing essential skills in public speaking, leadership, rhetoric and diplomacy.

name: International Business Association at Cornell
description: The purpose of the International Business Association at Cornell shall be to promote an awareness of global business, foster a network of those with a common interest in international business, and provide support to those in the Cornell University community who are exploring international careers.

name: International Graduate and Professional Students Organization
description: The mission of International Graduate and Professional Students is to bring together international graduate and professional students of Cornell University in a community where they can connect, belong, and thrive.

name: International Interior Design Association Cornell Campus Chapter
description: The purpose of IIDA Cornell University Campus Center shall be to serve as a pre-professional, event-based organization for students interested in careers in commercial interior design and architecture. In alignment with IIDA’s mission to provide meaningful resources to designers, we aim to foster a community that helps students advance their profession and connect education with practice.

name: International Students Association
description: The recently rechristened International Students Association (ISA), previously the International Students Union (ISU) and International Students Board (ISB) is an organization of students from a diverse background committed to promoting dialogue and awareness about world events, cultures and issues. We fulfill this goal through the ISA's original events and the funding of student organizations, as well as assisting in the planning and execution of their events. description: The Cornell Investment Banking Club (CIBC) is a student-run club at Cornell University with a core focus on preparing members to secure jobs within the financial industry, with a specific focus on recruitment in investment banking, through leadership opportunities, industry exposure and education.

name: Iranian Graduate Students
description: The purpose of IGS shall be to serve as a substrate for social, academic, and cultural interactions between current and prospective Iranian graduate students, and the Cornell community at large.

name: Jamaican Students' Association at Cornell University
description: The Jamaican Students’ Association at Cornell University aims to foster a vibrant and inclusive community that celebrates the rich cultural heritage of Jamaica. For students from Jamaica and those with an interest in Jamaican culture, we strive to establish a welcoming and empowering environment. We will work to foster unity, diversity, and awareness on campus through cultural events, educational programs, and community outreach. Promote interaction amongst Cornell students of all background through the promotion of the aforementioned topics 3. Offer support and resources for the Japanese, Japanese - American, and Japanese interest community at Cornell University

name: JazzPlus
description: JazzPlus encourages its members to carry on the deeply rooted histories and traditions of jazz, while simultaneously augmenting them through inspiration from other genres. While many members of the organization participate in department jazz ensembles, JazzPlus is open to everyone. JazzPlus presents workshops and clinics to musicians and listeners of the Cornell and Ithaca communities. Topics of discussion may include but are not limited to: jazz style, technique, composition, fundamentals, improvisation, history, culture, and performance. name: Jewish Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of the Jewish Graduate Student Association shall be to provide Jewish Cornell graduate and professional students in all programs and degree paths (and their friends and partners) and Jewish young professionals in the Ithaca area with community, social events, and a network for support and resources.

name: Jewish Voices for Peace at Cornell
description: Jewish Voice for Peace is the largest progressive Jewish anti-Zionist organization in the world. We’re organizing a grassroots, multiracial, cross-class, intergenerational movement of U.S. Jews into solidarity with the Palestinian freedom struggle, guided by a vision of justice, equality, and dignity for all people.

name: JGSM - Access Johnson
description: Access Johnson is the club for accessibility, accommodations, and advocacy at Johnson.

name: JGSM - Adam Smith Society at Cornell Johnson
description: The Adam Smith Society is a nationwide, chapter-based association of MBA students and business leaders who work to promote on-campus debate and discussion about the moral, social, and economic benefits of capitalism.

name: JGSM - Asian Affinity Business Association
description: There is a growing need to create a stronger and more inclusive community for those of Asian heritage among prospective students, current students, alumni, partners, faculty, and staff at the SC Johnson School of Business. We hope to foster a community at Johnson that builds relationships among current Asian Affinity Business Association members, provides professional support and mentorship, and promotes greater awareness and allyship of the Asian heritage across the general Johnson community.

name: JGSM - Associate Real Estate Council
description: AREC is Cornell's graduate student-run real estate organization. It is committed to enhancing Cornell's presence in the industry and providing its members with educational and career development opportunities. AREC membership should be viewed as a stepping stone to lifetime involvement in real estate as a Cornellian, including membership in the Cornell Real Estate Council.

name: JGSM - Association of Veterans
description: To recruit high potential US and Non-US military veterans into the Johnson School, and assist with their success in transitioning to the classroom and into their desired career.

name: JGSM - Black Graduate Business Association
description: The Black Graduate Business Association (BGBA) at Johnson is dedicated to the recruitment and support of students of African descent. Additionally, the organization is committed to the professional, academic, and social development of its membership. Members of the BGBA have the unique opportunity to initiate and execute key events in the Johnson community, interact with corporations on an individual basis, and coordinate with faculty, staff, alumni, and students in programs that shape our community.

name: JGSM - BR Tech Strategy
description: At BR Tech Strategy, we envision creating a dynamic platform where MBA students collaborate with Cornell inventors and early-stage startups to unlock the commercial potential of innovative, university-generated technologies. Through strategic partnerships with Cornell’s engineering school, we aim to bridge the gap between academia and real-world business application, empowering MBA students to apply their core skills in meaningful, hands-on consulting projects. name: JGSM - Canadian Business Club
description: We are an organization representing Canadians interested in careers in business, and allow them to network and connect with one another.

description: Community Impact serves as a platform for the Johnson community to engage and give back to the local Ithaca community through volunteering, fundraising, and learning from the relationships among the for-profit, non-profit, and public sectors, and promoting socially responsible business.

name: JGSM - Cornell Energy Club
description: The Cornell Energy Club is a student-led club that connects Cornell graduate students pursuing careers in the energy industry. We are united in our motivation to drive change and tackle the most challenging problems facing the energy industry.

name: JGSM - Corporate Leadership Club
description: The Corporate Leadership Club is a valuable resource for Johnson MBA students pursuing careers in Marketing, General Management, and Corporate Finance. CLC's goal is to equip its members with the skill set to become better educated and prepared for corporate internship and full time recruiting. Through active involvement from all members, CLC maintains high visibility at Johnson, as well as with corporations, recruiters, alumni, and related MBA communities. name: JGSM - EMBA New York City Program
JGSM - ETA Club at Cornell
description: To inform about the search fund asset class, to serve as a meeting platform for Cornellians interested in entrepreneurship through acquisition (ETA), and to connect current students, alumni, the investor community, and other interested parties

name: JGSM - European Club
description: The European Club supports European Students at the Johnson School and students of all nationalities with an interest in Europe through Campus Activities and Career Support.

name: JGSM - Family Business Club
description: The Johnson Family Business Club serves as a forum for students with an interest in privately held corporations. This club works with local family businesses to generate meaningful connections and opportunities to prepare for working within, leading, and passing on a family-owned enterprise over the course of time. This club is for any student who has a business in their family, regardless of the size, industry, or the student's personal experience within it. Additionally, students planning to start a family business in the future or who are interested in working for family businesses in consu

name: JGSM - Greater China Business Club
description: The Greater China Business Club (GCBC) at Johnson is a student organization that brings together members in the Cornell Johnson community sharing or interested in Chinese culture. Johnson GCBC is committed to encouraging culture sharing, supporting its members to navigate the MBA program, and providing a networking platform.

description: The Cornell MBA High Tech Club serves as a platform for professional development and personal growth, providing students with critical tools, and a network of professional support to engage confidently with the technology sector. We cultivate a culture of tech-forward curiosity where students can explore the breadth and depth of tech careers, and receive structured guidance and resources to succeed in recruiting for roles across the tech landscape.

description: The purpose of Hindu Business Society shall be to create a safe space for Hindu students of the SC Johnson College of Business at Cornell University where members can embrace and express their Hindu identity, learn about the Hindu religion and Hindu culture, share their life experiences, and apply learnings in their personal and professional lives. description: To Hispanic American MBA students at Johnson, HABLA is the organization that helps recruit high potential Hispanic candidates and corporate sponsorship, supports our 1st and 2nd year students with mentoring, leadership, speaker events, and empowers Hispanic students through leadership training to develop into thoughtful leaders that will make positive changes in their communities.

name: JGSM - Hospitality Business Club
description: To facilitate career development opportunities, enhance industry knowledge, and encourage camaraderie among hospitality industry-focused Johnson students, alumni, and the Cornell community.

name: JGSM - Human Capital Association
description: The Human Capital Association provides a forum for students, faculty and corporate executives to explore the various dimensions of human resource issues prevalent in global business. HCA aims to be a provider of educational and professional development with compelling speakers, workshops and symposiums. HCA promotes collaboration with the Center for Advanced Human Resource Studies (CAHRS), and the Society of Human Resource Management (SHRM) at the ILR School, as well as the Consulting Club and the Center for Leadership at Johnson. The group's values are respect, inclusiveness, passion, integri

name: JGSM - Investment Management Club
description: The Investment Management Club (IMC) aims to help Johnson students who are interested in pursuing a career in investment management (buy-side, sell-side, private wealth management) and related fields recruit for internship and full-time roles through coordinated efforts with the CMC, CWGs, and weekly meetings organized to provide skill-based programming.

name: JGSM - JD-MBA Society
description: The purpose of the Society shall be to promote Cornell's JD-MBA Program, foster communication among its members, plan social gatherings, and strengthen ties between JD-MBA students and alumni.

name: JGSM - Jewish Business Association
description: The Jewish Business Association connects Jewish and allied Cornell MBA students with alumni across business, building relationships that continue after graduation. We host dinners, speaker series, and career-focused events that bring students and alumni together around shared Jewish identity.

name: JGSM - Johnson Africa Business Society
description: The Johnson Africa Business Society (JABS) is an organization that serves as a professional and cultural incubator for Cornellians who have a strong interest in business opportunities in Africa.

name: JGSM - Johnson Christian Fellowship
description: The purpose of the Johnson Christian Fellowship is to honor and glorify Jesus Christ, and to love and support each other and our Johnson classmates spiritually, socially, and emotionally.

name: JGSM - Johnson Consulting Club
description: The Consulting Club is a student-run organization, with one of our consultants in residence as an advisor. It is one of the largest professional clubs at Johnson. The Club's mission is twofold: to assist our members in pursuing careers in consulting and to develop and nurture relationships with top consulting firms.

name: JGSM - Johnson Cornell F1 Club

name: JGSM - Johnson Cornell Tech MBA Program
JGSM - Johnson Crew
description: At Johnson Crew, our mission is to foster a vibrant community of MBA students united by a passion for rowing.

name: JGSM - Johnson FC
description: To provide a community for Cornell graduate school students to play, watch, and follow soccer together.

name: JGSM - Johnson Food and Agriculture Club
description: Johnson Food, Beverage, and Agribusiness Club provides a space to educate the Johnson community on trends in the food, beverage, and agriculture industries. The club organizes cross-cultural and educational events to share the importance of food, beverage, and agriculture is for society and culture. JFBA is open to Johnson students and the Cornell graduate community.

name: JGSM - Johnson Gaming Club
description: The Johnson Gaming Club brings classmates together through video games and board games, creating a space to have fun, meet people, and build community! The club also offers an opportunity to learn more about the video game industry and connect with others who share an interest in gaming.

description: The Johnson - Golf Club's mission is to promote the game of golf in the Johnson community through friendly competition and member education. The Johnson Golf Club was created to facilitate student learning and mastery of the game of golf. In addition, golf will be used as a networking tool to promote interaction among students, faculty, alumni, and recruiters.

name: JGSM - Johnson Healthcare Club

name: JGSM - Johnson Ice Hockey Club

description: The MBA Student Council proactively works to improve the Johnson School by providing direction and implementing change. The committee consists of 1b elected students. The SC seeks input from students, faculty and staff on both strategic and tactical issues facing the school, focusing on strategic issues. Strategic areas range from alumni development to branding of the school to long term planning. Tactical areas range from curriculum requirements to food service to social events. The SC meets weekly with deans and other key faculty and staff members.

name: JGSM - Johnson MPS Student Council
description: To build lifelong relationships within the MPS programs, to help MPS students improve professional networks and to improve alumni relations

name: JGSM - Johnson on Tap
description: Johnson on Tap brings the Cornell Johnson community together through a shared appreciation of beer. Our mission is to create welcoming, social experiences that strengthen bonds among students, alumni, and partners, while fostering curiosity about traditions and cultures around the world.

name: JGSM - Johnson Out For Business
description: Out for Business Mission Statement: Out For Business (O4B) is the business club for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ+) Cornell Johnson students, their partners, and active allies. As future business leaders, we are committed to building a safe and welcoming environment for all students to be their full authentic selves. We strive to promote equality, diversity, and acceptance through education, advocacy, and social events. Our goal is to empower and support LGBTQ+ students in their personal and professional growth, and to foster an environment where everyone feels valued,

name: JGSM - Johnson Outdoor Ventures Club
description: The Outdoor Ventures Club provides an opportunity for the Johnson community to take advantage of the numerous outdoor activities in Ithaca and the surrounding areas.

name: JGSM - Johnson Poker Club
description: The purpose of Johnson Poker Club is to provide a platform for poker enthusiasts to come together for poker nights, and to provide an opportunity to learn poker, foster camaraderie within the Johnson community and participate in poker tournaments.

name: JGSM - Johnson School Student Services
description: This is the Student Services Office for the Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management in the Cornell SC Johnson College of Business.

name: JGSM - Johnson Ski & Snowboard Club
description: The Ski Club provides that much needed escape from the rigors of business school and fosters a strong community of skiiers and boarders.

name: JGSM - Johnson Southeast Asian Club
description: SEAC aims to celebrate the cultures of countries across Southeast Asian region (Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar/Burma, and Brunei). We do that through community events and career support.

name: JGSM - Johnson Tennis Club
description: To provide a platform for students of the Johnson Graduate School of Management and other graduate students on campus to engage in recreational tennis.

name: JGSM - Johnson Wine and Spirits Club
description: Johnson Wine & Spirits is designed to promote wine and spirit education and appreciation through lectures, tastings, speakers and various other events.

name: JGSM - Korean Business Association
description: 1) Strengthen Cornell Johnson MBA presence in Korean MBA society 2) Increase awareness and understanding of Korean culture throughout the Johnson community 3) Strengthen the Johnson School brand in Korea 4) Foster and maintain a network of Johnson School alumni throughout Korea

name: JGSM - Latin American Business Association
description: The combined countries of the Latin American region have a population of more than 585 million people and an aggregate GDP of more than $5.5 trillion USD, representing more than 7% of the world's economy. The Latin American Business Association is the official organization for Latin American students studying at Johnson.

The mission of the club is to prepare members to succeed in recruiting for finance positions across a variety of industries.

description: Joining the South Asian Business Club allows students with an interest in the region to network with prominent South Asians in the United States and abroad, express themselves through cultural events, as well as feel at home in Ithaca when families and friends are thousands of miles away. With an increasing number of students who can trace their roots to the region, this club was started to serve as a platform for representing the interests of the students; with career services, alumni, and other student clubs. South Asia includes the following countries: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sr

name: JGSM - Sustainable Global Enterprise
description: To empower future leaders to integrate social and environmental sustainability into business and to advance the professional development of Johnson students interested in sustainability-related careers by providing the Johnson community with forums for networking and education.

name: JGSM - VC@Johnson
description: VC@Johnson is the gateway to the venture capital world at Cornell's SC Johnson Graduate School of Management. Our goal is simple: to build a community where Johnson students and industry professionals can connect, learn, and innovate in the venture capital sector. We plan to be the go-to hub for venture capital insights and networking at Johnson.

name: JGSM - Women's Management Council
description: The Women's Management Council sponsors efforts to increase the enrollment of women within the Johnson School, influences the environment around us to promote and support women in business, provides a structure for connecting with present and future women leaders, and supports the diverse professional and personal aspirations of women within our community.

name: Judo Club at Cornell
description: We exist to promote the Japanese martial art of judo through organized practices. We meet regularly so that our members can improve their skills, have fun, and eventually compete should they wish!

name: JUGATAE
description: The mission of the organization is to provide a forum for addressing the needs of students in Entomology and to organize a seminar program in Entomology and allied fields, with the purpose of promoting interest and disseminating information therein.

name: Juggling Club
description: To provide a forum for those interested in juggling and other circus arts.

name: Just About Music Program House
description: The JAM community was created as a space within the Cornell community to foster growth, gain a better understanding, and build appreciation for all genres of music. Our residents are from a wide spectrum of the musical world and we strive to educate others (and ourselves) about the music diversity within our community. JAM encourages students and staff to be active participants in musically themed community. As a community, we want to foster your growth as an aspiring artist or appreciator of music.

name: Kali Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of the Cornell Kali Club shall be to spread cultural awareness and cultivate physical and mental strength through weekly trainings of kKali, Filipino Martial Arts, at Cornell University. There is already a PE course on campus and many students are looking to supplement their regular classes with more training and also to invite others not enrolled in the class to join, train together and learn more about Filipino martial culture.

name: Kappa Alpha Pi Pre-Law Fraternity
description: Dedicated to providing interested students information about the law school application process, law school, and the legal profession, Kappa Alpha Pi aims to facilitate interaction between brothers, individuals within the law profession, and the community as a whole. Kappa Alpha Pi pursues these goals by providing the membership with the opportunity to participate in events focused on law and service designed to help the community of law. KAPi also provide its members access to people in the area of law. Our fraternity is designed to educate about the field of law, but also strives to provide

name: Kappa Alpha Psi
description: This fraternity strives to unite college men of culture, patriotism, and honor in a bond of fraternity; to encourage honorable achievement in every field of human endeavor; to promote the spiritual, social, intellectual, and moral welfare of its members; to assist the aims of colleges and universities; and to inspire service in the public interest.

name: Kappa Alpha Theta
description: Kappa Alpha Theta was founded at Cornell in 1881 and was the first female fraternity. Iota left the Cornell campus in 1965 after a policy disagreement with the Kappa Alpha Theta headquarters' administration. In 1980, Iota returned to Cornell as the national office realized the demand for a chapter at Cornell. One of Iota's most famous alumnae is Anna Botsford Comstock, for which Comstock Hall is named after.

name: Kappa Delta
description: The Omega Chi Chapter of Kappa Delta received its charter in the spring of 1917, becoming the 21st chapter in the national sorority. In 1928, Kappa Delta moved into its first house and current residence at 109 Triphammer Rd. KD is one of three Cornell sororities that still owns its original property. The Omega Chi Chapter of Kappa Delta left Cornell's campus on October 21, 1969 when the entire house deactivated in protest of KD national's refusal to allow Jewish sisters as members. The house was reinstated in May of 1975 after a change in Kappa Delta policy. Today, the Omega Chi Chapter of Kap

name: Kappa Delta Rho
description: On May 24, 1913, Harold A. Severy, an alumnus of the Middlebury chapter doing graduate study here at Cornell University, founded KDR's second chapter. The original twenty-three members of Beta chapter made their home at the local YMCA, and the chapter remained active until the first World War, when it closed temporarily. Beta chapter was refounded in 1920 and moved to 306 Highland Road (next door to our present address). The house continued to grow throughout the 1920s and was a strong athletic fraternity during the 1930s, winning, perhaps for the last time in history, Cornell's all-sports tro

name: Kappa Kappa Gamma
description: The purpose of a chapter shall be: to advance the mission and purpose of Kappa Kappa Gamma Fraternity; to unite women through membership in a close bond of friendship, seeking to instill in them a spirit of mutual love and helpfulness; to properly maintain the organization and operation of the chapter; to cooperate with the host institution to advance academic interest and promote higher standards of social conduct; and to cooperate with other campus organizations in solving mutual problems and building higher standards of womanhood.

name: Kappa Phi Lambda
description: We, the sisters of the Kappa Phi Lambda Sorority strive to strengthen sisterhood amongst women by providing service and promoting cultural diversity to our members and our community, thus securing the bond of kinship for posterity. Kappa Phi Lambda exists to further educate individuals about Pan-Asian culture, while keeping our own identities. We aim for academic excellence, keeping in mind the importance of education and learning as the key to strength, awareness and fulfillment.

name: Kappa Sigma
description: Kappa Sigma focuses on the Four Pillars of Fellowship, Leadership, Scholarship, and Service.

name: Kappa Theta Pi Cornell Chapter
description: Build an active community of students with a shared interest in technology.

name: Kessler Scholars
description: The Kessler Scholars Program empowers high-achieving, first-generation Cornell students to realize their full potential as leaders and changemakers. We cultivate academic excellence while fostering a collaborative community where scholars support one another, engage with curiosity and purpose, and develop a lifelong commitment to giving back. Through mentorship, resources, and shared experiences, we prepare our scholars to lead with integrity, serve their communities, and create lasting positive impact in the world.

name: Kiteboarding Club at Cornell
description: To promote kiteboarding in a safe and affordable manner, while protecting the natural environment and advocating for positive social change. We aim to make kiting accessible to the Cornell Community.

name: Klezmer Ensemble at Cornell University
description: Weekly rehearsals on Tuesdays from 7pm-9pm The purpose of CUKE is to provide a musical, nondenominational, informal setting for students and community members of all backgrounds to learn about Jewish culture and play Klezmer music.

name: Knit With Care
description: The purpose of this organization is to teach people how to knit and crochet and to promote joy through fiber arts. Additionally, this club serves to further support Cornell's community of crafters.

name: Korean American Students Association
description: Our mission is to represent the Korean American community of Cornell University, and share and celebrate Korean and Korean American culture.

name: Korean Catholic Community at Cornell
description: The purpose of 4C shall be to provide a ground for Koreans or people of Korean descents who believe in Roman Catholicism to carry out and continue the work of Jesus Christ on Earth through fellowships and different activities.

name: Korean Church at Cornell
description: The purpose of this community of faith is to learn, teach and live the examples of love and service that Christ has shown us. We aim to glorify God through worship, training, fellowship, witness, thanksgiving and service. We provide spiritual and practical support to the Korean and greater Asian community on campus.

name: Korean Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of KGSA is to perform the following functions: (1) To enhance the relationships among Korean graduate students. (2) To promote relationships with other communities, both here at Cornell University and internationally. (3) To provide a means for Korean graduate students at Cornell University to obtain pertinent information related to career development and establish a social network to benefit them after graduation. (4) To serve as a liaison between the administration, the Korean graduate students at Cornell and other organizations. (5) To provide social, cultural and educational fu

name: Korean Student Association
description: The Korean Student Association at Cornell University is a student organization that focuses on enriching the college experience. Our aim is to listen to the needs of students, plan events with the members in mind, and foster a strong sense of community. With over 400 Korean-American and Korean-International student constituent, hosting events year-round, the Cornell KSA is one of the largest and most active student-run, not-for-profit organizations on campus. Each year, the KSA programs a variety of social, cultural, political events – each of which contributes to its main goals: fostering and

name: L.H. Bailey’s Botany Bunch – Botanical Society of America Cornell Student Chapter
description: The Mission of L.H. Bailey’s Botany Bunch – Botanical Society of America Cornell Student Chapter shall be to fulfill responsibilities of a Botanical Society of America student chapter, to promote interest in botanical subjects, provide botanical themed events, and serve as a resource for students about Botanical Society of America grants, programs, and other opportunities. This organization is a registered student organization of Cornell University.

name: La Asociación Latina
description: La Asociación Latina has an objective as of 1975, we the Latinx Students at Cornell University have united with the intent to create a collective organization that will serve as a forum to address the social, cultural, political and educational concerns of the Latinx community at Cornell University.

name: Laidlaw Leadership and Research Program
description: he Laidlaw Undergraduate Leadership and Research Program promotes ethical leadership and international research around the world—starting with the passionate leaders and learners found on campuses like Cornell. Eligibility First- and second-year students from any college or major may apply. You should have a strong academic background and must be able to commit to full participation in the program. U.S. citizenship is not required. In order to be eligible for program funding, scholars must commit to all components of the program. Upon acceptance, scholars will be required to sign a commitment

name: Lambda Chi Alpha
description: We believe in Lambda Chi Alpha Fraternity and its traditions, principles and ideals. The crescent is our symbol; pure, high ever growing, and the cross is our guide; denoting service, sacrifice, and even suffering and humiliation before the world, bravely endured if need be, in following that ideal. May we have faith in Lambda Chi Alpha and passion for its welfare. May we have hope for the future of Lambda Chi Alpha and strength to fight for its teachings. May we have pure hearts, that we may approach the ideal of perfect brotherly love.

name: Lambda Phi Epsilon
description: Lambda Phi Epsilon offers an eternal brotherhood that values trust and loyalty. Founded on February 25, 1981 in UCLA, Lambda Phi Epsilon is the widely renown as the largest and preeminent international Asian interest fraternal organization, providing outstanding leadership, philanthropy, and advocacy in the community. Our mission is to guide each brother on a lifelong discovery of authenticity and personal growth. As we are all grounded by our motto, "To Be Leaders Among Men," we bring together a diverse and dynamic group of men who share interests, concerns, backgrounds and cultures, and who

name: Lambda Pi Chi
description: Latinas Promoviendo Comunidad is the first Latina-focused sorority founded at an Ivy-league institution, we were established on April 16, 1988 at Cornell University. Patricia Rivera, Maria Caban, Eva Marie Sosa, Migdalia Franklin and Irma Almirall-Padamsee strove to establish an organization that would transcend their collegiate experience and consolidate their strength as responsible leaders of the community. They worked diligently to develop an impactful organization whose mission and goals would encompass the experiences of all women, but especially those of U.S. Latinas and whose ideals wo

name: Lambda Theta Phi
description: The mission of Lambda Theta Phi is to empower the Latin male through scholarship, Brotherhood, opportunity, and protection of identity and equality.

name: Language Expansion Program
description: Through weekly peer-led Language Corners, the Language Expansion Program provides a cooperative and encouraging environment for students to practice their target languages and exchange cultural knowledge. We foster language proficiency and cultural empathy within the Cornell community, with the goal that members will better serve their communities through translation and interpreting.

name: Language House
description: The Language House at Cornell University promotes a supportive and congenial environment of language immersion for select Cornell students by providing access to live-in native speakers, faculty, and staff who facilitate programs and activities that enhance students' linguistic and cultural competence in their target language and cultures in order for them to be prepared to flourish in a global society.

name: Language Resource Center
description: The Language Resource Center (LRC) is a hub for language innovation and collaboration at Cornell University. Our mission is to connect, support, and empower language learners and teachers. The LRC provides flexible physical and virtual spaces, facilitates access to resources, and advocates best practices. Our vision is to raise awareness of the value of language learning, leverage technology in service of cultural and social experiences, and grow the language community within and beyond Cornell.

name: Large Animal Undergraduate Society at Cornell
description: The purpose of Large Animal Undergrad Society at Cornell is to promote students who are interested in large animal medicine. The club aims to provide student with hands-on opportunities to work with large animals and to promote diversity within the field. The club will host networking opportunities with leaders in the industry and support members in entering the field!

name: Last Lecture at Cornell
description: If you were retiring tomorrow and given the chance to give one last lecture, what would you say? Each semester, we host a Last Lecture event where we invite one faculty member to answer this question in front of the Cornell community. Last Lecture was a beloved Cornell tradition before the pandemic that we have brought back.

name: Latidos at Cornell
description: Through our initiatives, events, and community, our mission is to empower Latinx students (and the broader Cornell community) pursuing careers in medicine. We work to dismantle systemic barriers in health care and cultivate the next generation of physicians and health leaders—leaders whose skills, voices, and compassion will save lives and redefine what equitable medicine looks like.

name: Latina/o Studies Program & LSP Student Success Office
description: Latina/o Studies is dedicated to the study of the historical, linguistic, literary, social, economic, and political experiences of a vastly heterogeneous population in the United States, that today totals over 55 million people. Officially founded in 1987 as the Hispanic American Studies Program, our name was changed to the Latina/o Studies Program in 1995. We nurture familia, inquire into the important questions of the day, and through our courses and other intellectual activities—conferences, lectures, exhibits, dialogues, and other research initiatives and activities--learn how Latinas/os c

name: Latine Graduate Student Coalition
description: The purpose of the Latine Graduate Student Coalition is to provide a forum for graduate and professional students to support one another in achieving academic excellence and recognition. While centering the experiences, needs, and voices of Latine students, LGSC welcomes all graduate and professional students committed to its mission.

name: Latino Living Center
description: The LLC has, and will continue to, build socially conscious and community-minded individuals. Our goals have been, and still are, t0 provide knowledge of our culture and the problems facing Latinxs so that the future leaders of our communities will be prepared with the skills and sensitivity necessary to effect social change. The LLC has aimed to attract more Latinx students to Cornell University, thus enabling more students to complete academic programs. Through a philosophy of openness and inclusiveness, the LLC moved forward increasing student leadership and support, multicultural competenc

name: Latino Medical Student Association
description: LMSA Plus At Cornell aims to foster an environment where Latino students interested in health care can thrive both professionally and personally, and allow them to find a community of like-minded students. LMSA Plus at Cornell seeks to acknowledge the health needs of the Latino community, as well as to promote the interests and support of those undergraduate premedical students who identify themselves as Latino students of Cornell University through social, cultural, educational, political and other activities. As part of a larger professional national network of The Latino Medical Student Ass

name: Latinx Association of Pre-laws
description: To provide Latinx self-identifying undergraduate students at Cornell with resources to aid them in their preparation for law school.

name: Latinx Student Empowerment
description: Latinx Student Empowerment provides support and resources to Cornell University’s Latinx students on their academic and personal journeys. As a senior staff member of the Centers for Student Equity, Empowerment, and Belonging in the Dean of Student office, the Associate Dean of Students and Director of Latinx Student Empowerment leads strategic planning and collaborative partnerships to improve the Latinx/e student experience at Cornell University. They offer guidance to student organizations, coordinate and implement programming, and serve as a support network for Latinx/e students. A key pri

name: LAW - American Constitution Society the Cornell Law School Student Chapter
description: The American Constitution Society for Law and Policy is a progressive legal organization that promotes the U.S. Constitutional values of "individual rights and liberties, genuine equality, access to justice, democracy and the rule of law."

name: LAW - Asian Pacific American Law Student Association
description: This organization shall adhere to the philosophy that diversity will always enlarge our understanding of the different values that need to be understood as we enter the global economy; that unity should be embraced so that we may assist the less fortunate members of our Asian community; and that leadership will take on many forms, and ultimately is a very individualistic decision based on no arbitrary set definition.

name: LAW - Association of Law & Economics at Cornell
description: Promote the study of law and economics; hold various speaker events and social programs open to the Cornell community.

name: LAW - Basketball Group
description: Our mission is to attend basketball tournaments with other law schools to maintain law student wellness and increase collaboration among neighboring law schools.

name: LAW - Black Law Students Association
description: The Black Law Students Association is a professional, nationally-affiliated organization of Black law students dedicated to improving opportunities in legal education. The Cornell chapter actively involves itself in a wide variety of professional, academic, political, cultural, social, and educational activities. BLSA also sponsors various social activities with other law school and non-law school organizations.

name: LAW - Briggs Society of International Law
description: The Briggs Society of International Law (Briggs) exists to further students' and society's understanding of international law and contemporary, international legal issues. The eponymous Professor, Herbert W. Briggs, was a distinguished lawyer, scholar, and educator in the international legal community. As an organization, we work to follow in the late Professor Briggs's footsteps. Briggs hosts guest speakers and introduces students to possible careers concerning international law.

name: LAW - Business Law Society
description: The core mission of the Business Law Society is to foster an interdisciplinary education that equips students with comprehensive knowledge and skills to address the legal and business challenges encountered in private practice and corporate settings.

name: LAW - California Law Students Association
description: CALSA is a Cornell law student organization that provides support to students from California and those that want to work or establish a connection in California. CALSA uses existing ties to California through alumni and other connections to provide substantive information regarding internships, fellowships, clerkships, Summer Associate positions, and the California state bar exam. CALSA is open to all individuals seeking a connection to California. Our purpose is to provide the necessary resources and framework to assist CALSA members achieve the necessary means to succeed in the legal profes

name: LAW - Christian Legal Society
description: The Christian Legal Society (CLS) is a national Christian fellowship organization committed to acting justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly with God (Micah 6:8). CLS inspires, encourages, and equips Christian lawyers and law students, both individually and in community, to proclaim, love and serve Jesus Christ through the study and practice of law, the provision of legal assistance to the poor and needy, and the defense of inalienable rights to life and religious freedom. The Cornell Law student chapter provides fellowship and mentorship opportunities to the Cornell law community.

name: LAW - Cornell JSD Association
description: The purpose of CJSDA shall be to contribute to the overall success and well being of JSD students and graduates.

name: LAW - Cornell Law Review
description: The Cornell Law Review publishes seven print issues of legal scholarship, as well as multiple online issues, each year. The purpose of the Law Review is to advance legal scholarship and provide student editors with an opportunity to hone their legal writing skills, critically engage with legal scholarship, and take part in organizing and running a complex organization.

name: LAW - Cornell Law Students Association
description: CLSA promotes the general welfare of Cornell Law School Students as the student government and student bar association of Cornell Law School. CLSA organizes social events to which all Cornell Law School students are invited. CLSA also allocates funding to other Cornell Law School student groups.

name: LAW - Cornell Law Students Corporate Connect
description: The purpose of Corporate Connect shall be to help law students succeed in their career goals as young professionals at Cornell Law School.

name: LAW - Cornell Middle Eastern and North African Law Students Association
description: The Cornell Middle Eastern & North African Law Students Association (MENALSA) is an affinity group created to serve and bring together Middle Eastern and North African students at Cornell Law. MENALSA's mission is threefold: (1) to build a cultural community amongst Middle Eastern and North African law students and alumni, (2) to further the professional and academic development of its members, and (3) to organize around political and legal issues that impact Middle Eastern and North African communities.

name: LAW - Environmental Law Society
description: The Environmental Law Society (ELS) is an independent student organization at Cornell Law School designed to increase student exposure to the quickly-evolving practice of environmental law, as well as to appreciate the importance of environmental public interest work both domestically and abroad.

name: LAW - Federalist Society at Cornell
description: The Federalist Society is founded on the principles that the state exists to preserve freedom, that the separation of governmental powers is central to our Constitution, and that it is emphatically the province and duty of the judiciary to say what the law is, not what it should be.

name: LAW - First-Generation Student Association
description: The mission of the organization is to: promote advocacy, community, empowerment, and identity exploration for all law students who identify with the first-generation and/or low-income student experience and supporters of these students. This group recognizes a wide range of first-generation students, including those who will be the first lawyers in their families, but prioritizes the needs of first-generation high school and college graduates who attended public primary and secondary schools and are from low-income backgrounds. Relying on the honor code, FGSA considers "low-income" to include

name: LAW - If/When/How: Lawyering for Reproductive Justice
description: The mission of If/When/How: Lawyering for Reproductive Justice shall be to develop a student community that works towards the realization of reproductive justice in all its dimensions. The organization will work towards ensuring an intersectional approach towards reproductive rights that empowers individuals to choose if, when, and how they would like to have children. Through advocacy and campaigning, the student community shall mobilize and advocate for reproductive justice that is free from coercion, discrimination, and violence. In doing so, LJR will also emphasize its focus on the interse

name: LAW - Intellectual Property and Technology Students Association
description: IPTSA's purpose is to provide the law school community with outlets, both academic and social, to pursue interests in Intellectual Property, including Patent Law, Copyright Law, Trademark Law, and Technology Transfer Law, via specific events.

name: LAW - International Arbitration Society at Cornell
description: Cornell International Arbitration Society shall provide a forum for the scholarly analysis and discussion of international commercial and investment arbitration, their legal problems and developments.

name: LAW - International Law Journal at Cornell
description: Founded in 1967, the Cornell International Law Journal (ILJ) is one of the oldest and most prominent international law journals in the United States. Four times a year, the Journal publishes scholarship that reflects the sweeping changes that are taking place in public and private international law. Each issue features articles by legal scholars, practitioners, and participants in international politics, as well as student-written notes.

name: LAW - International Law Students Association
description: The organization aims to promote community, empowerment, and advocacy for all international students at Cornell Law School. In particular, ILSA aims to address the needs of incoming international law students who are new to the United States. ILSA harnesses the power of alumni and peer mentoring to build knowledge and skills that help new international law students navigate the profession of law.

name: LAW - Jewish Law Student Association
description: The purpose of the Jewish Law Students Association (JLSA) is to maintain a Jewish presence at the school and represent all segments of the Jewish community. JLSA provides social, cultural, and religious activities for the entire community. In addition, JLSA seeks to augment awareness of legal and political issues of concern to Jews, as well as, awareness of the Jewish experience in the legal world. JLSA is affiliated with the National Law Student Network.

name: LAW - Journal of Law and Public Policy
description: JLPP's mission is to edit and publish scholarly articles and notes in the fields of law and public policy.

name: LAW - Korea Law and Culture Society
description: The purpose of the Korea Law and Culture Society and Culture Society (KLCS) shall be to provide the resources, mentorship, and necessary help for all students who desire to practice law in Korea or more generally foster their connections to Korea both cultural and professional.

name: LAW - Latino American Law Student Association
description: The purpose of LALSA is to utilize the collective resources of the members to: (1) Articulate and promote the academic and professional needs and goals of Latino law students; (2) Foster and encourage professional competence; (3) Focus on the relationship of the Latino law student and attorney to the American legal structure; (4) Instill in the Latino law student and attorney a greater awareness of and commitment to the needs of the Latino community; (5) Influence the legal community to bring about meaningful change to meet the needs of the Latino community; (6) Preserve and promote awareness

name: LAW - Law and Political Economy Collective
description: To advance the practice and study of Law and Political Economy among law students.

name: LAW - Law School Soccer Club
description: The purpose of the Law School Soccer Club is to organize soccer games for the physical and mental wellness for students in the Law School and other departments at Cornell University. Soccer is an amazing way for students to relieve stress, have fun, and meet new people from different departments on campus. The club also will help improve soccer abilities in a competitive, safe, and fun environment. The club welcomes both graduate and undergraduate students. We hope to see you on the field!

name: LAW - Legal Information Institute Supreme Court Bulletin
description: The LII Supreme Court Bulletin is a student-run publication associated with Cornell's Legal Information Institute. LII Supreme Court Bulletin provides student-written previews of every upcoming United States Supreme Court case to over 14,000 e-mail subscribers and millions of visitors to the LII website. While many of these readers are lawyers and judges, many are reporters, police officers, and other educated non-lawyers. The previews contain far more than a mere recitation of the facts and the procedural posture below. Each case preview provides a thoughtful and neutral analysis of the legal

name: LAW - Lincoln Douglas Society Cornell Chapter
description: The purpose of The Lincoln Douglas Society Cornell Chapter shall be to function as a debating society at Cornell Law School promoting civil discourse and free speech by hosting open debates on relevant topics.

name: LAW - LLM Association
description: The purpose of the LLM Association is to represent the LLM student body at Cornell University Law School. The LLMA holds scholarly and social student events.

name: LAW - Mock Trial
description: To prepare Cornell Law students to be effective trial advocates at internal, regional, and national competitions and throughout their careers

name: LAW - Muslim Law Student Association
description: Our mission is to spread awareness of events in the Muslim world and to help foster a community of inclusiveness.

name: LAW - National Lawyers Guild
description: The NLG is dedicated to the need for basic change in the structure of our political and economic system. NLG aims to bring together all those who recognize the importance of safeguarding and extending the rights of workers, women, LGBTQ people, people with disabilities and people of color, upon whom the welfare of the entire nation depends; who seek actively to eliminate racism; who work to maintain and protect our civil rights and liberties in the face of persistent attacks upon them; and who look upon the law as an instrument for the protection of the people, rather than for their repression

name: LAW - Native American Law Student Association
description: The purpose of the Cornell Law School NALSA shall be to: articulate and promote the professional needs and goals of Native Law Students and their allies; foster and encourage professional competence; focus upon the relationship of the Native American Law Student, the Native American Attorney and their allies to the American legal structure; instill in every attorney and Law Student a greater awareness and commitment to the needs of the Native American community; influence the legal community to bring about meaningful change to meet the needs of the Native American community; adopt and implemen

name: LAW - Older Wiser Law Students (O.W.L.S.) at Cornell
description: The purpose of Older Wiser Law Students (OWLS) shall be to foster a supportive community for students who have taken significant time off prior to law school; are transitioning into second careers; are partnered, married, and/or parenting; or view their academic path as non-traditional. We define a significant amount of time as 5 years or more separated from an undergraduate institution. The group caters to the social, academic, and other needs of those who are transitioning back to student life after a number of years out of school or who have serious non-academic commitments that fall outsid

name: LAW - Public Interest Law Union
description: Cornell Law School's Public Interest Law Union offers opportunities for students interested in a public interest legal career to explore the diversity of career options available to them. The group hosts public interest speaker events, provides volunteer service opportunities for members of the law school, and helps raise funds for grants for law students working in a Public Interest job in the summer.

name: LAW - Society of Wine and Jurisprudence
description: To educate members and the broader community about relevant (primarily legal) issues that impact the production, distribution, and consumption of wine. In keeping with that goal and our broader mission, we also seek to engage our members in professional development and etiquette.

name: LAW - South Asian Law Students Association
description: The South Asian Law Students Association promotes education and leadership among South Asian law students and expands students' understanding and appreciation of South Asian political, legal and social issues. SALSA hopes to provide a space for law students interested in the South Asian experience to gather, create support networks, and form a community.

name: LAW - Sports and Entertainment Law Society
description: SELS is the go-to student organization for all matters concerning sports and entertainment law. We look to bring in guest speakers, engage in competitions, and generally network with those in the sports and entertainment law fields. Sports and entertainment law spans arbitration, labor law, contracts, copyright application and infringement, and much more. This organization is a registered student organization of Cornell University.

name: LAW - Tax Law Association at Cornell
description: Promote the study of tax law

name: Law - Veteran Student Association at Cornell Law
description: CLVA is an organization for law students with (1) current or prior military service, (2) an interest in law related to military affairs, veteran's affairs, and international law, and/or (3) an interest in a career as a JAG officer, Dept. of Veterans Affairs attorney, or other veteran-related law practice.

name: LAW - WOMEN OF COLOR COLLECTIVE
description: Women of Color Collective's (WOCC) purpose is to provide a supportive space for African-American, African, Afro-Caribbean, Asian, South Asian, Middle Eastern, Hispanic/Latina, Native American, Bi-racial, Multi-racial and other women students of color at Cornell Law School. Through cultural, social, professional, educational and community service programs, WOCC will advance the needs of women and students of color and enrich the educational and mentorship experience of women of color at Cornell Law School. In addition, WOCC's purpose is to address the unique challenges currently faced by women

name: LAW - Women's Law Coalition
description: The Women's Law Coalition promotes women in the law through mentorship programs, speakers, networking events, and professional panels.

name: Les Femmes de Substance
description: The purpose of Les Femmes de Substance is to foster community and leadership within the Black female population on Cornell's campus. Through educational experiences and programs, Les Femmes strives to create women of substance, who will make every effort to give back and build up their surrounding communities.

name: Less Than Three A Cappella
description: Less Than Three wants to share an eclectic and diverse musical repertoire with the Cornell community while helping each member to grow as a singer. Less Than Three seeks to promote music for all audiences and performers.

name: Let's Get Ahead at Cornell
description: Let’s Get Ahead empowers more than 700 students nationwide through free, high-quality tutoring, mentorship, and academic enrichment programs. Our mission is to close opportunity gaps in education by connecting dedicated mentors with students who benefit from personalized support. Beyond academics, we lead initiatives that address community needs—such as food drives, clothing donations, and school supply distributions—to ensure students and families have the resources they need to thrive. Through our global initiative in Ghana, we extend our commitment to educational equity abroad by supporting

name: LGBT Resource Center
description: The LGBT Resource Center provides advocacy, outreach, education, support, and community to LGBTQ+ students of all identities, backgrounds, and experiences.

name: Lifted at Cornell
description: We are dedicated community service participants who assist and engage in service projects on Cornell's campus and in the Ithaca community. Our flagship event is Lifted at the end of the semester.

name: Line Dancing Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of the Line Dancing Club at Cornell shall be to create an inclusive country dance community and contribute to the social dance scene at Cornell through the instruction of line dance choreographies.

name: Linguistics Circle at Cornell
description: The CLC serves to promote exchange of ideas among graduate students in the field and to advocate for the graduate student body within the department. Throughout the course of the academic year the CLC invites a series of outside speakers from linguistics departments around the country and the world. Speakers deliver talks attended by faculty, graduate and undergraduate students (followed by a reception) and are often available for one-on-one meetings with interested graduate students. The CLC also publishes The Proceedings of SALT, which contains articles developed from work presented at the a

name: Lion Dance at Cornell
description: Cornell Lion Dance strives to carry on the tradition of Lion Dancing while enriching the Cornell and Ithaca communities.

name: Litera: Ukrainian Educational Outreach
description: The mission of Litera shall be to provide educational outreach opportunities to elementary, middle, and high school students in Ukraine in the form of virtual group outreach sessions led by Cornell students, faculty, and staff who are volunteer members of Litera.

name: Literary Society at Cornell University
description: Organized by and for English majors and enthusiasts, the society plans events each semester to inspire interest in the major. Events may include panel discussions with English Department professors, student poetry readings, book club discussions with Cornell authors, pre-performance discussions for theater productions at the Schwartz Center, a mentor program between under- and upper-class English majors and luncheons with visiting writers. The Literary Society is comprised of English enthusiasts of all different areas – from English majors with concentrations spanning literary theory, creative

name: Logos: The Cornell Undergraduate Philosophy Club and Journal
description: Logos: The Cornell Undergraduate Philosophy Club and Journal is a refereed journal at the Sage School of Philosophy in Ithaca, New York. An entirely student-run journal, Logos publishes undergraduate work in all branches and traditions of philosophy. Undergraduates from around the globe are invited to submit papers annually for peer-review. Accepted papers are published in the current year's edition of Logos, and the authors of the top three submissions are awarded cash prizes.
