In addition to publishing the journal, Logos functions as the general-interest philosophical club for the undergradua

name: LOKO
description: LOKO is a union among students of all backgrounds that is aimed at promoting Korean music, fine arts, and culture through dance performances.

name: Love Living at Home
description: Helping people 62 and over in Tompkins County

name: Lunatic Magazine at Cornell
description: Our purpose is to entertain and delight the Cornell University community with humor, mirth, and satire. We publish a glossy print magazine once a semester with stories, articles, comics, and art. We also run a website where we post content regularly.

name: Lutheran Student Fellowship
description: The Fellowship provides a space for students to carry out the tenets of the Lutheran faith and help educate the Cornell community about our faith.

name: MAC Doctoral Peer Mentoring Club
description: The MAC Mentoring Program is a graduate student-run initiative from the Graduate School Office of Inclusion & Student Engagement (OISE). Designed to address the needs of a diversity of doctoral students across all graduate fields through peer mentoring, this program focuses on helping new graduate students identify and form community at Cornell. MAC strives to promote a social environment that is inclusive of all doctoral students at Cornell. During the academic year, MAC hosts two monthly events, general body meetings (GBMs) and MAC-Meetups, to help broaden and strengthen a sense of community

name: Magic the Gathering Club at Cornell
description: The Cornell Magic the Gathering Club is a community built around the collectible trading card game Magic: the Gathering, connecting players and hosting tournaments and casual events.

name: Mainland China Students Association
description: Mainland China Students Association works to provide a network and community for Cornell students who are interested in Mainland Chinese affairs. We hold events to foster cultural enrichment for both MCSA members and the greater Cornell community. Examples include Taste of China, Cultural Show, Chinese New Year Gala, karaoke, movie night, etc. MCSA also strives to hold strong relationships with other organizations on campus with the goal of promoting unity at Cornell. MCSA is committed to bringing the best cultural experience for all those interested.

name: Mapping Society at Cornell
description: The purpose of MSC is to grant students opportunities to engage in mapping and related geospatial activities that address challenges at local, national, and global scales. Students will create, analyze, and share open data and learn to use open source software in this process.

name: Marginalia: the Cornell Undergraduate Poetry Review
description: Marginalia Review publishes the poetic works of Cornell's undergraduates, regardless of college or major. We hope to foster a community of poets, artists, and literary admirers by producing at least two publications a year and by hosting multiple workshops and readings each semester.

name: Mariachi Regional en Cornell University
description: It is our mission to share our passion for traditional Mariachi music with individuals from any background, and through this music add to Cornell University's increasingly diverse student population.

name: Mario Einaudi Center for International Studies
description: The center organizes, stimulates, and supports research, teaching, and outreach programs and activities to enhance graduate and undergraduate education and to prepare Cornellians to contribute in the international sphere.

name: Mars Rover at Cornell
description: Our student-run team fosters creativity and intellectual growth through the development of our rover. As engineers, we strive to cultivate a creative environment where brilliant young minds can develop innovative, intellectual, and leadership qualities through our vision of building a rover that may one day aid in the exploration of the final frontier.

name: Medical Ethics & Dilemmas Society
description: The mission of the Medical Ethics and Dilemmas Society (MEDS) is to foster a community of students dedicated to exploring and understanding the complex ethical issues in medicine and healthcare. MEDS aims to promote thoughtful discussion, critical analysis, and collaborative problem-solving to address ethical dilemmas, both historical and contemporary. The society is committed to cultivating ethical leadership, empathy, and a commitment to finding morally sound alternatives to questionable medical practices, preparing its members to navigate the challenges of the medical field with integrity a

name: Medics in Armenia at Cornell
description: The purpose of Medics in Armenia is to educate and train students interested in and/or pursuing a future in medicine by traveling to Armenia to shadow medical professionals and to volunteer at impoverished communities across Armenia.

name: Medieval Studies Graduate Association
description: The Medieval Studies Graduate Association is dedicated to being a forum for sustained discussion and debate within the student medievalist body on campus and to strengthening connectivity between these students. It aims to provide a platform for underrepresented groups and disciplines. It also provides an official channel for discussion with faculty, the MS Department, and the Graduate School. It was founded at a time when there was no such forum in existence. Its purpose is to encourage collaboration by Cornellians from across the spectrum of departments and programs on campus, so that they c

name: Medieval Studies Student Colloquium
description: The Medieval Studies Student Colloquium is a forum dedicated to showcasing the ideas and research of the medievalist community at Cornell. Now in its thirty-sixth year (academic year 2025-2026), MSSC is an annual one-day colloquium organized by the graduate students of the Medieval Studies Program. Each year, MSSC is an opportunity for all interested in the Middle Ages at Cornell—as well as visitors from other institutions—to share papers in a relaxed and friendly environment. In recent years, MSSC has also organized events leading up to the colloquium, including lectures and workshops led by

name: Mediocre Melodies
description: The Mediocre Melodies is a revolutionary a cappella group that is truly the first of its kind. We are, quite frankly, average singers who have always wanted an a cappella experience but don't quite have what it takes to make one of the big ones! We are co-ed and focused on having fun and making friends while also creating some beautiful music along the way. Along with being an a cappella group, we donate all possible proceeds to charity. In short, we are "Bad Singers for a Good Cause".

name: Medium Design Collective
description: Medium is an interdisciplinary design organization at Cornell University, whose mission is to build an interdisciplinary collective of individuals, as a platform for engaging in dialogue and collaboration about design. Majors from all seven colleges are represented in our collective, which is split into incubates, events, marketing, web, education, and publication. Each year, Medium creates design projects and a publication centered around a theme, and puts on events that showcase different facets of design and workshops that teach design skills. In this way, we hope to spark dialogue through

name: MEDLIFE
description: MEDLIFE is a non-profit organization that works in developing countries to improve access to MEDs: Medicine, Education, and Development. Our overarching mission is to help families achieve greater freedom from the constraints of poverty, empowering them to live healthier lives.

name: Melodramatics Theatre Company, Inc.
description: The purpose of The Melodramatics Theatre Company shall be to bring together students and faculty of Cornell University, along with Ithaca College, and the Tompkins County Community to present one entertaining musical theatre production of artistic excellence per semester.

name: Men Of Color in Athletics
description: The mission of Men of Color in Athletics shall be to provide men of color within Cornell Athletics a support network and space to share their experiences. We aspire to foster an atmosphere that encourages the embracing of diverse cultural backgrounds, highlighting the resilience and passion that empower men of color to balance their roles as accomplished students and athletes at the pinnacle of their pursuits.

name: Men of Last Call
description: We are Last Call, an award-winning all-male a cappella group at Cornell University. You can find us singing and performing all across campus from arches to concert halls. If you'd like to check us out, come to one of our semesterly concerts! Or, if you can sing, act, arrange, compose, dance, rap, or beatbox, consider trying out - we're always looking to add to our family. Hope to see you soon!

name: Men's Club Ice Hockey at Cornell
description: The mission of Cornell Men's Club Ice Hockey is to achieve visible excellence through competition for championships, while promoting wellness and school spirit, through a commitment to developing leaders beyond the game of hockey.

name: Men's Club Lacrosse at Cornell
description: As with any competitive sports team, we practice and compete against other club lacrosse teams. This includes SUNY Cortland, Binghamton, Syracuse, etc. Although we are definitely competitive, it is also important to us that we maintain an enjoyable environment for everyone involved. We practice about once a week and have a handful of games each semester, with more in the spring season. If you played in HS and miss the sport, don't hesitate to get involved.

name: Men's Club Volleyball at Cornell
description: Cornell Men's Club Volleyball is dedicated to playing competitive volleyball in a fun, engaging environment. As part of the Eastern Collegiate Volleyball Association (ECVA), we play at least three weekend tournaments per semester, capped off by the national tournament hosted by NCVF. Our conference includes Syracuse, Buffalo, Binghamton, Army, RIT, Cortland, and Brockport. If you love playing volleyball, this is the closest to varsity Cornell has to offer. Contact us or find us playing on the beautiful beaches of north campus. See you at try outs in early September.

name: Men's Club Water Polo at Cornell
description: The purpose of the men's water polo team is to allow for highly competitive play in a fun environment for all interested students.

name: Men's Fencing Club
description: Our organization was founded following the disbandment of the Cornell Men's Varsity Fencing team in 1991. We serve as the non-varsity counterpart to the Women's Varsity Team and compete in National and Regional competitions throughout the United States. We hope to spread the sport of fencing on the Cornell Campus and strive to provide an outlet for experienced men fencers to compete against other club and varsity teams throughout the nation. A part of our club makes up the Women's Varsity Practice Squad, who assist the girls in practice and receive coaching from the Women's coaching staff.

name: Men's Rugby Football Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of Men’s Rugby Football Club shall be to foster the growth of rugby among Cornell University students through organized competition, skill development, and the promotion of physical fitness and teamwork.

name: Men's Swim Club at Cornell University
description: The Men's Cornell Club Swim Team is a Cornell club sports team where anyone with prior competitive swimming experience can train for competition with the team. The team will practice weekly and compete in intercollegiate meets throughout the semester in order to gauge personal development and to bond as a team.

name: Mews and Loving House: the LGBTQ+ Living Learning Unit
description: Welcome to the Mews Hall and Loving House: the LGBTQ+ Living Learning Unit community page! Mews Hall is home to over 200 first-year students and Loving House consists of 30 students from all class years. Our community is located on North Campus, conveniently located next to the Appel Commons, Robert Purcell Community Center and the Helen Newman Gym. The Mews community is committed to providing a high quality living learning experience that allows residents to learn about self and community through opportunities for engagement and leadership. The community is supported by a staff who is trained

name: Mexican Students Association
description: The Mexican Student Association's (MexSA) purpose is to connect students of Mexican descent at Cornell and abroad. By navigating the manifestation of culture, MexSA aims to foster leadership and aid in civic engagement, creating an empowering and supportive community. Deep and familial bonds await for anyone who decides to join MexSA.

name: Middle Eastern Music Ensemble at Cornell
description: MEME at Cornell currently focusses on sharing the intricacy and beauty of Arabic vocal music and instruments with the Cornell and Ithaca community. The group's primary instrumentation will consist of the takht ensemble: oud, nay, qanoun, violin, and riq, darbuka, duff, and the additional string section of viola, cello, and bass. The music of MEME at Cornell will be largely based around Egypt and the Levant, including Muwashahat, classical songs such as Um Kalthoum, and folk songs or songs from other regions that are compatible with a traditional takht ensemble.

name: Milstein Program in Technology & Humanity
description: The Milstein Program selects a small cohort of extraordinary first year undergraduates each year who are excited by interdisciplinary thinking, dynamic collaboration, and emergent technology. The Program offers a supportive community of engaged learners, speaker series along with core courses, unique short courses, mentorship, career development, and funded research opportunities, including an 8 week immersive experience at Cornell Tech on Roosevelt Island. We are the & in Arts & Sciences.

name: Minds Matter at Cornell
description: Cornell Minds Matter (CMM) promotes mental health awareness and emotional well-being for all Cornell students. We work to reduce the stigma of mental illness by holding educational events and creating safe spaces to foster a healthy, balanced lifestyle. CMM acts as a liaison between students, faculty, staff, and administration to advocate for the student perspective on mental health resources and campus policies. Through our project teams and G-Body members, we continue to provide accessible resources that serve the needs of our diverse living-learning community. Whether your interests stem fr

name: Minorities in Agriculture Natural Resources and Related Sciences
description: The purpose of MANRRS at Cornell shall be to develop and empower individuals in agriculture, natural resources, and related sciences by nurturing potential, supporting unique journeys, and connecting members to opportunities that inspire leadership and innovation. The goals of Cornell MANRRS are to: promote and strengthen interest in agriculture, natural resources, environmental sciences, and related fields through educational, professional, and community-based initiatives. Create opportunities for students to explore careers, develop professional skills, build meaningful connections, and enga

name: Minority Animal Science Students
description: The primary focus of MASS (Minority Animal Science Students) is to support underrepresented minority students in the field of animal science. This organization understands the continuous struggle of minorities pursuing a future in animal studies, including lack of representation in the field. It shall be the goal of MASS to consciously support these students in the animal science division of undergraduate studies at Cornell University and encourage their success.

name: Minority Industrial and Labor Relations Student Organization
description: The Minority ILR Student Organization (MILRSO) provides social, academic, and pre-professional support to its members. Open to all students, MILRSO facilitates a cross-cultural dialogue that addresses the experiences of underrepresented identities in the workplace. MILRSO maintains corporate and alumni contacts to aid members' professional development. For MILRSO, underrepresented identities include: people of color, the LGBTQ community, non-conforming persons, women, or gender. MILRSO exists as a place for these communities to feel welcome and to feel supported.

name: MiXed at Cornell
description: Mixed at Cornell is a Cornell University organization that aims to create a supportive network for multiethnic, multiracial, multicultural, and multinational individuals - by facilitating dialogue and providing a platform for the members of our mixed community.

name: Mock Trial Association
description: The Cornell Undergraduate Mock Trial Association is a student-run undergraduate organization that competes against other collegiate mock trial teams in various tournaments throughout the fall and spring semesters. Over the course of the academic year, we work to develop critical thinking, public speaking, legal reasoning, and acting prowess, culminating in numerous trials where we argue a prepared case before a panel of judges. Because of the variety of roles, Cornell's Mock Trial Team is comprised of a wide diversity of members with an array of interests and career aspirations within the lega

name: Modern Living Rentals - North Campus Properties
Modern Living Rentals - South Hill Properties
Moot Court at Cornell University
description: Moot Court at Cornell University shall be established for the primary purpose of allowing undergraduate students to pursue their interest in constitutional law and legal argumentation. Although Cornell hosts many law-centered organizations, few, if any, serve undergraduate students in their legal pursuits. Whereas organizations such as mock trial focus on performative aspects of argumentation, moot court brings a unique combination of competitive argumentation and exposure to substantive constitutional principles.

name: Mosaic Hospitality Association
description: The purpose of Mosaic Hospitality Association shall be to provide education, leadership training, mentorship, and customized support to encourage the full mosaic of hospitality talent in building meaningful careers and lasting economic opportunity for all.

name: Movimiento Estudiantil Chican at de Aztlan
description: MECHA provides academic and personal support to students in the organization, enhances the community's awareness of Chicanx culture through educational, cultural, and social programming, and promotes the continued education of Chicanx students. We are working towards a decolonial understanding of the "Chicanx" label. It transcends beyond an identity; it is a philosophy and mindset. "Chicanx" is inclusive of any person of any ethnicity or race. Although MECHA used to cater to the Latinx community, the organization is open to anyone willing to liberate and empower the marginalized. We aim to cel

name: MSBA Data Science Club at Cornell
description: The MSBA Data Science Club at Cornell Johnson College of Business is an organization founded in 2022 by students of the M.S. Business Analytics program at SC Johnson Graduate School of Management. The mission of the MSBA Data Science Club at Cornell is to inspire and prepare students to excel in data science and machine learning, providing them with education, skills, and networking opportunities to solve complex business problems through data-driven solutions. We equip our members for DS/ML interviews, facilitate networking with faculty, alumni, and industry professionals, encourage the devel

name: Mu Epsilon Delta
description: Mu Epsilon Delta is a national co-educational, pre-health professional fraternity whose mission is to prepare members to succeed in pre-health careers through the development of scholarship, fraternity, and service. We encourage excellence in health science scholarship through promoting a holistic model of healthcare by fostering cooperation and collaboration between various pre-health disciplines, educations, an professionals

name: Muay Thai Club
description: Cornell Thai Boxing Club provides members of the Cornell community an opportunity to learn and practice the combat sport of Muay Thai. All levels of interest and experience are welcomed and respected. To participate in controlled contact sparring, it must be sanctioned by the instructor and both participants must sign the Waiver and Release Form.

name: Multicultural Community-Fueled Activities Board
description: The purpose of MCFAB shall be to bring performers of color to the Cornell campus. We are built and made for the community, by the community, in order to make minority students feel heard and listened to. MCFAB respects the interests of the Cornell student body and makes it its mission to bring diverse and exciting talents to campus.

name: Multicultural Greek and Fraternal Council
description: The mission of our Council is to operate as a united governing body for all organizations. We are dedicated to promoting unity and serving as a support system for all organizations. We will serve as a model for the underrepresented student community and operate as a united body to effectively advocate the issues and concerns of our organizations and the entire campus community that we serve.

name: Multicultural Student Leadership and Empowerment
description: Welcome to Multicultural Student Leadership and Empowerment! Our mission is to encourage student learning through the co-curricular and foster an inclusive campus environment. With a commitment to increasing cross-cultural awareness and competency, we support students and student organizations in their efforts to offer a wide variety of programs and initiatives that explore both the shared and unique experiences, histories, and heritages of our diverse community. We do this through supporting more than 150 student organizations, advising key programs and organizations, promoting peer to peer m

name: Mundial FC Mens Club Soccer at Cornell
description: Mundial FC is an organization committed to playing competitive college-level soccer with established players of different backgrounds and playing styles. The team consistently represents Cornell at the Region 1 tournament, and in 2023, won the Regional Championship, making Mundy first out of over 160 teams in the northeast. In 2023, Mundial was ranked 5th in the country., and appeared in the National Championship Tournament for the second year in a row. Mundial values creating a competitive, but more importantly, fun environment, and promoting strong friendships on and off the field. We compet

name: Music Graduate Association
description: The Music Graduate Association is the official organization for the graduate students in the Music department. We organize small and large events to help our academic and professional development, and social outings to help foster a sense of community amongst the grad students. We also serve an advocacy role through discussing issues that affect our members at meetings and bringing them to the faculty in our department or GPSA.

name: Music Lovers Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of the Music Lovers Club at Cornell is to foster a vibrant community through the shared love of music, offering events and activities that explore diverse genres and deepen musical knowledge. Our mission is to create an inclusive environment wherein members can discover new music, celebrate their favorites, and engage with the broader musical community.

name: Music Production at Cornell
description: We strive to build a community of people interested in all aspects of music production. Regardless of experience, we hope to allow polish every interest in music into concrete growth.

name: Muslim Educational and Cultural Association
description: Provide educational, cultural and religious services to the Cornell community and its surrounding communities in order to promote an Islamic environment and an awareness of Islam.

name: Muslim Professional Association
description: The mission of Muslim Professional Association (MPA) is to foster the development of socially-aware leaders within Cornell University and beyond, with a focus on the Muslim community. MPA aims to build professional skills and prepare members for successful careers in industry or postgraduate programs through engagement with complex issues, leadership opportunities, and strategic development.

name: Mutual Investment Club of Cornell
description: The Mutual Investment Club of Cornell (MICC) is the largest undergraduate student-run investment club at Cornell University, currently with approximately $115,000 in assets. Our core business is managing an internationally diversified portfolio of equity and fixed income securities. Our mission is to bring asset management capabilities into the hands of students with the goals of promoting education, performance, and industry exposure to students of all levels.

name: Myanmar Students Association at Cornell
description: This organization aims to promote awareness of Myanmar, its culture on the Cornell Campus and the Ithaca Tompkins community, and to have space for a community of students with ties to, or interests in Myanmar.

name: National Alliance on Mental Illness at Cornell
description: Provide support to families, relatives and friends of people diagnosed with mental health conditions; Educate about serious mental illnesses; and advocate for families impacted by mental illness.

name: National Association of Anorexia and Associated Disorders Chapter at Cornell
description: As a long-time volunteer with ANAD and someone who has personally experienced the challenges of eating disorders, I am passionate about bringing the ANAD School Ambassador Program to Cornell.In alignment with ANAD’s mission and core values, Cornell ASAP (Awareness, Support, and Prevention) will foster an open, inclusive community that promotes self-care, body acceptance, and overall wellbeing. We believe in the power of connection, compassion, and long-term community relationships as key elements of healing and awareness. Our group will collaborate closely with ANAD to ensure that all communic

name: National Society of Black Engineers at Cornell University
description: To increase the number of culturally responsible Black engineers who excel academically, succeed professionally and positively impact the community.

name: Native American and Indigenous Students At Cornell
description: Native American and Indigenous Students at Cornell (NAISAC) exists to promote and preserve understanding of Indigenous cultures of the Americas, to raise awareness of Indigenous issues, and to foster networks among American Indians, Alaska Natives, Native Hawaiians, First Nations, and other Indigenous students and alumni of Cornell University.

name: NatureRX
description: Nature Rx is built on the premise that time spent in nature is therapeutic, can supplement clinical interventions, and contributes to overall mental health and well-being. We work to help students of all disciplines and levels improve their cognitive ability, lessen symptoms of anxiety, and reduce stress through interactive events in nature. We welcome our members to delve into their personal background, love for the great outdoors, inner wellness and an interest in improving the health of their community as a part of NatureRx.

name: Naval Reserve Officer Training Corps at Cornell
description: Cornell Naval ROTC, through a disciplined, resilient, and collaborative culture, forges servant leaders committed to excellence.

name: Nazaqat
description: We aim to convey the elegance and beauty in Kathak, a classical Indian dance form, through creative fusion choreographies on semi-classical or modern music. We hope to make choreographies that preserve grace and story-telling in the dance form yet creatively combine it with contemporary Indian and Western music and dance.

name: Neo-Soul Ensemble
description: Neo-Soul an instrumental group that encourages musicianship and creativity in an effort to craft meaningful and innovative musical performances.

name: Nepalese Student Association at Cornell
description: The Nepalese Student Association at Cornell (NSAC) is dedicated to fostering a welcoming and inclusive community for Nepalese and Nepalese American students. Our mission is to create a vibrant and supportive environment where individuals from Nepal and of Nepalese descent can come together, celebrate their cultural heritage, and navigate their academic journeys effectively in a foreign land.

name: Network of Enlightened Women - Cornell University Chapter
description: The mission of NeW is to foster the education and leadership skills of university women. NeW is also devoted to expanding the intellectual diversity on college campuses. NeW members meet regularly to discuss the opportunities and challenges facing women today, as well as current political issues.

name: Neurobiology and Behavior Graduate Student Society
description: The purpose of the NBBGSS is to facilitate communication between the graduate students and the faculty in the field of NBB at Cornell. Our goals include disseminating important information to graduate students and acting as a formal voice for graduate students within the workings of the department. Additionally, the NBBGSS fosters community among graduate students in the field by organizing social events and discussion forums.

name: NeuroNerds
description: The mission of NeuroNerds is to design, build, revise, and share neuroscience and psychology lessons with local youth in the Central New York region. In working towards these goals, NeuroNerds aims to address educational inequities within the STEM education available to primary and secondary school students in the Central New York region.

name: New Life Presbyterian Church
description: New Life Presbyterian Church

name: Nexus at Cornell
description: Our mission is to redefine the scope of impact that Cornell students can make. We aim to develop novel solutions that will be deployed by global organizations to create positive social change. Our members think like researchers, build like engineers, and execute like entrepreneurs.

name: Nigerian Students Association
description: The purpose of the Nigerian Students Association is to foster cultural unity and understanding among the Nigerian community at Cornell. We hope to provide a forum that will celebrate the diversity embodied in Nigeria through cultural events, educational seminars, and community outreach programs, as well as sharing the culture not only with Nigerian students, but with the Cornell community at large.

name: Nolan Research Student Association
description: Transform critical thinking into promising research questions and encourage collaborations beyond the traditional boundary.

name: NOMAS: Cornell
description: Cornell NOMAS is the Cornell University Student Chapter of the National Organization of Minority Architects (NOMA), a national organization founded in 1971 to support and advocate for the advancement of underrepresented professionals in architecture and the built environment. Since 1992, Cornell NOMAS has served as a critical platform for mentorship, academic excellence, professional development, and community engagement within the College of Architecture, Art, and Planning. We are committed to promoting equity, representation, and culturally responsive design while preparing students to becom

name: Nordic Ski Racing at Cornell
description: The purpose of Nordic Ski Racing at Cornell is to provide an opportunity for Cornell students to compete in the sport of Nordic (cross-country) skiing. We also provide instruction and equipment for those students who do not know how to Nordic ski to come learn how to ski.

name: North African Student Association at Cornell
description: The purpose of the North African Student Association shall be to create a supportive community for students of North African heritage and those interested in the region. Our mission is to celebrate and share the diverse cultures, histories, and languages of North Africa, while fostering dialogue, representation, and cross-cultural understanding on campus.

name: North Campus Faculty Living-Learning Programs
description: North Campus Faculty-in-Residence and Faculty Fellows play a fundamental role in the North Campus living-learning community, helping to create a shared experience and supportive environment that fosters academic and intellectual learning, personal development, holistic well-being, and a sense of belonging and connectedness.

name: Nothing But Treble
description: We hope to bring joy to the Cornell and Ithaca community through music and song. Our organization brings undergraduate women together who like to sing and perform. We hold own concerts each semester and perform at many other events and shows throughout the year.

name: Nutrition Graduate Student Organization
description: NGSO is a graduate student organization at Cornell University established to promote interaction among graduate students in the Division of Nutritional Sciences (DNS) and to facilitate communication and interaction between the graduate students and the DNS faculty and administration.

name: Office of Academic Discovery and Impact
description: The Office of Academic Discovery and Impact (OADI) at Cornell University serves as a centralized hub that provides academic and professional-development support and resources for undergraduate students who are traditionally underrepresented and/or underserved in higher education.

name: Office of Diversity & Inclusion at AAP
description: We are committed to the belief that architecture, art, and planning are simultaneously intellectual and material practices, and that leadership in cultural production demands both expertise in a specific discipline and wide knowledge in the liberal arts.

name: Office of Federal Relations
description: The Office of Federal Relations represents Cornell University’s interests before the federal government and educates the Cornell community about relevant federal government policies and actions. In carrying out efforts to promote federal government partnerships with Cornell, we take into consideration the priorities and initiatives and the land-grant mission of the university. Our office in Washington, DC, is available for use by Cornell University faculty and staff conducting university business in the nation’s capital. Our staff offers support to Cornell representatives who travel to Washing

name: Office of Inclusion and Student Engagement
description: Our mission is for graduate students to establish a sense of belonging at Cornell and achieve their academic and professional aspirations; and to facilitate access, equity, diversity, and inclusion within graduate education through evidence-based practices and positive systemic change.

name: Office of Inclusive Excellence
description: The Office of Inclusive Excellence empowers all students to grow and thrive in their academic, professional, and personal lives, and we foster community-wide recognition and celebration of the invaluable capacity of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging to enable and accelerate success for all.

name: Office of Spirituality and Meaning-Making
description: Through programming, community-engaging, and religious services, the Office of Spirituality and Meaning-Making (OSMM) provides opportunities for exploration of spiritual beliefs, consideration of one's meaning and purpose, examination of the interconnected nature of humanity, and the pursuit of a more socially just world. OSMM is the home of Cornell United Religious Work (CURW), a community of affiliates - religious, spiritual, and ethical leaders - who offer support, programming, and service opportunities.

name: Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards
Office of the Assemblies
description: The Office of Assemblies (OA) provides administrative support and financial oversight to the Student (SA), Graduate and Professional Student (GPSA), Employee (EA) and University (UA) Assemblies, and their respective committees. A fundamental mission of the OA is to engage constituencies across campus and increase participation in the shared governance process and voice effectively the interests and concerns of the non-academic members of the campus community. The OA serves to maintain channels and processes for the members' continuous involvement in the decision-making process of the Universit

name: Office of the Dean of Students
description: The Office of the Dean of Students serves as a central point of contact for the advocacy, empowerment, and education of all students. The Office of the Dean of Students (DOS) cultivates the holistic growth and development of students through advocacy, empowerment, and education. We enhance the student experience by offering comprehensive support and resources, providing co-curricular opportunities, and fostering a sense of belonging.

name: Office of University Commencement Events
description: The Office of Cornell Commencement Events is the planning resource for families, students, faculty, staff, and volunteers.

name: Officer Resource Group
description: The Officer Resource Group is a space for all Group Officers to find resources for leadership, group management, and use of CampusGroups. We will send out monthly emails with reminders and recommendations, and you are welcome to use the Group Page to ask each questions as well!

name: Omega Phi Beta
description: Our purpose is to Serve and Educate people of diverse backgrounds through sisterhood, leadership, and guidance. As positive role models, we promote unity of all cultures, focus on the empowerment of our gender and raise the standards of excellence in our academic, social, and personal endeavors.

name: On Tap Dance Troupe
description: On Tap Dance Troupe is Cornell's only all-tap dancing troupe. This group of fun-loving tappers performs at shows both on and off campus. Every spring, On Tap hosts its own spring show, featuring original student choreography.

name: Open Orchestra at Cornell
description: To create a non-competitive, less demanding community for Cornell students who play string instruments, with a common performance goal.

name: Operations Research Graduate Association
description: The purpose of ORGA shall be to unite all ORIE PhD students and create events and interaction within the department and broader community.

name: Optica Cornell Student Chapter
description: The purpose of this organization is to further the commitment to optics research put forth by the Optica Foundation and create a community for those in both academia and industry here at Cornell.

name: Orchestra Board at Cornell
description: The purpose of the Cornell Orchestra Board is to unify the members of the Cornell Symphony Orchestra and Cornell Chamber Orchestra through various performance, service, and social events throughout the year. The board also plans orchestra tours and community outreach events in the Ithaca community.

name: Order of Omega
description: The Mission of the Order of Omega, Beta Upsilon Chapter, is to bring together leaders from diverse backgrounds within the Cornell Greek system in promoting our identity as the Greek honors society. We will represent the positive attributes of the Greek community and advocate for chapter philanthropy events while discouraging and shunning the negative aspects of our community that prevent us from representing ourselves and our peers in a positive light.

name: Organization for Afghan Students
description: The purpose of the Organization for Afghan Students is to create a space for members of the Cornell community of Afghan origin and those interested in Afghanistan's culture to learn about and celebrate this culture together.

name: Organization of Cornell Planners
description: The Organization of Cornell Planners (OCP) manages departmental professional development and social events for Master's students of Regional Planning, Historic Preservation Planning, and Regional Science. OCP interfaces with several student groups committed to advancing the field of planning: Design Connect, the Women's Planning Forum, and the International Planning Students Organization are among many student organizations whose activities are promoted and co-sponsored by the OCP. OCP can co-host events with student organizations outside CRP and AAP. OCP also provides mentorships to incoming

name: Organization of Urban and Regional Studies
description: It is the mission of the Organization of Urban and Regional Studies (OURS) at Cornell University to effectively and responsibly facilitate and maintain four primary activities: Forming a community among the undergraduate students in the Urban & Regional Studies program in the College of Architecture, Art, and Planning. Giving students a wider perspective of the field of urban and regional studies through hands-on urban experience. Providing a voice for undergraduate students in City & Regional Planning Department affairs. Acting as a resource for students to connect students to alumni, interns

name: Orthodox Christian Fellowship
description: The Orthodox Christian Fellowship (OCF) is the official collegiate campus ministry program under the Assembly of Canonical Orthodox Bishops of North and Central America. Our mission is to support fellowships on college campuses, whose members experience and witness to the Orthodox Christian Church through community life, prayer, service to others and study of the Faith.

name: Outdoor Odyssey
description: Outdoor Odyssey is a completely student run organization designed to help incoming Cornell freshmen and transfer students adjust to a new college experience. The program offers a variety of outdoor preorientation programs, led by specially trained upperclassmen guides, each August. Odyssey strives to maintain inclusivity and welcomes participants of all levels of outdoor experience.

name: Outing Club at Cornell
description: Since 1928, Cornell Outing Club has been helping Cornellians get outside and enjoy the outdoors. Whether you're interested in learning a new activity, developing your outdoors skills, or meeting other people who share your passion for outdoor adventure, there's a place in the Cornell Outing Club for you.

name: Pakistani Students Association
description: Our student organization is dedicated to amplifying the voices of Pakistani students at Cornell and beyond. We're passionate about fostering unity among the youth of the Subcontinent and challenging prevailing stereotypes, along with creating a safe and welcoming space for Pakistani students to meet one another.

name: Pan-African Muslim Student Association
description: Cornell PAMSA is Cornell University's Black Muslim Student Organization dedicated to creating a community for Black Muslims on campus. To create this community, PAMSA will provide a space for the education and discussion of the cultural, political, and social landscape of the Muslim and Black Diaspora convergence.

name: Pan-African Students Association
description: The Pan-African Students Association (PASA) aspires to foster a strong solidarity among pan-African people, scholars and all those interested in African culture and developmental issues. PASA hopes to create awareness of the rich cultural diversity, history and present state of Africa through its programs and events and in collaborations with other groups and institutions.

name: Pandaemonium Germanicum
description: 1. To foster the social and intellectual environment of graduate students in the Department of German Studies. 2. To represent the interests and concerns of graduate students in the Department of German Studies. 3. To participate in the social and intellectual life of the university. 4. To promote a critical understanding of German Studies. 5. To address and support the professional development of future academics in the discipline of German Studies.

name: Pandora Dance Troupe
description: A student-led, student-choreographed dance troupe, Pandora specializes in contemporary, ballet, modern, jazz, lyrical and hip hop. Our troupe puts together a showcase every fall, and participates in a number of guest performances throughout the year. Every spring, Pandora hosts "Spring into Motion" and invites several campus organizations to join them in performing at this annual benefit concert.

name: Pangea Club at Cornell
description: The mission of the PCC shall be to disseminate knowledge related to Earth and atmospheric sciences, such as, but not limited to, the structure and history of the Earth, as well as to explore local geological phenomena that has shaped, and continues to shape, Ithaca and the greater Finger Lakes region through interactive and hands-on field trips.

name: Panhellenic Association at Cornell University
description: The official name of this organization is the Cornell Panhellenic Association, and the Panhellenic Council is the governing organization of the 11 Panhellenic sorority chapters at Cornell. The purpose of the Panhellenic Association shall be to develop and maintain women's fraternity life and interfraterity relations at a high level of accomplishment.

name: Pants Improv Comedy
description: To teach and perform improvisational comedy and to encourage and celebrate enthusiasm for improv in the Cornell and Ithaca community.

name: Parkinson's Pals
description: Our mission is to pair Parkinson's patients with an undergraduate student to alleviate the social isolation and depression felt amongst Parkinson's patients. It is noted that nearly 55% of Parkinson's patients experience some form of depression. By fostering intergenerational connections, we hope to provide a new face and friend for patients.

name: PATCH - Pre-Professional Association Toward Careers in Health
description: PATCH is an organization within the College of Human Ecology that strives to help pre-health students develop their abilities, potential, and passions as they explore human health careers and prepare for medical or graduate school. Through participating in community outreach activities, students can expect to develop leadership, collaboration, and problem-solving skills. PATCH brings together pre-health students in a supportive, educational atmosphere that fosters growth and development through intellectual conversations and faculty interaction, encourages health career exploration and diversi

name: Paul Rubacha Department of Real Estate
Peace Action Chapter at Cornell
description: To practice different aspects of peace and understanding among a diverse group of students as it relates to nuclear disarmament and environmental impacts.

name: Pelvic Pain Association at Cornell
description: The Pelvic Pain Association at Cornell (PPAC) promotes solidarity and activism around reproductive health issues. We are inclusive of many different conditions that may cause chronic pelvic pain, including PCOS, endometriosis, adenomyosis, vulvodynia, IBS, ovarian cysts, uterine fibroids, and many others, including undiagnosed conditions. We are not a provider of health care advice or affiliated with any other pelvic pain organization.

name: Perfect Match
description: The purpose of the organization is to develop a matching algorithm for Cornell students to meet each other based on interests and similarities. The matching service will commence annually every February followed by a meet and greet event.

name: Perfect Pair Cornell Chapter
description: Perfect Pair fosters one-on-one, intergenerational connections between older adults and college students. We strive to reinforce a mutual sense of community and purpose for our pairs: a goal that underlies our efforts to combat loneliness and improve overall health and wellbeing. We achieve this by ensuring that our pair connections are personalized: based on shared background and interests. Simultaneously, we encourage pairs to re-engage with their passions by offering individualized and accessible programming. We hope for older adults and students to feel that their life perspective and qual

name: PERIOD at CORNELL
description: We are a group of young activists united by the belief that menstrual care is a basic right. Our mission is to celebrate periods and provide products to those in need. Service, education, and advocacy are the three pillars of our organization.

name: Persian Students Organization
description: The Persian Students Organization (PSO) aims to build a community for Persian undergraduate students at Cornell by hosting events promoting Persian culture, engaging in international philanthropic activities, and fostering learning about Iran and the Iranian people on campus. The PSO shall be free and open to everyone, regardless of race, gender, ethnicity, beliefs, etc. The PSO is not religiously or politically affiliated.

name: Ph2
description: The purpose of our organization is to bring together graduate Linguistics students interested in Phonetics and Phonology. During our meetings, we read articles, practice conference talks, learn new academic skills, and more. We will also organize academic events where we invite guest speakers to give talks and hold meetings with students, as well as social events where students can get to know their peers and faculty better.

name: Phenomenon Step Club
description: Phenomenon Step Team's purpose is to spread the culture and history of stepping throughout the Cornell campus. This tradition dates back to South African Gumboot dance and lives through stepping, especially in the Black community, as a powerful form of expression, unity, and history.

name: Phi Alpha Delta Pre-Law Fraternity
description: Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity (PAD) was founded on November 4, 1897. Since then, the organization's network has grown to make it the largest organization of lawyers and pre-law students in the world: 1 in 6 lawyers in the United States is a card-carrying member of PAD The Cornell pre-law chapter of Phi Alpha Delta is the largest pre-law organization at Cornell University. Our chapter has over 60 members and an extensive alumni network. Our alumni are law students at Harvard, Stanford, NYU, UPenn, Cornell, among others. Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity, International is a professional law frater

name: Phi Beta Sigma
description: Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity was founded at Howard University in Washington, D.C., January 9, 1914, by three young African-American male students. The Founders, Honorable A. Langston Taylor, Honorable Leonard F. Morse, and Honorable Charles I. Brown, wanted to organize a Greek letter fraternity that would truly exemplify the ideals of brotherhood, scholarship, and service. The Founders deeply wished to create an organization that viewed itself as "a part of" the general community rather than "apart from" the general community. They believed that each potential member should be judged by his own m

name: Phi Chi Theta
description: "To promote the cause of higher business education and training for all individuals, to foster high ideals for everyone pursuing a career in business; to encourage fraternity and cooperation among people preparing for such careers; and to stimulate the spirit of sacrifice and unselfish devotion to the attainment of such ends."

name: Phi Delta Epsilon International Medical Fraternity
description: Phi Delta Epsilon International Medical Fraternity creates physicians of integrity with a life-long commitment to our guiding principles of philanthropy, deity, and education through fellowship, service, mentoring, and formal training in leadership, science, and ethics.

name: Phi Gamma Delta
description: We seek to uphold our core values which include Friendship, Knowledge, Service, Morality, and Excellence. Members are encouraged to live by three priorities by these respective order: scholarship, fraternity, and self.

name: Phi Gamma Nu Professional Business Fraternity
description: Phi Gamma Nu at Cornell proudly upholds Three National Pillars which represent the underlying ideals of the fraternity. As such, events and activities organized by Phi Gamma Nu brothers work to fulfill these goals in practice. Through Professionalism, Phi Gamma Nu at Cornell seeks to constantly spread interest in the business field throughout college campuses. To this end, the National Board promotes the chapters' organization of creative professional events including networking workshops and speaker events. Through Philanthropy, Phi Gamma Nu chapters are able to build strong bonds with their

name: Phi Kappa Tau
description: The mission of Phi Kappa Tau is to champion a lifelong commitment to brotherhood, learning, ethical leadership and exemplary character.

name: Phi Sigma Pi National Honors Fraternity- Beta Nu Chapter
description: We consecrate ourselves to a life of social service with the goal of improving humanity through our principles: Scholarship, Leadership, and Fellowship.

name: Phoenix Society at Cornell
description: Reimagine, redesign, and build anew a phoenix for Dragon Day in an inclusive learning environment to build skills, gain knowledge and develop teamwork. This will be a yearlong effort starting in the fall semester each year.

name: Physics Graduate Society
description: To foster social wellbeing in the physics graduate community.

name: Pi Alpha Xi
description: The mission of this Honor Society is 1) to recognize high scholarship, 2) to foster good relationships among its members, 3) to promote or to facilitate the exchange of ideas among members of the professions, and 4) to establish cordial relations among students, educators and industry members.

name: Pi Beta Phi
description: The mission of Pi Beta Phi Fraternity for Women is to promote friendship, develop women of intellect and integrity, cultivate leadership potential and enrich lives through community service. In March of 1918, the Beta Phi Fraternity was founded here at Cornell University. Under the supervision of Miss Louise Case, Beta Phi began working toward its goal of petitioning for a charter of Pi Beta Phi. The future 13 charter members had to submit to the closest investigation as to character, activities, scholarship, and personality. These women were as follows: Helen Miriam Sharrett, Margaret Lounsbu

name: Pi Delta Psi
description: Pi Delta Psi is an Asian-interest cultural Fraternity founded on February 20, 1994 at Binghamton University in Binghamton, New York. Since our founding, the primary mission of Pi Delta Psi has been to spread Asian American Cultural awareness in an effort to empower the entire Asian American community. We are guided by four pillars; Academic Achievement, Cultural Awareness, Righteousness, and Friendship/Loyalty.

name: Pi Kappa Alpha
description: PIKE was recolonized in the Spring of 2013 with about 70 men. Pi Kappa Alpha is dedicated to developing men of integrity, intellect, and high moral character and to fostering a truly lifelong fraternal experience. To fulfill this mission, Pi Kappa Alpha will: Ôû¬ Encourage all our members to live the values taught in our ritual. Ôû¬ Provide innovative services and programs designed to enrich the lives of our undergraduates, alumni, and communities. Ôû¬ Create opportunities for our undergraduate and alumni members to participate in the life of Pi Kappa Alpha on a daily basis. Ôû¬ Promote and fo

name: Pi Kappa Phi
description: For over 100 years Pi Kappa Phi has been building better men on college campuses across the country. From our humble roots at the College of Charleston to over 131 campuses today, Pi Kappa Phi stands for a commitment to fundamental values. We are a first CLASS fraternity which firmly believes in the tenets of Character, Leadership, Academics, Sportsmanship, and Service. These principles are not only valued but instilled through leading-edge educational, service and leadership opportunities. Here at Cornell, The Psi Chapter of Pi Kappa Phi upholds the highest traditions of CLASS, with the drive

name: Pi Lambda Sigma
description: Pi Lambda Sigma (POLIS, for short) aims to promote, deepen, and advance the interests of students passionate about pursuing careers in or related to government, politics, and policy. A "pre-government student" is defined as any student looking to be employed by a government (at any level or location) or contract for, advocate, or lobby the government as the principal focus of their career.

name: Pi Sigma Epsilon
description: The Pi Sigma Epsilon Zeta Alpha chapter was founded in 2011 by Cornell students who wanted to form a business fraternity focused on a wide range of business fields. This business fraternity has a national focus on sales and marketing but we emphasize a diversity of interests within business. This has enabled us to attract students with a wide range of career goals and interests, thus expanding our campus and alumni networks. Our alumni have played a major role in the founding and growth of PSE, and thus have a very close tie to the roots of our fraternity. Our brothers are constantly reaching

name: Piano Society at Cornell
description: The Piano Society at Cornell provides a community for pianists and piano fans in the Cornell community of all ages, abilities, and interests. We provide member-to-member lessons to help beginners sharpen their skills and to help intermediate students keep up with their practicing and performing. We hold formal and informal concerts throughout the year. We host various social events to foster a community of people on campus who love piano. We collaborate with other organizations on campus who are looking for pianists. We connect our members with resources on campus including university lessons,

name: Planned Parenthood Generation Action
description: Planned Parenthood Generation Action works with Planned Parenthood of Greater New York to educate students on sexual health and engage them on the issues that threaten their access to reproductive health care. We aim to make Cornell a safer, healthier, and more informed community.

name: Plant Biology Graduate Student Association
description: Coagulation. Community to inspire. Meeting of the minds.

name: Plant Pathology Graduate Student Association
description: This organization exists to represent and promote the professional activities of graduate students and to facilitate communication among graduate students and between graduate students and faculty of the Field of Plant Pathology and Plant-Microbe Biology at Cornell University. The PPGSA also serves as a grievance board for the students and is actively involved in improving the conditions for graduate study in the department.

name: Pole Posse
description: This organization works to provide instruction in pole dancing. Although pole dancing is increasingly seen as a sport or fitness routine, we aim to prioritize its origins in our practice of it. Sex workers and other workers in ''informal" or "alternative" professions were practicing and cultivating pole dancing long before it become more mainstream. We believe that the active attempt to verbally cleanse pole dancing by separating it from its origins in sex work enacts violence upon this marginalized group. As a club, we refuse to indulge in this cleansing by exclusively invoking pole dancing a

name: Political Strategy Group at Cornell
description: Political Strategy Group at Cornell provides pro-bono analysis and strategic advisory to political campaigns and activist organizations, while instilling the value of civic engagement in the next generation of leaders.

name: Pre-collegiate Summer Scholars Program
description: The Pre-Collegiate Summer Scholars Program (PSSP) is designed to help you prepare for your first year at Cornell.

name: Pre-Dental Society at Cornell
description: Our mission is to foster a community at Cornell for all students who are curious or seriously considering a profession in dentistry.

name: Pre-Physician Assistant Association at Cornell
description: The mission of PPAAC is to cultivate an engaging and intentional community among students at Cornell who are interested and/or actively pursuing a career as a physician assistant (PA). PPAAC empowers members to advance their academic and professional path in the medical field with the goal of improving the quality and accessibility of healthcare.

name: Pre-Veterinary Society
description: The Pre-Veterinary Society is organized to provide a support network and pre-professional network for pre-vet students at Cornell. This includes seminars, contacts for important faculty members, advising for classes and applications, and hosting events during the year for local causes.

name: Prison Reform and Education Project (PREP)
description: To advocate on behalf of legislative reform, educate students on relevant issues, and integrate existing organizations to work for prison reform in the United States.

name: Pro-Yos
description: The purpose of the Pro-Yos shall be to promote a caring and inclusive community of members dedicated to learning and performing the diabolo, also known as the Chinese yoyo. The Pro-Yos shall promote public awareness of diabolo and engage the Cornell community and the surrounding Ithaca area community, through regular performances during the course of each academic year at events and showcases.

name: Professional Development of Women at Cornell University
description: PDOW is an all-female-led organization with the purpose of equipping women on campus with valuable personal finance knowledge and skills, like budgeting and investing, that go beyond the classroom setting. PDOW also introduces members to various career paths within the business world, which they can pursue upon graduating from Cornell, and helps prepare member for the job interview and application process.

name: Professional Fraternity Council
description: The purpose of this council is to maintain the system of PFOs, connect the PFOs in their individual points of action, support the recruitment of new members to PFOs, build relationships and networks between its PFO members, support mutual efforts of fundraising by the PFOs, and provide professional opportunities to the members of the PFOs, general student body, and community at large.

name: Program for Research on Youth Development and Engagement
Program Houses at Cornell
description: Program Houses offer students a higher level of community engagement than non-themed halls, shared through a special interest, life style, or culture. These close-knit communities are made of upper level and new students.

name: Project Generations
description: Project Generations aims to bridge the gap between the student and elderly population by matching students to senior citizens in the Ithaca community. Through a weekly, one-on-one volunteer visit, Project Generations allows students to build close friendships with their seniors, who may otherwise have not had a friendly visitor to spend time with.

name: Project Hope at Cornell
description: To promote awareness and to improve the quality of education for children facing poverty in rural areas of China and Hong Kong.

name: Project Level The Field Cornell Chapter
description: The purpose of Project Level The Field shall be to empower students to reach their full academic potential by providing high-quality resources free of charge. Project Level The Field believe that every individual, regardless of their background or financial situation, should have access to the tools and information needed to excel in their educational journey. Project Level The Field Cornell Chapter shall reflect the same mission as Project Level The Field, Inc.

name: Project Smile Global Cornell
description: Project Smile Global is a national student-led 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to fighting oral health disparities worldwide. Our mission is to provide access to oral healthcare for underprivileged communities around the globe. We are a team of dedicated volunteers who believe that everyone deserves a healthy smile. We work towards this goal by organizing dental events, providing basic oral care education, and advocating for better oral health policies at the local and national levels. Join us in restoring confidence through healthier smiles. Starting a PSG chapter at Cornell would

name: Prospect of Whitby
description: The Prospect of Whitby has been a cooperative house at Cornell University since 1965. We are dedicated to social justice, inclusion, and creating a safe living space for people with diverse life experiences.

name: Protestant Cooperative Ministry at Cornell
description: PCM is an ecumenical Christian campus ministry program supported by the Presbyterian Church (USA), the United Methodist Church, the United Church of Christ and the American Baptist Church. We hold Sunday services in the Chapel in Anabel Taylor Hall at 11 AM. In addition to Sunday services, PCM has also organized a pick-up choir, service trips, Sunday discussions, and participation in community service and events.

name: Proyecto Palante
description: Our mission is to honor and share Latino culture with the Cornell community through diverse dance techniques, programming, and music.

name: Psi Chi the International Honors Society in Psychology
description: Psi Chi is an international honor society whose purpose shall be to encourage, stimulate, and maintain excellence in scholarship of the individual members in all fields, particularly in psychology, and to advance the science of psychology.

name: PUBPOL 2301: Introduction to Public Policy / Brooks School of Public Policy
Puerto Rican Student Association
description: The Puerto Rican Student Association was created with the purpose of fostering a sense of community among Puerto Rican undergraduate and graduate students at Cornell University. PRSA coordinates and sponsors culturally and politically educational activities regarding Puerto Rican issues and promotes and develops programs that will seek the involvement of Puerto Rican students and the greater Latino community at Cornell. PRSA strives to foster a support network of Puerto Rican alumni, thereby uplifting the Puerto Rican community at Cornell and throughout future endeavors.

name: PulseGuard at Cornell University
description: To educate members of the Cornell community around the use of compressions-only CPR. PulseGuard will maintain communication with CUEMS on this type of education sharing.

name: Puppet Club
description: To provide a creative, low-stress space for Cornell students to create and perform with puppets.

name: QGrads
description: QGrads strives: (a) To build a strong community at Cornell by creating spaces for graduate students of all sexual orientations and gender identities to feel heard, seen, and supported. (b) To plan events and programming that promote the personal and professional development of graduate students of all sexual orientations and gender identities. (c) To actively address the needs of our members. (d) To advocate for social justice on and off campus.

name: qSTEM
description: The mission of qSTEM is to promote the social and professional development of LGBTQ+ students of Cornell University who are interested in STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) fields.

name: Quant Fund at Cornell
description: The purpose of Quant Fund at Cornell is to foster a community of innovators to explore cutting-edge developments in quantitative finance. The complex nature of financial markets necessitates innovation upon traditional investing approaches. By fully utilizing the latest technology, the quantitative approach makes financial analysis less subjective and more precise.

name: Quantum Computing Association
description: The Quantum Computing Association at Cornell (Cornell QCA) aims to inspire interest in Quantum Information Science and equip students with the background and skills necessary to participate in the field. We teach an introductory lecture series, host events, and pursue research with project members, allowing students of all experience levels to learn and contribute to the rapidly growing quantum computing industry.

name: Queery
description: Queery is focused on empowering queer individuals, questioning individuals and their allies interested in the tech field at Cornell.

name: Quill & Dagger
description: Quill & Dagger is a senior honor society at Cornell University that recognizes undergraduate students for leadership, character, and service.

name: Quisqueya: Dominican Students' Association
description: Quisqueya—The Dominican Students Association—was founded at Cornell University in 1995 with the intention of spreading awareness concerning the Dominican experience and culture.

name: Quiz Bowl Club, Cornell
description: The Quiz Bowl Club provides an enjoyable, supplementary learning experience for Cornellians through the collective playing of quizbowl questions. We are primarily recreational, though the game is inherently competitive. We represent Cornell at quizbowl tournaments held at universities across the Northeast several times per semester, and usually send one or two teams to national competitions. For more information on college quizbowl, you can check out https://acf-quizbowl.com/. No prior experience is necessary to enjoy the game.

name: Quodlibet
description: To provide a lively forum for all those interested in all things medieval on campus. To organize a series of lectures to highlight current research topics relating to medieval studies.

name: Rainy Day
description: Rainy Day is the longest running literary magazine on the Cornell University campus, publishing a biannual magazine presenting the finest student literary works to the widest audience possible. We are a cooperative group of editors who critique work through interactive meetings. Our staff members come from myriad backgrounds: Economics, Biology, Philosophy, English and other majors. We have been publishing for 50 years at Cornell and were founded by Professor Kenneth A. McClane who is now W.E.B. Du Bois Professor of Literature Emeritus and who said in our 30th anniversary issue, "Rainy Day mig

name: Raptor Program at Cornell
description: It shall be the purpose of CRP to care for, rehabilitate, and manage a variety of captive raptor species. It shall train students in the proper care and handling of raptors. It shall engage the campus and greater community through formal and informal education programs designed to teach audiences about raptor biology and conservation. It shall select species for propagation and appropriately pair breeding individuals.

name: REACH - Raising Education Attainment Challenge
description: REACH is a service-learning organization that focuses on tutoring and mentoring students in and around Ithaca. We love volunteering and working with students to better their learning experiences.

name: REAL A Cappella Group
description: The purpose of Cornell REAL A Cappella shall be to spread Chinese musical culture and create a platform for Chinese students who love singing, performing, music arranging, and video recording to produce music videos, albums, and good-quality live performances.

name: Real Estate Development and Investment Trust at Cornell
description: CREDIT is an organization committed to enabling undergraduate students with education in the development and investment opportunities within the real estate industry. CREDIT will expose a selective group of committed students to advanced business strategies to maximize their real estate education using both theoretical pedagogy and practical experience.

name: Recreational Fencing Club
description: Provide opportunities for Olympic style fencing in a welcoming and motivational atmosphere.

name: Recreational Tennis Club
description: Our club provides a resource for students to have fun playing tennis outside of a competitive or selective environment. We help students find people to play with or similar skill levels and offer opportunities for beginners to learn and others to improve.

name: Red Key Athlete Honor Society
description: To recognize outstanding undergraduate contributors to both Cornell athletics and the Cornell community. We value academic achievement, propagation of fellowship and strong loyalty amongst all Cornell athletes, and enhancement of the Cornell and Ithaca communities through service.

name: Redbud Cooperative
description: Statement on the Cooperative Identity A cooperative is an autonomous association of persons united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social, and cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly-owned and democratically- controlled enterprise. Cooperatives are based on the values of self-help, self-responsibility, democracy, equality, equity, and solidarity. In the tradition of their founders, co-operative members believe in the ethical values of honesty, openness, social responsibility, and caring for others. The cooperative principles are guidelines by which co-operatives put their v

name: Remote Area Medical Cornell Chapter
description: The purpose of Remote Area Medical Cornell University Chapter shall be to provide free, high-quality medical, dental, and vision care to those in need regardless of income, identification, or insurance. Doing so will provide Cornell students the opportunity to learn from professionals and patients in a variety of settings across the U.S. and support the care of patients who would not otherwise receive services. Cornell students will take part in non-clinical volunteer roles under the guidance of a team lead, such as checking patients in, translating, and directing patients to treatment.

name: Reserve Tennis Club at Cornell
description: The Cornell Reserve Tennis Club is intended for intermediate and advanced tennis players who want to play regular tennis with a group of similar players. You are a perfect candidate for this club if you A) played tennis regularly in high school, but now find yourself struggling to make time for tennis or find hitting buddies, B) tried out for the Cornell Tennis Club and didn't make it, or C) played tennis casually in the past and want to improve. We practice multiple times a week and also play several matches against other area colleges each semester. Our goal is to create a small, close commu

name: Residence Hall Association
description: A. Promote and foster a sense of cohesion within the campus residential community; B. Provide training for residential community leaders in the areas of leadership, communication, representation, programming, advocacy, and personal and community development; C. Involve its members as active participants in the process of self-governance; D. Provide a forum in order to communicate and exchange ideas, as well as voice concerns about residential community life; E. Provide programs and activities through which its members may have the opportunity to grow and develop emotionally, physically, academ

name: Residential Life, SCL
description: Residential Life furthers the academic mission of Cornell University and the principles outlined in the First Year Experience model. By providing a safe, diverse, purposeful living and learning environment aligned with these values, we support student involvement and active citizenship. Through partnerships with university faculty and staff, we foster students' personal growth, critical thinking, intellectual engagement, and social responsibility.

name: Residential Sustainability Leaders
description: The purpose of the Residential Sustainability Leaders shall be to create a culture of sustainability within Cornell's residential communities. This is accomplished by building a bridge between Cornell students and the University in a leadership program focused on increasing knowledge of sustainability. Our team focuses on the advancement of environmental justice principles, peer-to-peer education, program planning and evaluation, and providing a sense of place and belonging to enact meaningful, sustainable change within the Cornell community.

name: Rho Psi Eta Delta Chapter
description: Rho Psi Eta is dedicated to fostering a community of like-minded women who are passionate about pursuing a career in a health-related field.

name: Rhythm Gaming at Cornell
description: The mission of Rhythm Gaming at Cornell shall be to establish a space for the enjoyment and appreciation of rhythm games, both for people who already are entrenched in the scene as well as to help new people get interested and get involved.

name: Ring of Steel: Ithaca
description: Ring of Steel: Ithaca is a theatrical stunt group created to bring the "art of stage violence" to Cornell University and Ithaca College students as well as the Ithaca community via teaching and performances. Members begin their training using bokken (or boken) and then advance to steel swords. We study rapier, rapier and dagger, broadsword, quarterstaff, and hand-to-hand combat. The club began in Spring 2003 and is a chapter of the The Ring of Steel Action Theatre located in Ann Arbor, MI.

name: Rise Dance Group
description: Rise Dance Group aims to extend the opportunity of dance to all Cornell students who seek to continue their passion for dance. Our group is open to many styles and backgrounds, performing routines in styles such as contemporary, jazz, and many more based on our dancers' interests. We are a close group of friends who not only enjoy dance but are an involved part of the amazing dance community at Cornell.

name: RISEUP (Realizing Integration, Support, and Education for Underserved Populations) at Cornell
description: The purpose of RISEUP shall be to empower underserved populations, primarily refugees, immigrants, and asylum seekers, through comprehensive educational initiatives and resources aimed at reducing healthcare disparities.

name: Risley Ministry for Arts and Shops Development
description: Within Risley, The Shops have historically been student run, allowing all possible creativity and use. However, student safety is at risk without proper training and knowledge. Therefore, we have created The Risley Ministry of Arts and Shops to balance student safety and student use.
