name: Robotics Graduate Student Organization
description: The purpose of this organization is to foster fellowship between labs and members of the Cornell graduate student robotics community and beyond, independent of department affiliation.

name: Rock Climbing Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of our organization is to further develop Cornell's recreational and competitive rock climbing community. Through training, we seek to improve our climbing abilities, compete in official USAC competitions, compete in informal local competitions, and take climbing trips to outdoor locations.

name: Rocketry at Cornell
description: The Cornell Rocketry Team designs, manufactures and tests a high-powered rocket every year for competition in the Spaceport America Cup. We travel to IREC in Midland, TX to compete against 150 other collegiate teams from 22 different countries. The primary goal at competition is to launch the rocket to exactly 10,000 feet using our Student Research and Developed (SRAD) hybrid rocket motor. Every year, our rocket carries with it a unique scientific payload that leverages the high altitude or high acceleration environment onboard the rocket. The team designs and manufactures almost every part of

name: Romanian Student Association at Cornell
description: The Romanian Student Association at Cornell seeks to bring together international Romanian and Romanian-American students, giving everyone a chance to delve deeper into Romanian culture, history, traditions, and more. Our association aims to bridge the connection between Romanian students and the broader Cornell community while offering support to new students arriving from Romania. RSA promotes cultural awareness and diversity on campus by organizing social, cultural, and educational events that celebrate Romanian heritage. Membership in RSA is open to all Romanian students and to anyone in t

name: Roper Center for Public Opinion Research
Rotaract
description: Rotaract is the college level representative of Rotary International, whose motto is "Service Above Self." We spread their message by providing opportunities for members of the Cornell community to engage in service and volunteering.

name: Running Club at Cornell
description: Cornell Running Club was founded to promote the sport of running at Cornell. We meet regularly at 5PM in front of Goldwin Smith Hall on weekdays, and in the same location at 4:15PM once daylight saving time ends. The club's aim is to provide a safe, social environment for Cornell community members who would otherwise run alone. Members receive email updates about social activities, competitions, and club proceedings such as elections, and can also join our Slack for more frequent updates. The club welcomes runners of all experience levels and our runs vary from 3 to 10 miles or more at a varie

name: Sabor Latino Dance Ensemble
description: Sabor's mission is to represent our Latin American, Caribbean, and African roots through dances as well as our ties to our experience as Latinos in the U.S. Through our annual concert, guest dance performances, and community service, we present the significance of music and dance in our Latino cultures. Sabor has four pillars: Culture, Community, Self-Expression and Family which we foster by doing what we love best which is dancing, bonding with other communities across Cornell's campus and most importantly, educating the community around us.

name: SAGES - Student Association of the Geneva Experiment Station
description: The Student Association of the Geneva Experiment Station (SAGES) is led by students pursing Master's and Doctorate degrees in the agricultural sciences and holds events open to the entire Cornell AgriTech at The New York State Agriculture Experiment Station Community. SAGES exists to promote leadership, to encourage the study of agricultural issues relevant to the State of New York, and to promote a better relationship between the Station and the population of the city of Geneva and surrounding communities. Members have an expressed interest in the advancement of the agricultural sciences thro

name: Sailing Club at Cornell
description: A competitive sailboat racing team that competes throughout the Inter-collegiate sailing association (ICSA).

name: Salsa ¡Pa’lante! Casineros at Cornell
description: Salsa ¡Pa’lante! Casineros at Cornell, established in 2004, is dedicated to enhancing and growing the Latin dance community at Cornell University by performing Salsa Casino choreographies and improvised Rueda de Casino demonstrations and by offering Salsa Casino lessons. “Casino” is a Cuban dance commonly identified as “Salsa” or “Cuban Salsa” in the United States. When our organization uses the term “Salsa Casino,” we refer to what Casino means in its original Cuban form while acknowledging its overlap with Salsa and the semantic nuance that exists in the Latin dance community more broadly. name: Saudi Students Association
description: The Saudi Student Association at Cornell (SaudiSA) celebrates and promotes the Saudi Arabian culture, history, and tradition throughout the Cornell and Ithaca community by organizing and hosting relevant events and activities. SaudiSA also gathers and represents all current and alumni Cornell Saudi students and addresses their needs and concerns.

name: SC Johnson College of Business Minors
description: The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business offers nine minors, each open to eligible undergraduate students at Cornell University.

name: Scabbard & Blade Society
description: Believing that military service is an obligation of citizenship, and that the greater opportunities afforded college men and women for the study of military science give them certain responsibilities as citizens, we, as cadet officers in various colleges and universities conferring baccalaureate degrees, do form this society and adopt this constitution in order to unite in closer relationship the military departments of American universities and colleges; to preserve and develop the essential qualities of good and efficient officers; to prepare ourselves as educated men and women to take a mor

name: Scholars of Finance - Cornell Chapter
description: Inspire character and integrity in the finance leaders of tomorrow.

name: Scholars Working Ambitiously to Graduate
description: Scholars Working Ambitiously to Graduate (SWAG) is a mentorship program designed to increase retention and graduation rates among men of color at Cornell University. We achieve this goal through academic enrichment, professional development, and community building.

name: School of Civil & Environmental Engineering
description: We discover and develop new knowledge and sustainable technologies that improve the practice of civil and environmental engineering in service to society. We educate future creators and innovators who will employ their grounding in science and engineering to become leaders in many spheres of society. We strive to create the knowledge necessary to transform the art and practice of civil and environmental engineering for all segments of society through sustainable and resilient systems and solutions. Central to this vision is the fostering of a new generation of leaders with the knowledge, creat

name: School of Operations Research and Information Engineering
Science & Technology Studies Graduate Student Association
description: The purpose of the organization is to work on behalf of the graduate students in the Department of Science and Technology Studies at Cornell. We organize beginning of the year and end of the year events to introduce graduate students to each other and to build our community. We also bring in outside speakers and organize lunch and workshops with them. More recently, we have funded a writers' group which helps students in our department (and those from other departments who would like to join in) work on their writing projects through workshopping either dissertation chapters, journal articles,

name: Science and Technology Entry Program-Upward Partnership (STEP-UP)
description: STEP-UP strives to increase the exposure of underrepresented, marginalized and low income family high school students to scientific education (graduate and undergraduate). STEP-UP mission is to positively impact the high school student population in the Ithaca Area through outcome-based programming, scientific exposure, diversity initiatives and interactions with College and Graduate students. Additionally, we want to foster a community where we can discuss science related current events and increase the understanding of current scientific research.

name: Science Olympiad at Cornell
description: The purpose of Science Olympiad at Cornell is to organize members of the Cornell community to host an annual Science Olympiad invitational tournament at Cornell University for high school student teams. We also aim to volunteer both at secondary school Science Olympiad competitions in the Southern Tier and New York region as well as in the local community.

name: Seal and Serpent Society
description: The Society of the Seal and Serpent was founded to promote good fellowship among certain students of Cornell University, to establish ideals for newly entering students, to bind them together with a selfless spirit both in undergraduate life and life after graduation, and thus raise to a high standard their characters, morals, and scholarship.

name: SensTech
description: SensTech is a biomedical engineering project team that gives students hands-on experience in biosensor research, engineering design, business development, outreach, and biomedical science. Each year, the team participates in the international SensUs competition, where university teams develop biosensors in response to a healthcare-focused competition theme. Through this work, members from a broad range of majors and schools collaborate to design, build, test, and present a biosensor prototype and business model. SensTech aims to prepare students with real-world experience in interdisciplinary

name: Sephardi & Mizrahi Student Council
description: Our organization represents diverse histories of Sephardic and Mizrahi Jewish backgrounds. Our family stories derive from Spain/Portugal, Algeria, Egypt, Iraq, Iran, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Syria, Tunisia, and Yemen. Therefore, the purpose of the Sephardi & Mizrahi Council shall be to share our stories and values. We hope to celebrate the wisdom and warmth of our Sephardi & Mizrahi traditions and live the example of what these values have to offer to our greater Cornell University community.

name: Sexual Assault Prevention and Safety Club
description: SAPS’ mission is to create an in-house and inter-house support system for Cornell Greek Life members affected by sexual assault and harassment by institutionalizing interactive education, preventive measures, and communication regarding sexual violence. Namely, SAPS seeks to change the culture in Greek Life through moderated dialogues and discussion forums on the topic of SA, and how to understand, respond, and prevent it. SAPS seeks to create an institutionalized system that students can look to for years to come by passing down knowledge and committee responsibilities to the younger generati

name: Shadows Dance Troupe
description: Shadows Dance Troupe exists to provide Cornell students with the opportunity to dance and perform, with qualifications including experience, merit, enthusiasm, effort, and personal commitment. Shadows holds auditions twice a year: at the beginning of the fall semester and at the beginning of the spring semester. We are always looking for strong, talented dancers. If you are interested in auditioning, please look out for information on our Instagram (@shadowsdancetroupe) or contact one of our co-chairs!

name: Shake Ultimate
description: To field a strong ultimate team that can compete at a regional level while developing the skills and athleticism of all players and to promote a fun and inclusive environment for all.

name: Shimtah at Cornell
description: Our mission is to teach, share, and perform traditional Korean folk music within the Cornell and Ithaca community. We hope to promote the traditional musical aspect of Korean culture, and thus contribute to the cultural and ethnic diversity here at Cornell University. We wish to display the passion and skill of those in Shimtah, and in turn, the reasons for our dedication to this form of music. This club also provides opportunity for students of Korean heritage or those interested in Korean culture to form a social network.

name: Sigma Alpha Epsilon
description: To promote and exemplify our core values of scholarship, service, leadership, and friendship.

name: Sigma Alpha Mu
description: To foster and maintain among its sons a spirit of fraternity, a spirit of mutual moral aid and support; to instill and maintain in the hearts of its sons love for and loyalty to Alma Mater and its ideals; to inculcate among its sons such ideals as will result in actions worthy of the highest precepts of true manhood, democracy, and humanity.

name: Sigma Alpha Sorority
description: The objective of this sorority shall be to promote its members in all facets of agriculture and to strengthen the bonds of friendship among them. it is the purpose of its members to strive for achievement in scholarship, leadership, and service, and to further the development of excellence in women pursuing careers in agriculture.

name: Sigma Chi
description: Sigma Chi, the second largest fraternity in the nation, is one of the most influential and highly respected at Cornell. In our 105 years, the Alpha Phi chapter has been characterized by its tight-knit brotherhood and commitment to excellence in academics and athletics. Since 1925, Sigma Chi brothers have made their home in elegant Greystone Manor. The extensive grounds feature beautiful medieval stonework, and a park-like backyard complete with a spacious in-ground swimming pool and small gorge. name: Sigma Delta Tau
description: The mission of Sigma Delta Tau is to enrich the college experience of women of similar ideals, to build lasting friendships and to foster personal growth. Sigma Delta Tau shall encourage each member by providing intellectual, philanthropic, leadership and social opportunities within the framework of mutual respect and high ethical standards

name: Sigma Gamma Rho
description: It is the mission of Sigma Gamma Rho Sorority, Inc. to enhance the quality of life for women and their families in the U.S. and globally through community service, civil, and social action. Our goal is to achieve greater progress in the areas of education, health awareness, and leadership development. Our members, affiliates, staff, and community partners work to create and support initiatives that align with our vision.

name: Sigma Lambda Upsilon
description: In 1993, six women recognized a need for diversity and wanted to create a voice for women on their campus. name: Sigma Nu
description: To develop ethical leaders inspired by the principles of Love, Honor, and Truth. To foster the personal growth of each man's mind, heart, and character. To perpetuate lifelong friendships and commitment to the Fraternity.

Tau Phi Delta changed its name to The Sigma Pi Fraternity, United States in 1907 and began establishing new chapters that same year. name: SiGMA: Sibley Graduates in Mechanical & Aerospace
description: SiGMA is made up of the Graduate students in the Sibley School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. This group fosters a strong community among the graduate students by facilitating social, academic, and outreach events.

name: Sikh Students Association
description: Purpose and Aims: 1. The Cornell Sikh Students Association (CSSA) is a multi-purpose organization. It will serve as the voice of Sikh students on campus and allow them the opportunity to practice and express their faith at Cornell. 2. CSSA will serve as a platform for members, visitors and the greater student and public population to learn about and discuss Sikhi, as well as pioneer public awareness and education regarding (but not limited to) Sikhi's beliefs, identity, history and the significance of its festivals. name: Singapore Students Association
description: i. To create awareness of Singapore in the Cornell Community. ii. To provide opportunities for recreation and interaction among members and the Cornell community at large.

name: Sitara at Cornell
description: Sitara is Cornell's Premier Bollywood fusion competitive dance team performing in competition, showcases, and events here on campus and across the nation. STA strives to fuse elements of various dance styles and genres including Bollywood, hip hop, Indian Classical, Western Contemporary, and South Indian styles. Our mission is to promote a diverse and inclusive space to explore and celebrate our passion for dance and music.

name: Skateboarding Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of the Cornell Skateboarding Club is to organize all members of the Cornell Community who are interested in, already enamored of, or willing to learn about or participate in the sport of skateboarding into a cohesive, active, and vibrant community of skateboarders and skateboarding enthusiasts. We aim to provide equipment and obstacles for seasoned and beginning skateboarders alike, as well as frequent transportation to offcampus skateboarding locales in the Ithaca area and beyond. We also aim to educate folks who want to get into skateboarding but don't know how. One main goal is

name: Slope Day Programming Board
description: The Slope Day Programming Board serves as an organization through which students work with faculty, staff, and other community members in all colleges, departments, and divisions to plan and promote Slope Day. The Board promotes a day that fosters a safe and healthy environment with multiple social and recreational options. The group recruits and trains students for Slope Day to assist with monitoring, entertainment, food and beverage distribution, and other activities. The group will be responsible for use of appropriated student funds, pursuant to guidelines established by the Student Assemb

name: Social Business Consulting
description: The Social Business Consulting Group (SBC) is a non-profit consultancy comprised of Cornell students. Founded in 2007, we provide pro-bono consulting services to further the causes of social entrepreneurs globally, while gaining practical consulting and management experience. The services we offer currently touch on specialties ranging from business development and market-entry strategy to educational curriculum and evaluation studies – and our list of services is continuously expanding. We empower students to affect positive social change, while teaching the skills and nurturing the qualities

name: Social Enterprise at Cornell
description: SEC empowers students to build a career in social and environmental impact. We believe that every student brings a crucial perspective that can shape a brighter tomorrow, and keep our resources and events open to all! We hope to serve as a catalyst in three respects: Education. SEC provides educational resources so that students in a variety of professional pursuits can learn about impact investment, social consulting, social entrepreneurship, and social design. Innovation. SEC fosters creativity and supports innovative solutions to social and environmental problems through ideathons, workshop

name: Social Enterprise Group at Cornell
description: Social Enterprise Group at Cornell (SEGC) is an undergraduate consulting organization at Cornell University dedicated to market-driven solutions to social issues

description: The Society of Spanish Debating is an organization which seeks to teach debating skills to Spanish speaking students at Cornell. Its mission is to promote the Spanish language in Cornell, and train and teach to analyze rhetoric, logic, and proper presentation of arguments and positions in Spanish in hopes of creating community leaders, lawyers, and politicians who will be able to connect, understand, and better represent the Spanish speaking communities of the United States. Furthermore the Society of Spanish Debating will host and compete in debate tournaments that will be in the Spanish lang

name: Society for Advancement of Chicanos/Hispanics and Native Americans in Science at Cornell
description: SACNAS strives to promote diversity at Cornell by aiding the success of Chicano/Latino, Native American, and underrepresented students to pursue graduate education and obtain the advanced degrees. SACNAS's mission is to impact the student population through outcome-based programming and diversity initiatives that are necessary for advanced careers in science, research, and leadership positions in STEM.

name: Society for Buddhist Studies
description: Our mission is to promote the study of Buddhism at Cornell University.

name: Society for India
description: Society for India is Cornell University's Indian group on-campus and strives to promote Indian and the Indian diaspora's culture and awareness through various events. Our goal is to foster cross-cultural interaction transcending all geographical boundaries as well as providing a strong support system that thrives to provide personal and professional assistance to all Cornell students.

name: Society for Natural Resources Conservation
description: SNRC is a student-run organization committed to creating real environmental impact on campus and the surrounding community by identifying pressing challenges in natural resource conservation, cultivating informed dialogue and practical solutions, and inspiring collective action. SNRC confronts the environmental consequences of human consumption by turning awareness into responsibility and responsibility into action. Through education, advocacy, and direct hands-on engagement, SNRC empowers students across disciplines to protect natural resources, restore shared spaces, and strengthen a culture

name: Society for the Humanities
description: Established in 1966, the Cornell Society for the Humanities brings distinguished visiting fellows, Cornell faculty, and graduate student fellows together each year to pursue research on a rotating interdisciplinary focal theme. Legendary seminars and experimental, innovative courses fuel an unmatched research and learning environment.

name: Society for the Promotion of Indian Classical Music And Culture Amongst Youth
description: The mission of SPICMACAY at Cornell shall be to promote South Asian music and engage the Cornell community in the subcontinent’s deeply rich and diverse musical heritage. The goals of this organization shall be to uniquely introduce South Asian musical forms to campus, primarily through performance. We also hope to foster a musically-inclined community through weekly jamming sessions and at least one performance per semester.

name: Society for Women in Business
description: The Society for Women in Business (SWIB) connects students of all majors with each other and with professional leaders in the business world. We aim to empower talented and intelligent women through education and experience. Through research projects, panels, speaker events, skill-building workshops, and networking events, our goal is to provide our members with the tools to help them advance both personally and professionally.

name: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers
description: The Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers (SHPE), Inc. is a non-profit organization dedicated to increasing the participation of Hispanic professionals and college students in the fields of engineering, technology, science, and math.

name: Society of Horticulture Graduate Student Group
description: To provide a unified network of graduate students in the field of horticulture in order to support one another throughout our professional careers. In addition, we strive to promote greater appreciation and knowledge of horticulture in our community.

name: Society of Physics Students
description: To support, uplift, and advocate for the Cornell undergraduate physics community

name: Society of Women Engineers at Cornell University
description: The Cornell Student Section of the Society of Women Engineers promotes women in Engineering by advocating the importance of diversity and by uniting resources to encourage academic, leadership, professional, and personal excellence for the entire Engineering community.

name: Sociology Graduate Student Association
description: The Cornell Sociology Graduate Student Association (SGSA) began in 2003 to address the needs of Cornell sociology graduate students at each stage of the graduate program. The GSA has continued to be a vital part of the sociology graduate program at Cornell through the organization's active role in enhancing the educational, professional, and social interactions among our graduate students and faculty.

name: Soil and Crop Sciences Graduate Student Association
description: The goals of this organization are to promote a sense of community and professional development for graduate students and post docs within the Soil and Crop Sciences section.

name: Sorority & Fraternity Life
description: Sorority & Fraternity Life advocates for the fraternities and sororities in pursuit of fraternal ideals and serves as a resource to develop and educate leaders in a diverse, self-governed, living-learning environment. The vision of Sorority & Fraternity Life is to cultivate a model of distinction for fraternities and sororities through demonstrated success and innovative practices.

name: Soulaan Nation
description: SoulAAn Nation strives to foster cultural unity and understanding among the African American community at Cornell and bring awareness of African American culture to the larger Cornell community. We hope to provide a forum to celebrate the diversity embodied in the African American community through cultural events, educational seminars, publications, and community outreach programs. SoulAAn Nation aims to add a pillar to the broader cultural community, not take away from what’s already established.

name: Sounds of Spirit at Cornell
description: To create a space that embraces Christian values through culturally diverse music production. We hope to create an environment that is welcoming to all, inviting those to appreciation cultural diversity through music, seek meaning, and provide a reminder of home to those familiar to our melodies. The music we create and play will be from all parts of the world, with an emphasis on African diasporic gospel melodies, and incoporate an array of vocals and instrumentation.

name: South Asian Business Association
description: The organization would provide new members with a semester-long education process to help them explore different fields in business as well as have access to mentorship provided by current SABA students. The organization would also host various speaker, networking, and social events that would connect students with distinguished South Asian Cornell alumni to allow them to learn about career opportunities. The organization would also focus on celebrating South Asian culture through the context of business.

name: South Asian Council
description: We, the members of the South Asian community at Cornell University, do hereby establish the South Asian Council to serve as the umbrella organization for all organizations at Cornell University that are concerned with South Asian identity, representation, and issues. The South Asian Council will aim to raise awareness and advocate for South Asian interests, provide support for the South Asian community, and build collaborations internal and external to the community.

name: South East Asia Graduate Student Association
description: To bring together graduate students interested in and/or doing research with aerial concentration in South East Asia.

name: Southeast Asia Program
description: To promote the acquisition and dissemination of knowledge about countries, cultures, and languages of Southeast Asia.

name: Speech and Debate Society at Cornell University
description: The purpose of the Cornell Speech and Debate Society is to provide an opportunity for Cornell undergraduate students to compete in organized intercollegiate debate and speech competitions, as well as to conduct other activities associated with college forensics. The Cornell Speech and Debate Society is a registered student organization at Cornell University

name: Splash at Cornell
description: Splash! seeks to bring under-served, passionate 7th-12th graders to campus to expose them to higher education via courses taught by Cornell undergraduates, graduate students, and faculty members.

name: Spoon University Cornell Chapter
description: The purpose of Spoon University Cornell Chapter is to create a space where students can explore and share their passion for food through digital media and campus events. We aim to educate, inspire, and connect our community through content that highlights food culture, wellness, and creativity. The goals of this organization are to produce engaging food-related content, teach students about cooking and nutrition, and host events that celebrate diverse cuisines. We also aim to provide hands-on experience in writing, photography, video production, and social media management.

name: Sport Taekwondo at Cornell
description: We provide Cornell students with the opportunity to learn the martial art of taekwondo and compete in intercollegiate tournaments and other events.

name: Sports Analytics at Cornell
description: We are a group of students who are passionate about the growing role of analytics in professional and collegiate sports. We want to create an inclusive environment of diverse skill sets where students can research and discuss topics in the field.

name: Sports Business Society at Cornell
description: The Cornell Sports Business Society is Cornell's premier undergraduate student organization dedicated to involving our members in the sports industry and advancing the world of sports. We aim to engage members in the sports business community by preparing members to be active professionals. Our club supports this mission through six main activities: guest speakers and special events, weekly radio show, semesterly Sports Inc. magazine, club blog, club research department, and media development. Students from all Cornell colleges and majors are welcome to participate and become involved in SBS.

name: Sports Medicine Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of SPORTS MEDICINE CLUB AT CORNELL shall be to expose aspiring medical professionals to unique clinical experiences through Cornell’s Sports Medicine department and therefore encourage a greater understanding of a multidisciplinary healthcare approach and foster a collaborative learning environment that optimizes the care of athletes.

name: Squash Club at Cornell
description: The purpose of the Club is to form a community of squash players at Cornell for both recreational and competitive play. We strike a balance between the pressure and time commitment of varsity squash and the limited recreational play time associated with intramural squash. We play throughout the school year at Reis Tennis Center and Belkin Squash courts, where we aim to practice 2 times per week. In addition to practices, we host matches and travel to both club and varsity squash teams.

name: Sri Lankan Association at Cornell University
description: The Sri Lankan Association at Cornell University (SLACU) is dedicated to fostering a robust and inclusive network for the Sri Lankan community within Cornell. Our mission is to enrich the Cornell community through the promotion of Sri Lankan culture and heritage, while facilitating a seamless transition for incoming graduate students from Sri Lanka. We are committed to creating an inviting space that encourages cross-cultural engagement and understanding, thereby contributing to the vibrant diversity of the Cornell community.

name: Sri Lankan Students' Association
description: The purpose of this organization is to serve as a community for students of Sri Lankan ethnicity, as well as those interested in Sri Lankan culture. We hope to bring awareness of Sri Lankan culture to the Cornell body.

name: Startup Consulting at Cornell
description: Startup Consulting at Cornell is a student organization that advises startups across a diverse range of industries and functional areas. Through semester-long projects, our members learn valuable strategy consulting skills while driving a tangible impact on startups.

name: State of the Pod
description: State of the Pod was founded on the mission to inform and engage the public on emerging issues in science and technology. The podcast production seeks to foster scientific inquiry for both its participants and broader Ithaca community while offering an accessible platform for all students to develop the skills necessary to produce and host original content on the SOTP podcast.

name: Statistics Graduate Society at Cornell
description: The purpose of the SGS is to make all aspects of graduate student life in the field of Statistics -- academic, social, and professional -- more enjoyable, and is responsible for representing graduate students' concerns to The Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Graduate School, and The Cornell Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science.

name: Steel Bridge at Cornell
description: The purpose of Steel Bridge is to apply and enrich knowledge gained in the classroom, to become acquainted and to practice working together effectively, to learn to overcome the various challenges associated with designing an engineered project, and to create a successful end project.

name: Steminist Movement at Cornell
description: The Steminist Movement | Cornell seeks to mitigate the STEM gender gap by fostering a community around creating and providing free STEM education to middle school girls as a college chapter of the greater nonprofit The Steminist Movement, Inc.

name: Student & Campus Life
description: Student & Campus Life serves all Cornell students - undergraduate, graduate, and professional - and strives to promote an educational environment where you can thrive in pursuit of your academic and personal goals.

name: Student Activities Funding Commission
description: The SAFC allocates funds to nearly 750 undergraduate student organizations. Our mission is to support undergraduate organizations in their ability to foster community and belonging at Cornell through funding opportunities.

name: Student Assembly
description: The object of this assembly shall be to effect more extensive involvement in campus governance in the undergraduate student body. This is accomplished by charging the assembly with the authority and the responsibility to examine any matters which involve the interests or concern the welfare of the student community and to make proposals concerning those issues to the appropriate officers or decision-making bodies of the University.

name: Student Athlete Advisory Committee
description: To enhance the total student-athlete experience at Cornell by promoting opportunity, protecting student-athlete well-being, and fostering a positive student-athlete image.

name: Student Athlete Support Services
description: The primary mission of the Student-Athlete Support Services (SASS) office is to support the efforts of every student-athlete in balancing their academic and athletic goals in conjunction with existing campus services. The services, available to all student-athletes, have been designed to support their academic and personal objectives. The programs and services are based on the philosophy that the development of the whole person is of primary interest. At Cornell, student-athletes are first and foremost students, who are highly committed to both their academic and athletic pursuits.

name: Student Business Office (SBO)
description: We offer services to help registered student organizations spend their funding support so no one has to pay out of pocket. We offer support with Funding, Budgeting, Payment Requests, and Purchasing needs.

name: Student Club Insurance
description: Student Club Insurance

name: Student Neurodiversity Alliance at Cornell
description: The mission of this organization is to promote acceptance and inclusion of neurodivergent members of the Cornell community, to spread a more nuanced understanding of neurodiversity across campus, and to advocate for policies that will improve the experiences of neurodivergent people at Cornell. This organization is associated with Neurodiversity @ Cornell and their Neurodiversity Ambassadors program.

name: Student Organ Donation Advocates Cornell Chapter
description: Student Organ Donation Advocates Cornell Chapter is a non-profit community service organization that seeks to lead life-saving organ and tissue donation registration and education efforts on Cornell University's campus and in the greater Ithaca community.

name: Student Programming Council
description: The Student Programming Council is an umbrella organization for our major programming organizations on campus. We elevate the student experience by creating memories for all students at Cornell.

name: Students Against the Sexual Solicitation of Youth
description: Students Against the Sexual Solicitation of Youth (SASSY) was founded in 2007 through a Cornell Alternative Breaks trip since 2003, is committed to raising awareness and transforming public perception of the Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children (CSEC). SASSY works directly with Girls Educational and Mentoring Services (GEMS), a non-profit agency in New York City, whose mission is to "empower girls and young women, ages 12–24, who have experienced commercial sexual exploitation and domestic trafficking to exit the commercial sex industry and develop to their full potential. Studio encourages photographers of all skill levels to participate in events and submit their work.

description: Residential Life furthers the academic mission of Cornell University and the principles outlined in the First Year Experience model. By providing a safe, diverse, purposeful living and learning environment aligned with these values, we support student involvement and active citizenship. name: Taiko at Cornell

Since its founding in 2006, the group has performed at many different venues on the Cornell campus or around Ithaca with the purpose of spreading this art form. Cornell undergraduates of all musical abilities are encouraged to join Yamatai as a testament to the ease with which one can learn taiko. Yamatai aims to inspire and entertain audiences of all walks of life, while exploring the nexus between the contemporary and the traditional.

As the only South Asian a cappella group at Cornell, Tarana has the unique honor of combining the musical traditions of the East and the West, singing songs by artists from Ariana Grande to Arijit Singh. name: Thread Magazine

As a completely student-run publication, Thread is a conglomeration of student-made photography, styling, design, and writing. It seeks to place the students in proximity with technology that will lead to an increase in hand-eye coordination, fine motor skills, and will provide a platform for them to innovate. Ultimately, its goal is to train future leaders that will move humankind forward.

The term "Ujamaa" is Kiswahili, roughly meaning collective economics. The name affirms our commitment as a community to pool resources and be participants in each other's fulfillment.
