name: Urban Herbin (Urban Ethnobotany Club)
description: Our mission is to be able to teach members about the land we are inhabiting and how indigenous practices that are often overlooked can be utilized by everyday people to lead healthier lives. We strive to teach our community how to create greener spaces in unconventional areas like their own apartments and rooftops. Ultimately, we want to also teach our community about how indigenous medicinal plants can be grown in mundane environments to benefit their lives.

name: Vaccination Conversations with Scientists - Cornell Student Chapter
description: Vaccination Conversations with Scientists - Cornell Student Chapter is an outreach initiative promoting vaccine uptake by connecting Cornell University students (scientists-in-training) with community members to have conversations about the science behind vaccines. We attend training, phone banking, and community event canvassing events organized by the local organization Vaccination Conversations with Scientists as well as propose our own vaccine education initiatives on campus to disseminate information about upcoming vaccine clinics, the latest research and recommended public health guideli

name: Varsity Botany Club Cornell
description: The mission of Varsity Botany Club shall be to inspire an appreciation for the value of botany in our world, to develop knowledge of diverse botanical topics, to promote the pursuit of excellence in botanical science, and to explore the interconnectedness of biological life on Earth

name: VASA DEI at Cornell
description: The purpose of VASA DEI shall be to unite all believers at Cornell as one body of Christ, through the gift of dance, to be vessels of His good news to bring praise and glory all to God.

name: Venture Capital at Cornell
description: The Cornell Venture Capital Club connects Cornell students and entrepreneurs with the dynamic world of venture capital. We provide Cornell undergraduates with the valuable and unique opportunity to work directly with leading venture capital firms; we host prominent entrepreneurs and venture capitalists as guest lecturers on Cornell's campus; we also provide resources for budding student entrepreneurs. Our flagship VC Internship Program provides high-potential Cornell undergraduates with the unparalleled opportunity to learn about the venture capital industry by working directly with leading VC

name: Ventures Accelerated
description: To bring together students to build stellar companies. To build a strong community filled with student entrepreneurs that will support, guide, and learn from one another. To help students passionate about start-ups succeed in bringing their ideas to reality. To connect student companies with prominent Venture Capital Firms, Accelerators, and mentors to further grow and scale their companies.

name: Vessels of Honor at Cornell
description: The mission of Vessels of Honor is to create a space for anyone within the Cornell and local Ithaca community to dive into the Bible as the complete, divine truth (John 17:17), build one another up in fellowship (Ephesians 4:16), and pursue Christ as the way, the reality, and the life (John 14:6). The club is open to anyone regardless of background, and no prior experience of Christ is required. Our meetings are centered around the ministry of believers who came before us, and through their work, laid a strong foundation for us to understand God's eternal purpose.

name: VET - American Association of Bovine Practitioners
description: The Cornell Student Chapter of the American Association of Bovine Practitioners is an academic organization of future veterinarians. Through our sponsored activities (guest lectures, farm visits, wet labs), we strive to fulfill the mission of the National AABP, an international association of veterinarians serving society as leaders in cattle health, welfare and productivity.

name: VET - American Association of Equine Practitioners Student Chapter
description: The purpose of SCAAEP is to enable veterinary students at Cornell to learn veterinary medicine as it pertains to equine medicine, both commercial and private, to provide veterinary students with educational opportunities in the equine aspects of veterinary medicine, to aid in the career development of students by informing them of the opportunities available in equine medicine, to enhance leadership characteristics and skills and to act as a liaison between equine veterinarians and students.

name: VET - American Association of Small Ruminant Practitioners - Student Chapter
description: For those who don't have much experience with large animals, AASRP is a great way to ease into the farm animal world! AASRP is a club devoted to teaching students of all interests about the care of goats, sheep, llamas, and alpacas. Activities include various lectures on sheep/goat management, hoof trimming, sheep shearing, wetlabs, venipuncture labs, and visits to local sheep, goat and llama farms. They welcome anyone interested in learning more and interacting more with small ruminants which are rapidly becoming more popular as dairy animals and as pets.

name: VET - American Society of Laboratory Animal Medicine, Student Chapter
description: The purpose of the Student Chapter of the American Society of Laboratory Animal Practitioners is to foster educational activities in the veterinary specialty of Laboratory Animal Medicine and to familiarize the members with standards, regulations, and techniques pertaining to this discipline.

name: Vet - American Veterinary Society of Animal Behavior, Student Chapter
description: The purpose of this organization shall be to: 1) To promote the importance of animal behavior in veterinary medicine. 2) To provide veterinary students with educational opportunities in relation to animal behavior, by encouraging guest speakers for Chapter Meetings. 3) To create and maintain an affiliation between Student Chapter members and members of the American Veterinary Society of Animal Behavior (AVSAB). 4) To enhance leadership characteristics in its members through organization as a Student Chapter. 5) To encourage camaraderie among veterinary students with an interest in animal behav

name: VET - Association for Non-traditional Students at Cornell College of Veterinary Medicine
description: Background and Mission: Despite their increasing presence in the collegiate environment, non-traditional students (NTS) are often overlooked and misunderstood, especially at the graduate level, with universities primarily catering to the needs of traditional students and lacking NTS support services. The definition of an NTS may vary, but a generally agreed upon definition for a non-traditional graduate student is someone who may be older (e.g., 25 years or older) than their fellow students and/or took a detour, rather than a direct route, from undergraduate to graduate school. This definition

name: VET - Association of Avian Veterinarians Cornell University
description: SCAAV works to enhance the educational opportunities of the veterinary students in the NYSCVM in regard to avian welfare and healthcare, specifically by informing students about veterinary problems and diseases, husbandry issues, preventative medicine, and scientific research currently encountered in dealing with both captive and wild birds.

name: VET - Association of Reptilian and Amphibian Veterinarians ZAWS
description: We aim to train veterinary students so that they can contribute to advancing reptilian and amphibian medicine, surgery, and conservation. We enhance the educational opportunities of the professional students in the veterinary college to learn about reptilian and amphibian medicine by hosting lectures and wet labs about veterinary problems and diseases, preventative medicine, husbandry issues, and scientific research currently encountered in dealing with both captive and wild exotic species.

name: VET - Association of Veterinary Scientists
description: To enhance collaboration and scientific growth between veterinary students, residents, and researchers interested or involved in veterinary science research.

name: VET - Cardiology Club
description: Cardiology Club organizes cardiology rounds, lectures, and wet labs for veterinary students and other interested members of the veterinary community to support further learning and exposure in the field of cardiology.

name: VET - CVM Peer Mentors
description: The purpose of CVM Peer Mentors shall be to foster an environment that supports the first-year veterinary student’s transition into veterinary school by hosting various events throughout the school year to engage first-year students and the broader CVM community and offer opportunities for camaraderie, enjoyment, and an outlet for academic and personal challenges. As upper-class vet students who advise first-year students, PMs additionally collaborate with faculty and staff to tailor resources to student needs.

name: VET - Dance Collective
description: The purpose of the CUCVM Dance Collective is to bring together the dance community within the Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine by celebrating our enthusiasm for art, music, and dance. As a non-audition based dance group open to students of any level and style of dance, we serve as a creative outlet for students who would like a fun and casual way to express movement and meet others with similar interests during our bi-monthly open classes. In addition to this, the CUCVM Dance Collective also offers performance opportunities to those students who would like the chance to choreo

name: VET - Dermatology Club
description: Dermatological issues are one of the most common reasons companion animals are brought to the vet office. They are hard to deal with, incredibly uncomfortable, and truly take a toll on our pets' quality of life. The goal of the Dermatology club is to help future veterinarians feel more comfortable diagnosing and treating skin cases. Through labs, lectures, and shadowing opportunities, students will feel more confident in their PE findings, formulating diagnostic steps, and gain more knowledge about the wonderful world of derm!

name: VET - First Generation Low Income Veterinary Student Association
description: The First Generation, Low Income Veterinary Student Association is dedicated to empowering veterinary students navigating unique challenges by cultivating an inclusive community that fosters academic excellence, leadership, and professional growth. Through mentorship, advocacy, and resource access, we strive to dismantle barriers and provide members with the tools, connections, and support needed to succeed in veterinary medicine. By championing equity, financial literacy, and collaboration, FiGLI advances systemic change to create a more diverse and just veterinary profession where all studen

name: VET - Jewish Association of Veterinary Students at Cornell
description: The purpose of Jewish Association of Veterinary Students shall be to provide a safe and inclusive association through which to practice and promote Jewish culture and customs through various events and gatherings, holiday celebrations, and community engagement. The organization also aims to engage with veterinary students interested in learning more about and engaging with Jewish culture and customs to further foster understanding and inclusivity on the veterinary college campus.

name: VET - Latinx Veterinary Medical Association at Cornell Student Chapter
description: To empower Latinx students and professionals in veterinary medicine and support aspiring Latinx veterinarians in order to better serve client demographics or "the next generation of Latinx veterinarians".

name: VET - Pet Loss Support Hotline
description: The first Pet Loss Support Hotline was set up in 1989 at the College of Veterinary Medicine at the University of California at Davis. Cornell used their guidelines in construction of our own hotline. The hotline is staffed by volunteer veterinary students who have undergone extensive training with professional grief counselors. Volunteers regularly attend discussion meetings with faculty advisors. These meetings assist hotline volunteers in dealing with the personal responses to grief and educate them to better serve the needs of callers. Literature relating to pet loss and grief is maintained

name: VET - Pride Student VMC Cornell (Broad Spectrum)
description: Student Pride VMC (formerly Broad Spectrum) strives to support, represent, and advance the interests of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and nonbinary, questioning, intersex, asexual, and otherwise gender/sexuality-marginalized (LGBTQIA+) students, faculty, and staff affiliated with Cornell College of Veterinary Medicine (CVM). We aim to foster inclusivity for LGBTQIA+ persons within the CVM community by organizing safe-space social gatherings, hosting speakers and educational events, advocating for LGBTQIA+ needs within the context of CVM, and collaborating with Pride VMC and other Student

name: VET - Psychopaths: American College of Veterinary Pathologists
description: As a student chapter of the American College of Veterinary Pathology, the Pathology club, aim: To encourage veterinary student involvement in the field of veterinary pathology and provide an additional opportunity for its associates to gain professional knowledge in this field. To make available to the students the opportunities offered by the American College of Veterinary Pathologists to its Student Chapters.

name: VET - Shelter Medicine Club
description: The Shelter Medicine Club's mission is to expose veterinary students to the myriad of issues surrounding animal sheltering and animal welfare issues. We collaborate with local shelters to host monthly clinics where students can gain hands-on experience through assisting with surgery prep and post-op care, administering vaccines, and performing physical exams. We host speakers on a wide range of subjects, such as careers in animal sheltering medicine, humane animal handling, rescuing animals during disasters, animal behavior, and pet overpopulation. We often work together with other clubs on an

name: VET - Sports Medicine Club
description: To provide education and information in various aspects of prevention, recognition, care and rehabilitation of injuries within equine and canine sports medicine and to promote the human-animal bond through activities that get people outside and working with their dogs. These activities may include agility, hiking, herding, tracking, Canine Good Citizen training and testing, and others as chosen by members. All breeds, mutts, sizes, ages, and fitness levels are welcome! Activities will be scheduled to provide students with a variety of dog-friendly options for relaxation and exercise. Lectures

name: VET - Student American Veterinary Medical Association at Cornell
description: The objectives of the Cornell University SAVMA shall be as follow: a. To foster a united school spirit and to provide support of issues for the benefit of students within the college; b. To provide opportunities for members to gain additional professional knowledge and an understanding of professional ethics; c. To provide the students the benefits offered by the American Veterinary Medical Association to its student chapters and the advantages of belonging to a professional organization; d. To support, facilitate, and encourage student, faculty, and administration involvement in activities of

name: VET - Student Chapter of the National Association for Black Veterinarians at Cornell
description: The mission of NABV is to "advocate, provide support, and cultivate an inclusive community for Blacks in veterinary medicine at every level of the profession through the organization, members and leadership." The purpose of the chapter is to provide support and community to Black students at CUCVM, to maintain strong relationships with Black alumni, and to offer opportunities for Black and minority pre-veterinary students to better understand the field.

name: VET - Student Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care Society
description: SVECCS is a student organization designed to promote the education and involvement of veterinary students in emergency and critical care medicine.

name: VET - Surgery Club
description: This club seeks to provide veterinary students with additional exposure to the world of veterinary surgery through lectures, wet labs, workshops, and other activities.

name: VET - Tabletop Vets
description: Tabletop Vets is a graduate/professional school organization founded to foster an environment in which all members of the Cornell Community may safely gather to play tabletop games. Members play a variety of games, including board-, card-, and pen & paper- games, in a setting which encourages social interaction and positive mental well-being.

name: VET - The Association of Asian Veterinary Medical Professionals at Cornell
description: 1. Provide professional and educational resources to AAPI veterinary professionals, veterinary students, and clients. 2. Encourage an interest in veterinary medicine among AAPI youth and support aspiring AAPI veterinary professionals through providing mentorship and other educational resources. 3. Facilitate networking opportunities among AAPI veterinary professionals. 4. Collaborate with similarly aligned diversity initiatives and affinity groups to advocate for greater general diversity in the veterinary profession.

name: VET - Theriogenology Club
description: The Student Chapter of the Society for Theriogenology is an organization for students who are interested in the study of reproduction in animals. In particular, it hopes to acquaint the student with the varying aspects of reproduction as it pertains to veterinary medicine - disease prevention, diagnosis, treatment, surgery, research, and related fields.

name: VET - Ultrasound A Cappella
description: Ultrasound brings together vet students to sing, perform and arrange both traditional and modern music in a mixed voices, non-auditioned group. We collaborate with the vet college's Dance Collective and musical theatre group, Vet Players, and perform yearly for the vet school and for the Cornell community.

name: VET - Veterinarians as One Inclusive Community for Empowerment
description: The purpose of Veterinarians as One Inclusive Community for Empowerment (VOICE) is: 1. To increase awareness, respect and sensitivity to differences among all individuals and communities in the field of veterinary medicine These include, but are not limited to, sex, race, color, age, national origin, religion, disability, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity/reassignment, gender expression, citizenship, pregnancy or parental status, veteran or military status, and educational background 2. To celebrate diversity within the profession of veterinary medicine a

name: VET - Veterinary Business Management Association
description: The Veterinary Business Management Association is a student-driven organization dedicated to advancing the profession through increasing business knowledge, creating networking opportunities, and empowering students to achieve their personal and professional goals.

name: VET - Veterinary Internal Medicine the Student Chapter
description: The purpose of the Chapter is to promote the specialties of cardiology, neurology, oncology, large animal internal medicine, and small animal internal medicine through the advancement of knowledge to veterinary medical students.

name: VET - Veterinary Medicine Open House
description: The Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine Open House organization is committed to the planning, organization, set up, and management of the annual Vet School Open House.

name: VET - Veterinary One Health Association
description: The objectives of the organization are as follows: 1) to provide veterinary students with educational opportunities in the one health aspects of veterinary medicine; 2) to aid in the career development of students by informing them of the opportunities available in the one and public health sector; 3) to enhance leadership characteristics and skills; 4) to increase awareness of disease and biosecurity as it pertains to food safety, environmental health animal health, and public health; and 5) to host an annual Veterinary One Health Symposium.

name: VET - Veterinary Players
description: The purpose of The Vet Players is to foster creativity among veterinary students and provide a creative outlet for exploration. The organization promotes communication, community, and creativity by putting on theatrical events and productions throughout the academic year.

name: VET - Veterinary Radiology Club at Cornell University
description: The purpose of the Cornell University Veterinary Radiology Club is to promote and encourage the study of radiology and other diagnostic imaging modalities by exploring all aspects of diagnostic imaging and radiotherapy through presentations, learning modules, and hands- on experience. Diagnostic imaging modalities include: small and large animal diagnostic radiology, diagnostic ultrasound, nuclear medicine, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging.

name: VET - Wildlife Disease Association Student Chapter
description: The objectives of the Student Chapters of the Wildlife Disease Association include the mission of the WDA, and more specifically aim to educating students interested in wildlife health and disease about the profession, career opportunities, job qualifications, externship opportunities. We also aim to enhance the skills of these students through lectures, workshops, conferences, and field trips. Finally, by connecting students interested in wildlife health and disease to mentors in WDA, networking is one of our main objectives.

name: VET - Women's Veterinary Leadership Development Initiative, Student Chapter
description: The purpose of this organization shall be to achieve leadership excellence in every sector of veterinary medicine that fully reflects the diversity of the profession and society. This organization shall support women in seeking and achieving leadership, policy, and decision-making positions within all areas of professional veterinary activity. This organization shall provide support and opportunities for students to learn leadership skills, and develop mentoring relationships

name: VET - World Aquatic Veterinary Medical Association
description: The Mission of the Chapter is to provide Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine students with information on aquatic veterinary educational, career and other opportunities, and to develop programs useful for the World Aquatic Veterinary Medical Association to help increase the knowledge, skills and involvement of veterinary students at CUCVM, and elsewhere, in aquatic veterinary medicine.

name: VET- Dawghouse FC
description: As students of the College of Veterinary Medicine (CVM), we know first hand that there is a lot of work and pressure constantly being pushed onto us. We want to create a space where we can relieve some of that stress through soccer! Soccer is a fantastic way to run off steam, have fun exercising, engage in healthy competition, and meet new people. Our intent for developing this club is not only to provide an outlet from school work, but to also help develop soccer skills, teamwork, and confidence in a fun and safe environment. The club is open to all who want to play soccer, both undergraduate

name: Veteran's Social Club
description: The Mission of the Veterans Social Club is to offer a stress-free environment for veterans and their supporters; to congregate and socialize without politics, religion, or other issues that cause emotional stress.

name: Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer
Vietnamese Student Association
description: The Cornell Vietnamese Association is an organization that promotes awareness, appreciation, and education of Vietnamese culture, heritage, and traditions within the organization as well as throughout the Cornell and Ithaca communities.

name: Viticulture and Enology Club, Cornell University
description: The purpose of CUVEC shall be to enrich the Cornell Viticulture and Enology experience through practice in and exploration of diverse topics within the wine industry and other allied industries in order to further develop the specialization of students.

name: Voices of Equity Cornell Chapter
description: The purpose of the Voices of Equity Cornell Chapter shall be to advocate for health equity of the Ithaca and greater-Ithaca area community through dismantling systemic barriers that inhibit an individual's access to quality healthcare. This will be done through educating members, inspiring individuals to prioritize our issue, and empowering individuals to act in order to alleviate health inequities.

name: Volunteers Around the World Veterinary Outreach
description: Veterinary Outreach provides interns with an opportunity to work first hand with experienced local veterinarians. Interns will fund raise for medications and supplies prior to the trip abroad. While in country, interns will assist the veterinarians with performing physical exams, giving vaccines, performing surgeries, deworming animals and assessing general health and well-being. All intern activities are under the direct supervision of a licensed veterinarian. This is an intensive internship, valuable to future veterinarians, veterinary technicians and other future healthcare providers as wel

name: VTPEH6142 Health, Wellbeing, and the Environment
Wait Terrace Cooperative
description: To facilitate learning and community in a residential context.

name: Wanawake Wa Wari Cooperative
description: Wanawake Wa Wari was originally founded in 1968 by a group of Black women who felt the need for an atmosphere that promoted self-awareness and personal confidence. Since that time Wari has served as a place where women of African descent have prepared for the world academically, culturally, and socially. It has also provided an atmosphere where women feel comfortable to deal with the issues that relate to their lives and history in the Ithaca community and beyond. We are striving to continue this tradition. Cornell is an equal opportunity employer. For more information, visit hr.cornell.edu/ee

name: Watermargin Cooperative
description: Watermargin was founded in 1947 by a group of World War II veterans who shared the purpose of promoting understanding between people of different races and religious affiliations. Over the years, the focus has expanded to encompass all intergroup relations. In the 1960's, Watermargin went co-ed, leading to a change in the motto from "All Men are Brothers" to "All People are Family." Watermargin's evolving mission is to encourage the expression of diverse views, to struggle against injustice, and to build communities. (http://www.watermargin.org/a/index.html)

name: WebDev
description: Cornell Webdev is an inclusive software club for self-driven web designers, developers, and enthusiasts!

name: Weill-Ithaca Network
description: Our mission is to provide a gateway for Cornell pre-medical undergraduates to gain exposure to the medical field by pairing students with a Weill Cornell medical student mentor and organizing events that include trips to the Weill Cornell campus in NYC. The broader vision of WIN is to bridge the geographical divide between the two campuses, thereby facilitating greater intercampus dialogue and collaboration at the student level. Distance should not become a significant obstacle for students' academic and professional growth. We hope to expand to include Physicians Assistants and PhD mentorship

name: Western Equestrian Club at Cornell
description: Our purpose is to further the equestrian skills of our members, specifically related to the Western riding discipline. We promote proper horse handling and riding techniques to make the experience valuable to both the horse and the rider, as well as compete regionally to further individual and team standing.

name: Whistling Shrimp Improv Comedy Troupe
description: To learn, practice, and perform the basic principles of improv comedy.

name: Wild Roses Ultimate Frisbee
description: The Cornell Wild Roses is a competitive women and gender queer college-level ultimate frisbee team registered with USA Ultimate. We practice 3 times a week and go to 4-5 tournaments per semester. Frisbee is a welcoming community where you're encouraged to be kind, work hard, and laugh harder. We are a tight knit group that genuinely loves spending time together and are committed to helping each other grow.

name: Willard Straight Hall Student Union Board (SUB)
description: The Student Union Board aims to celebrate Willard Straight Hall's historical responsibility and Cornell's student culture by hosting events that build social relationships within the Cornell community, welcoming all students back to at the start of the Fall and Spring semester through fun and unique activities, and supporting and recognizing the cultural and social diversity of the student community throughout the school year.

name: William Keeton House
description: Building community within the west campus housing system

name: Wind Ensembles at Cornell University
description: The purpose of CU Winds is to build, maintain and support a wind band and chamber winds community on the Cornell campus and in the surrounding Ithaca area. It gives Cornell students with musical experience the opportunity to rehearse and perform with a larger ensemble. Additionally, CU Winds promotes the appreciation of wind band music through concert performances, new music commissions, workshops, etc.

name: Winter Sessions - Residential Life Team
description: To provide communication between Residential Life Leadership and the student leaders (RA's).

name: Women in Chemistry
description: To create an environment where women feel comfortable discussing chemistry and can support their peers in their studies.

name: Women in Computing at Cornell
description: Women in Computing at Cornell strives to make computing inclusive for all. We aim to foster a supportive community of women* and allies equipped with the resources needed to recognize and overcome challenges. By creating opportunities for technical and leadership growth, we work to ensure that people of all identities are able to discover and pursue their interests and talents in order to positively impact the future of tech. *All gender identities are welcome and supported!

name: Women in Healthcare Leadership
description: Women in Healthcare Leadership is an independent, self-governing young professional organization at Cornell University which empowers women to pursue leadership roles and management positions within both private and public health care systems, hospital networks, and private firms by uniting professional development, personal growth, mentorship, and industry resources. The organization is also dedicated to the global elevation of women, in all industries, and serves to provide resources to those interested in professional development. We recognize the impact of uniting diverse thoughts and back

name: Women in Public Policy
description: Cornell Women in Public Policy (WIPP) graduate student organization was founded in 1994. Maintaining the historic mission of integrating women into public policy roles, WIPP's mission is also to facilitate the professional integration of people of all genders, races and ethnicities, abilities, sexual orientations, communities, and socioeconomic statuses into public policy roles. The organization promotes principles of equality, justice, and integrity in the public and private arenas while providing a support system and networking opportunities for its members. To this end, WIPP organizes discu

name: Women Leaders of Color
description: Our mission is to empower and provide resources to women of color who aspire to step into leadership positions in their community, workplace, and beyond. Through mentorship programs, inspirational speaking seminars, workshops, and events, WLC aims to enable opportunities and promote leadership and professional development among women of color in the Cornell community.

name: Women Leadership in Hospitality (WLiH)
description: Women Leadership in Hospitality is an organization dedicated to providing education, resources, mentorship, and leadership opportunities to women in order to empower them to be successful leaders in the world of hospitality and business.

name: Women of Aeronautics and Astronautics
description: The purpose of WOAA shall be to encourage the participation of marginalized genders in the fields of aeronautics and astronautics.

name: Women of Color Athletics
description: To provide women of color within Cornell Athletics a support network and space to share their experiences. We seek to stimulate the acceptance of cultural identities and celebrate the strength, brains and uniqueness that empowers women of color in their pursuit of being both a successful student and athlete at the highest level.

name: Women on Wall Street at Cornell Chapter
description: The mission of Women on Wall Street is to build an inclusive, transparent, and lifelong community for undergraduate women interested in finance, removing barriers to recruiting, sharing resources openly, and developing the technical and networking skills needed to thrive. This organization has the ability for members to connect with women at other universities as there are many other chapters of Women on Wall Street, including University of California, Berkeley and University of Florida.

name: Women's Club Basketball at Cornell University
description: The purpose of our organization is to provide women basketball players in the Cornell community to opportunity to play fun, yet competitive basketball.

name: Women's Club Lacrosse at Cornell
description: Advance skills and knowledge of lacrosse.

name: Women's Club Soccer at Cornell
description: The purpose of the Cornell Women's Club Soccer team is to provide the campus with the highest level of competitive soccer possible, outside of the Varsity program.

name: Women's Club Softball at Cornell
description: We provide an opportunity for competitive fast-pitch softball without the time commitment of varsity sports. Our mission is to create a welcoming and friendly, yet competitive environment for players who love being part of a team and want the flexibility to be involved in multiple on-campus activities.

name: Women's Club Volleyball at Cornell
description: We look to provide a way for girls to keep playing volleyball competitively. We practice twice a week and travel to tournaments on weekends.

name: Women's Club Water Polo at Cornell
description: We, the Cornell Women's Water Polo Club, believe that students with similar interests in playing and competing in water polo should come together to share their abilities to practice and play as a team in a competitive and fun setting. We believe that this serves to enhance the educational and athletic experience within the university environment. Therefore, we do hereby state as our purpose: to actively culture and represent the undergraduate and graduate population of Cornell University with a strong interest in playing competitive Water Polo.

name: Women's Freestyle Wrestling Club at Cornell
description: Our mission is to provide an opportunity for women at Cornell to practice and learn freestyle wrestling. The main style of wrestling taught in the U.S. is folkstyle, but this style is only competitive in U.S. high school boys' and college men's wrestling. Providing freestyle experience will afford greater opportunities for women seeking competition experience, as freestyle wrestling is for women at all levels of competition, from local open tournaments to the international level. We believe that freestyle wrestling can be a highly empowering and liberating activity for women.

name: Women's Higher Education Now
description: Women's Higher Education Now (WHEN) is a student organization that explores the intersectionality of issues related to gender equality, sustainable development, and equitable education on the global stage. WHEN is affiliated with and fundraises for the Asian University for Women, an international university located in Chittagong, Bangladesh that provides higher education to women from underserved communities in Asia.

name: Women's Ice Hockey Club at Cornell
description: To enjoy the sport of ice hockey, learn and improve skills, and create a successful team.

name: Women's Leadership Initiative at Cornell
description: The Cornell Women's Leadership Initiative is an undergraduate organization dedicated to empowering and supporting the next generation of women leaders at Cornell University. Our mission is to foster a culture that uplifts and inspires women in their leadership pursuits, both on campus and beyond.

name: Women's Opportunity Center
description: At the Women's Opportunity Center (W.O.C), we train our volunteers to believe in the women at the center, regardless of their path; to treat them respectfully, and to model professional relationships. Clients of W.O.C learn from our volunteers and then go out to impact the community. Speaker's Bureau, Philanthropic Donation Solicitation, Business Development intern, Fashion Retail Social Media & Influencer Intern, Community Analytics Intern and many more.

name: Women's Planning Forum
description: To celebrate women's contributions to the field of planning, provide a forum for discussion of gender issues in planning, and to promote gender equity in the classroom. Each year, we run a series of events on this theme, including dinners with guest speakers, monthly teas, and retreats, and general discussions. We also shed light on gender issues outside of planning, focusing on how women navigate space and build community together.

name: Women's Rugby at Cornell
description: The Cornell Women's Rugby Club exists to foster rugby competition and camaraderie on campus and across the country.

name: Women's Swim Club at Cornell
description: The Women's Cornell Club Swim Team is a Cornell club sports team where any prior competitive swimmers can continue to train for competition and attend meets with a team. The Women's team will practice weekly and work together in an inclusive environment, representing Cornell, improving as a swimmer and bonding as a team.

name: Women's Ultimate Frisbee, Cornell Thorny Roses
description: The Cornell Thorny Roses is a competitive college-level ultimate frisbee team registered with USA Ultimate. We travel to tournaments in the northeast area, and occasionally go south for tournaments. We practice 3-4 times a week and go to 4-5 tournaments per semester. Thorny is a tightly knit group of people who have fun together!

name: Wushu Club at Cornell
description: We are dedicated to promoting, practicing and performing Wushu, a sport comprising various styles of Chinese martial arts.

name: Young Democratic Socialists of America Cornell Chapter
description: Our mission is to educate and organize students to aid in a principled movement for social justice. Within and throughout this struggle, we articulate and defend the idea that true human liberation is impossible under capitalism. We seek social change which extends democracy into all aspects of life -- social, political and economic. This is the struggle for democratic socialism. Our vision of socialism is profoundly democratic, feminist, and anti-racist.

name: Youth Outreach Undergraduates Reshaping Success
description: Y.O.U.R.S. (Youth Outreach Undergraduates Reshaping Success) provides free after-school programming and mentorship for children and teens ages 7–17 living in rural Dryden, many of whom come from economically disadvantaged backgrounds. Cornell student volunteers partner with the O.U.R.S. program through Cornell Cooperative Extension of Tompkins County to foster confidence, leadership, healthy life skills, and positive adult–youth relationships. Programming is offered every weekday, with a different theme each day: Monday - Crafting, Tuesday - Cooking, Wednesday - LEGO/STEAM, and Thursday - Hiki

name: Zambia Community Education Initiative
description: The Zambia Community Education Initiative (ZCEI) is a student organization at Cornell University that aims to develop sustainable secondary education in Zambia by working with local communities to make education accessible to all. The ZCEI is currently working with the Chisekesi community in Southern Providence to fund the building of a secondary school. The inhabitants of rural Chisekesi have no high school, despite the presence of eight basic schools. The nearest high school is over 20km away and costs 600 dollars a year. name: Zoo, Exotics, & Wildlife Medicine at Cornell
description: The purpose of Zoo, Exotics, & Wildlife Medicine at Cornell shall be to bring together students interested in veterinary care for zoo, exotic, and wildlife species. We aim to build a supportive community, share knowledge, create hands-on learning opportunities, and make experiences in these fields more accessible to pre-veterinary students.
